        f"| Brier (null {metrics['brier_null']:.4f}) | {c['brier']:.4f} | {g['brier']:.4f} |",
        f"| Mean predicted | {c['mean_predicted']:.4f} | {g['mean_predicted']:.4f} |",
    ]
    for k in c["top_k"]:
        lines.append(f"| Top {k} PPV / sensitivity | {c['top_k'][k]['ppv']:.3f} / "
                     f"{c['top_k'][k]['sensitivity']:.3f} | {g['top_k'][k]['ppv']:.3f} / "
                     f"{g['top_k'][k]['sensitivity']:.3f} |")
    lines += [f"| Survey-weighted AUROC | | {g['auroc_survey_weighted']:.3f} |", "",
              "## Calibration by decile (gradient boosting)", "",
              "| Decile | n | Predicted | Actual |", "|---|---|---|---|"]
    lines += [f"| {d['decile']} | {d['n']:,} | {d['predicted']:.3f} | {d['actual']:.3f} |"
              for d in metrics["calibration_deciles"]]
    lines += ["", "## Subgroups (gradient boosting)", "",
              "| Group | n | Events | Rate | AUROC | Mean predicted |", "|---|---|---|---|---|---|"]
    lines += [f"| {r['group']} | {r['n']:,} | {r['events']:,} | {r['rate']:.3f} | {r['auroc']:.3f} | "
              f"{r['mean_predicted']:.3f} |" for r in metrics["subgroups"]]
    lines += ["", "## Permutation importance (AUROC drop, test panels)", "",
              "| Feature | Mean drop |", "|---|---|"]
    lines += [f"| `{f}` | {v:.4f} |" for f, v in list(metrics["permutation_importance"].items())[:10]]
    cc = metrics["comparison_coefficients"]
    lines += ["", "## Comparison model", "",
              f"Logistic regression: intercept {cc['intercept']:.3f}, age {cc['age_per_year']:.4f} "
              f"per year, any prior stay {cc['prior_stay']:.4f}.", "", f"_{metrics['note']}_", ""]
    return "\n".join(lines)


def write_reports(metrics: dict, out: Path, model_id: str | None = None) -> tuple[Path, Path]:
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    json_path, md_path = out / "metrics.json", out / "model_report.md"
    json_path.write_text(json.dumps(metrics, indent=2) + "\n")
    md_path.write_text(render_report(metrics, model_id))
    return json_path, md_path


def summary_line(name: str, m: dict) -> str:
    return (f"{name}: AUROC {m['auroc']:.3f} {_fmt_ci(m['auroc_ci95'])} AUPRC {m['auprc']:.3f} "
            f"{_fmt_ci(m['auprc_ci95'])} Brier {m['brier']:.4f} meanpred {m['mean_predicted']:.4f}")


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    parser.add_argument("--table", type=Path, default=None,
                        help="modelling table CSV (default: <data>/processed/meps_hosp12.csv)")
    parser.add_argument("--out", type=Path, default=None, help="report directory (default: <data>/reports)")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    table = pd.read_csv(args.table or processed_dir() / "meps_hosp12.csv")
    metrics = evaluate(table)
    paths = write_reports(metrics, args.out or reports_dir())
    s = metrics["split"]
    print(f"n_train {s['n_train']} n_test {s['n_test']} events_test {s['events_test']} rate {s['rate_test']:.4f}")
    print(summary_line("comparison", metrics["comparison"]))
    print(summary_line("gbm", metrics["gbm"]))
    print(f"weighted AUROC {metrics['gbm']['auroc_survey_weighted']:.3f} Brier null {metrics['brier_null']:.4f}")
    print("wrote", *paths)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

            "mean_predicted": float(p[mask].mean())}


def evaluate(table: pd.DataFrame) -> dict:
    train, test = split_masks(table)
    y = table[LABEL].to_numpy()
    X = feature_matrix(table)
    fitted = fit_validation(table)

    yt = y[test]
    p = fitted.gbm.predict_proba(X[test])[:, 1]
    pb = fitted.comparison.predict_proba(comparison_matrix(table)[test])[:, 1]
    weights = table["longwt"].to_numpy()[test]

    rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
    metrics = {
        "split": {"train_panels": list(TRAIN_PANELS), "test_panels": list(TEST_PANELS),
                  "n_train": int(train.sum()), "n_test": int(test.sum()),
                  "events_test": int(yt.sum()), "rate_test": float(yt.mean())},
        # Order matters: the shared rng is consumed comparison-first, as in the prototype.
        "comparison": _model_metrics(rng, yt, pb),
        "gbm": _model_metrics(rng, yt, p),
    }
    metrics["gbm"]["auroc_survey_weighted"] = float(roc_auc_score(yt, p, sample_weight=weights))
    metrics["brier_null"] = float(brier_score_loss(yt, np.full_like(p, y[train].mean())))

    deciles = pd.DataFrame({"y": yt, "p": p})
    deciles["decile"] = pd.qcut(deciles.p, 10, labels=False) + 1
    metrics["calibration_deciles"] = [
        {"decile": int(d), "n": int(len(g)), "predicted": float(g.p.mean()), "actual": float(g.y.mean())}
        for d, g in deciles.groupby("decile")]

    age = table["agey1x"].to_numpy()[test]
    sex = table["sex"].to_numpy()[test]
    prior = table["ipdisy1"].to_numpy()[test] > 0
    metrics["subgroups"] = [
        _subgroup("age 18-44", age < 45, yt, p),
        _subgroup("age 45-64", (age >= 45) & (age < 65), yt, p),
        _subgroup("age 65+", age >= 65, yt, p),
        _subgroup("male", sex == 1, yt, p),
        _subgroup("female", sex == 2, yt, p),
        _subgroup("no prior stay", ~prior, yt, p),
        _subgroup("prior stay", prior, yt, p),
    ]

    importance = permutation_importance(fitted.gbm, X[test], yt, scoring="roc_auc",
                                        n_repeats=5, random_state=0)
    metrics["permutation_importance"] = dict(sorted(
        zip(FEATURES, map(float, importance.importances_mean)), key=lambda kv: -kv[1]))

    coef = fitted.comparison.coef_[0]
    metrics["comparison_coefficients"] = {
        "intercept": float(fitted.comparison.intercept_[0]),
        "age_per_year": float(coef[0]), "prior_stay": float(coef[1])}
    metrics["note"] = SYNTHEA_NOTE
    return metrics


def _fmt_ci(ci) -> str:
    return f"[{ci[0]:.3f}, {ci[1]:.3f}]"

    s, c, g = metrics["split"], metrics["comparison"], metrics["gbm"]
    lines = [
        "# 12-month hospitalization model — evaluation report", "",
        f"Model: `{model_id}`" if model_id else "Model: validation models (not persisted)", "",
        f"Validation models trained on panels {s['train_panels'][0]}–{s['train_panels'][-1]} "
        f"(n = {s['n_train']:,}), tested on panels {s['test_panels'][0]}–{s['test_panels'][-1]} "
        f"(n = {s['n_test']:,}, {s['events_test']:,} hospitalized, rate {s['rate_test']:.4f}). "
        "The released model is refit on all panels; its own held-out performance is unknown "
        "by construction.", "",
        "| Measure | Comparison model | Gradient boosting |", "|---|---|---|",
        f"| AUROC [95% CI] | {c['auroc']:.3f} {_fmt_ci(c['auroc_ci95'])} | {g['auroc']:.3f} {_fmt_ci(g['auroc_ci95'])} |",
        f"| AUPRC [95% CI] | {c['auprc']:.3f} {_fmt_ci(c['auprc_ci95'])} | {g['auprc']:.3f} {_fmt_ci(g['auprc_ci95'])} |",
        f"| Brier (null {metrics['brier_null']:.4f}) | {c['brier']:.4f} | {g['brier']:.4f} |",
        f"| Mean predicted | {c['mean_predicted']:.4f} | {g['mean_predicted']:.4f} |",
    ]
    for k in c["top_k"]:
        lines.append(f"| Top {k} PPV / sensitivity | {c['top_k'][k]['ppv']:.3f} / "
                     f"{c['top_k'][k]['sensitivity']:.3f} | {g['top_k'][k]['ppv']:.3f} / "
                     f"{g['top_k'][k]['sensitivity']:.3f} |")
    lines += [f"| Survey-weighted AUROC | | {g['auroc_survey_weighted']:.3f} |", "",
              "## Calibration by decile (gradient boosting)", "",
              "| Decile | n | Predicted | Actual |", "|---|---|---|---|"]
    lines += [f"| {d['decile']} | {d['n']:,} | {d['predicted']:.3f} | {d['actual']:.3f} |"
              for d in metrics["calibration_deciles"]]
    lines += ["", "## Subgroups (gradient boosting)", "",
              "| Group | n | Events | Rate | AUROC | Mean predicted |", "|---|---|---|---|---|---|"]
    lines += [f"| {r['group']} | {r['n']:,} | {r['events']:,} | {r['rate']:.3f} | {r['auroc']:.3f} | "
              f"{r['mean_predicted']:.3f} |" for r in metrics["subgroups"]]
    lines += ["", "## Permutation importance (AUROC drop, test panels)", "",
              "| Feature | Mean drop |", "|---|---|"]
    lines += [f"| `{f}` | {v:.4f} |" for f, v in list(metrics["permutation_importance"].items())[:10]]
    cc = metrics["comparison_coefficients"]
    lines += ["", "## Comparison model", "",
              f"Logistic regression: intercept {cc['intercept']:.3f}, age {cc['age_per_year']:.4f} "
              f"per year, any prior stay {cc['prior_stay']:.4f}.", "", f"_{metrics['note']}_", ""]
    return "\n".join(lines)


def write_reports(metrics: dict, out: Path, model_id: str | None = None) -> tuple[Path, Path]:
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    json_path, md_path = out / "metrics.json", out / "model_report.md"
    json_path.write_text(json.dumps(metrics, indent=2) + "\n")
    md_path.write_text(render_report(metrics, model_id))
    return json_path, md_path


def summary_line(name: str, m: dict) -> str:
    return (f"{name}: AUROC {m['auroc']:.3f} {_fmt_ci(m['auroc_ci95'])} AUPRC {m['auprc']:.3f} "
            f"{_fmt_ci(m['auprc_ci95'])} Brier {m['brier']:.4f} meanpred {m['mean_predicted']:.4f}")


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    parser.add_argument("--table", type=Path, default=None,
                        help="modelling table CSV (default: <data>/processed/meps_hosp12.csv)")
    parser.add_argument("--out", type=Path, default=None, help="report directory (default: <data>/reports)")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    table = pd.read_csv(args.table or processed_dir() / "meps_hosp12.csv")
    metrics = evaluate(table)
    paths = write_reports(metrics, args.out or reports_dir())
    s = metrics["split"]
    print(f"n_train {s['n_train']} n_test {s['n_test']} events_test {s['events_test']} rate {s['rate_test']:.4f}")
    print(summary_line("comparison", metrics["comparison"]))
    print(summary_line("gbm", metrics["gbm"]))
    print(f"weighted AUROC {metrics['gbm']['auroc_survey_weighted']:.3f} Brier null {metrics['brier_null']:.4f}")
    print("wrote", *paths)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

def synthetic_table(per_panel: int = 300, seed: int = 0) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """A modelling table shaped exactly like meps.build's output (same columns, same order),
    with a real age / prior-stay signal so models have something to learn. Panels 21–27."""
    import numpy as np

    from outcome_prediction.model import FEATURES, LABEL

    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    n = per_panel * 7
    t = pd.DataFrame({"dupersid": np.arange(n), "panel": np.repeat(np.arange(21, 28), per_panel)})
    t["sex"] = rng.integers(1, 3, n)
    t["racethx"] = rng.integers(1, 6, n)
    t["regiony1"] = rng.choice([-1, 1, 2, 3, 4], n)          # -1: a MEPS missing code
    t["agey1x"] = rng.integers(18, 86, n)
    t["inscovy1"] = rng.integers(1, 4, n)
    t["povcaty1"] = rng.integers(1, 6, n)
    t["ipdisy1"] = rng.binomial(1, 0.12, n) * rng.integers(1, 3, n)
    t["ipngtdy1"] = t["ipdisy1"] * rng.integers(1, 6, n)
    for col, lam in (("ertoty1", 0.4), ("obtotvy1", 4), ("optotvy1", 0.5),
                     ("hhtotdy1", 0.1), ("rxtoty1", 12)):
        t[col] = rng.poisson(lam, n)
    t["totexpy1"] = rng.integers(0, 20000, n)
    for col in FEATURES[14:]:
        t[col] = rng.binomial(1, 0.15, n)
    t["longwt"] = rng.uniform(500, 5000, n)
    t["varstr"] = rng.integers(1, 100, n)
    t["varpsu"] = rng.integers(1, 3, n)
    logit = -4.0 + 0.035 * t["agey1x"] + 1.4 * (t["ipdisy1"] > 0)
    t[LABEL] = rng.binomial(1, 1 / (1 + np.exp(-logit)))
    order = ["dupersid", "panel", *FEATURES[:14], "longwt", "varstr", "varpsu", *FEATURES[14:], LABEL]
    return t[order]

"""Unit tests for the feature matrix, fitting, evaluation and the train pipeline — on a
synthetic table, so no MEPS data is needed."""
from __future__ import annotations

import json

import numpy as np
import pytest

from outcome_prediction.meps.build import build
from outcome_prediction.model import (
    CATEGORICAL, FEATURES, ContractMismatch, comparison_matrix, feature_matrix, split_masks,
)
from outcome_prediction.model.artifact import load_artifact
from outcome_prediction.model.evaluate import evaluate, render_report, top_k
from outcome_prediction.model.train import METRICS_PROVENANCE, train
from outcome_prediction.tests.conftest import person, synthetic_table


@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
def table():
    return synthetic_table()


@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
def metrics(table):
    return evaluate(table)


def test_feature_matrix_is_the_contract_in_order(table):
    X = feature_matrix(table)
    assert list(X.columns) == FEATURES and len(FEATURES) == 25


def test_categoricals_clip_negative_missing_codes_to_zero(table):
    X = feature_matrix(table)
    assert (table["regiony1"] == -1).any()
    assert X["regiony1"].min() == 0
    assert all(X[c].dtype.kind == "i" for c in CATEGORICAL)


def test_contract_mismatch_is_refused(table):
    with pytest.raises(ContractMismatch):
        feature_matrix(table.drop(columns=["choldx"]))
    reordered = table[[c for c in table.columns if c != "sex"] + ["sex"]]
    with pytest.raises(ContractMismatch):
        feature_matrix(reordered)


def test_build_output_satisfies_the_contract(write_panel):
    """The table M1's build writes is exactly what the model consumes."""
    df, _ = build({21: write_panel("h1.dta", [person("A", 21), person("B", 21)])})
    assert list(feature_matrix(df).columns) == FEATURES


def test_comparison_matrix_is_age_and_any_prior_stay(table):
    B = comparison_matrix(table)
    assert B.shape == (len(table), 2)
    assert np.array_equal(B[:, 1], (table["ipdisy1"] > 0).to_numpy())


def test_split_is_temporal(table):
    train, test = split_masks(table)
    assert set(table.panel[train]) == {21, 22, 23, 24, 25}
    assert set(table.panel[test]) == {26, 27}
    assert not (train & test).any()


def test_top_k_ppv_and_sensitivity():
    y = np.array([1, 0, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1])
    p = np.linspace(1, 0, 10)        # descending: first items are highest risk
    assert top_k(y, p, 0.2) == (0.5, 1 / 3)
    assert top_k(y, p, 0.3) == (2 / 3, 2 / 3)


def test_evaluation_covers_fr_e1_to_e5(metrics):
    s = metrics["split"]
    assert (s["n_train"], s["n_test"]) == (1500, 600)
    for name in ("comparison", "gbm"):
        m = metrics[name]
        assert m["auroc_ci95"][0] <= m["auroc"] <= m["auroc_ci95"][1]
        assert m["auprc_ci95"][0] <= m["auprc"] <= m["auprc_ci95"][1]
        assert set(m["top_k"]) == {"5%", "10%", "20%"}
    assert "auroc_survey_weighted" in metrics["gbm"]
    assert [d["decile"] for d in metrics["calibration_deciles"]] == list(range(1, 11))
    assert [g["group"] for g in metrics["subgroups"]] == [
        "age 18-44", "age 45-64", "age 65+", "male", "female", "no prior stay", "prior stay"]
    assert list(metrics["permutation_importance"]) and set(metrics["permutation_importance"]) == set(FEATURES)


def test_evaluation_is_deterministic(table, metrics):
    again = evaluate(table)
    assert again["gbm"]["auroc_ci95"] == metrics["gbm"]["auroc_ci95"]
    assert again["permutation_importance"] == metrics["permutation_importance"]


def test_models_learn_the_planted_signal(metrics):
    assert metrics["comparison"]["auroc"] > 0.6
    assert metrics["comparison_coefficients"]["age_per_year"] > 0
    assert metrics["comparison_coefficients"]["prior_stay"] > 0


def test_report_renders_every_section(metrics):
    report = render_report(metrics, "gbm-test")
    for heading in ("Calibration by decile", "Subgroups", "Permutation importance", "Comparison model"):
        assert heading in report
    assert "`gbm-test`" in report


def test_train_writes_a_loadable_artifact_and_reports(tmp_path, table):
    csv = tmp_path / "table.csv"
    table.to_csv(csv, index=False)

    directory, metrics = train(csv, tmp_path / "models", tmp_path / "reports")

    artifact = load_artifact(directory)
    meta = artifact.metadata
    assert meta["model_id"] == directory.name and meta["contract_version"] == "meps25-v1"
    assert meta["features"] == FEATURES
    assert meta["training"]["rows"] == len(table) and meta["training"]["panels"] == list(range(21, 28))
    assert meta["validation_metrics"]["provenance"] == METRICS_PROVENANCE
    assert meta["validation_metrics"]["gbm"]["auroc"] == metrics["gbm"]["auroc"]
    assert len(meta["training_score_quantiles"]) == 101
    assert meta["versions"]["scikit-learn"] == "1.9.1"
    # Both models are persisted and usable (O18).
    X = feature_matrix(table)
    assert artifact.model.predict_proba(X)[:, 1].shape == (len(table),)
    assert artifact.comparison.predict_proba(comparison_matrix(table))[:, 1].shape == (len(table),)
    reports = json.loads((tmp_path / "reports" / "metrics.json").read_text())
    assert reports["gbm"]["auroc"] == metrics["gbm"]["auroc"]
    assert (tmp_path / "reports" / "model_report.md").exists()


def test_train_never_overwrites_an_artifact(tmp_path, table):

    return evaluate(pd.read_csv(csv))

    s = metrics["split"]
    assert (s["n_train"], s["n_test"], s["events_test"]) == (44_497, 11_863, 1_042)

    assert 0.760 <= metrics["gbm"]["auroc"] <= 0.778
    assert 0.700 <= metrics["comparison"]["auroc"] <= 0.716

    g, c = metrics["gbm"], metrics["comparison"]
    assert round(g["auroc"], 3) == 0.769 and [round(v, 3) for v in g["auroc_ci95"]] == [0.754, 0.786]

def synthetic_table(per_panel: int = 300, seed: int = 0) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """A modelling table shaped exactly like meps.build's output (same columns, same order),
    with a real age / prior-stay signal so models have something to learn. Panels 21–27."""
    import numpy as np

    from outcome_prediction.model import FEATURES, LABEL

    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    n = per_panel * 7
    t = pd.DataFrame({"dupersid": np.arange(n), "panel": np.repeat(np.arange(21, 28), per_panel)})
    t["sex"] = rng.integers(1, 3, n)
    t["racethx"] = rng.integers(1, 6, n)
    t["regiony1"] = rng.choice([-1, 1, 2, 3, 4], n)          # -1: a MEPS missing code
    t["agey1x"] = rng.integers(18, 86, n)
    t["inscovy1"] = rng.integers(1, 4, n)
    t["povcaty1"] = rng.integers(1, 6, n)
    t["ipdisy1"] = rng.binomial(1, 0.12, n) * rng.integers(1, 3, n)
    t["ipngtdy1"] = t["ipdisy1"] * rng.integers(1, 6, n)
    for col, lam in (("ertoty1", 0.4), ("obtotvy1", 4), ("optotvy1", 0.5),
                     ("hhtotdy1", 0.1), ("rxtoty1", 12)):
        t[col] = rng.poisson(lam, n)
    t["totexpy1"] = rng.integers(0, 20000, n)
    for col in FEATURES[14:]:
        t[col] = rng.binomial(1, 0.15, n)
    t["longwt"] = rng.uniform(500, 5000, n)
    t["varstr"] = rng.integers(1, 100, n)
    t["varpsu"] = rng.integers(1, 3, n)
    logit = -4.0 + 0.035 * t["agey1x"] + 1.4 * (t["ipdisy1"] > 0)
    t[LABEL] = rng.binomial(1, 1 / (1 + np.exp(-logit)))
    order = ["dupersid", "panel", *FEATURES[:14], "longwt", "varstr", "varpsu", *FEATURES[14:], LABEL]
    return t[order]

(docs/phase8/prd.md §9 criterion 2; prototype-baseline.md §5.2).

prototype's version, M2 reproduced every printed digit — the tighter checks below record that,

@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
def metrics(meps_cache, tmp_path_factory):
    import pandas as pd
    table, _ = build({p: meps_cache / f"h{n}.dta" for p, n in LONGITUDINAL_PANELS.items()})
    # Round-trip through CSV, exactly as the pipeline does (build writes it, train reads it).

def test_split(metrics):

def test_acceptance_tolerances(metrics):
    assert 0.760 <= metrics["gbm"]["auroc"] <= 0.778
    assert 0.700 <= metrics["comparison"]["auroc"] <= 0.716


def test_matches_the_prototype_to_reported_precision(metrics):
    g, c = metrics["gbm"], metrics["comparison"]
    assert round(g["auroc"], 3) == 0.769 and [round(v, 3) for v in g["auroc_ci95"]] == [0.754, 0.786]
    assert round(g["auprc"], 3) == 0.265 and round(g["brier"], 4) == 0.0725
    assert round(c["auroc"], 3) == 0.708 and [round(v, 3) for v in c["auroc_ci95"]] == [0.691, 0.725]
    assert round(c["auprc"], 3) == 0.225 and round(c["brier"], 4) == 0.0751
    assert round(g["auroc_survey_weighted"], 3) == 0.780
    assert round(g["top_k"]["10%"]["ppv"], 3) == 0.293 and round(g["top_k"]["10%"]["sensitivity"], 3) == 0.333
    assert round(metrics["brier_null"], 4) == 0.0801

input.command:
gh pr create --base main --head feature/phase8-m2-training --title "feat(phase8): M2 — training, evaluation, verified model artifact" --body-file - <<'EOF'
## Summary

Phase 8 **M2**: train, evaluate and save the 12-month hospitalization model. It reproduces the research prototype on real MEPS data **exactly, to every reported digit**, which is tighter than the PRD's tolerance band.

```bash
python -m outcome_prediction.model.train      # evaluate + refit + artifact + reports (~18 s)
python -m outcome_prediction.model.evaluate   # reports only
```

## Verified against the prototype (`prototype-baseline.md` §5.2)

Test panels 26–27: 11,863 adults, 1,042 hospitalized. Training panels 21–25: 44,497 adults.

| Measure | Comparison model | Gradient boosting |
|---|---|---|
| AUROC [95% CI] | 0.708 [0.691, 0.725] | 0.769 [0.754, 0.786] |
| AUPRC [95% CI] | 0.225 [0.206, 0.250] | 0.265 [0.242, 0.290] |
| Brier (null 0.0801) | 0.0751 | 0.0725 |
| Top 10% PPV / sensitivity | 0.266 / 0.303 | 0.293 / 0.333 |
| Survey-weighted AUROC | | 0.780 |

Everything else also matches the prototype exactly:
- the other top-k values;
- all 10 calibration deciles;
- all 7 subgroup AUROCs;
- the permutation-importance ranking;
- the comparison model's coefficients (-4.047, 0.0280, 1.3055).

The confidence intervals match because the bootstrap draws random numbers in the same order the prototype did.

## Design notes

- **One definition** of the feature order, the train/test split and the hyperparameters, in `model/__init__.py`. A table whose features don't match the `meps25-v1` contract is refused.
- **Model files** (O17, O18):
  - Both models are saved.
  - `MANIFEST.sha256` is checked **before** any `joblib` loading, because unpickling can execute code. Missing, changed or unlisted files are refused, and so are manifest entries pointing outside the folder.
  - The training-score distribution is stored so the service can compute percentiles.
- **Model ID is derived from the training table's checksum**, e.g. `gbm-meps25-v1-950d8be12078`, so the same table always gives the same ID. An existing model folder is never overwritten, and that check runs before training starts.
- **Honest metadata:** the saved models are refit on all panels, so their own held-out performance is unknown. The metadata labels the stored metrics as coming from the validation models (design §11, defect 5).
- **`scikit-learn` pinned to exactly 1.9.1**, the prototype's version. Wheels are confirmed for Python 3.11 (CI) and 3.12 (devcontainer).
- Model files (`models/`) and reports (`data/reports/`) are gitignored; nothing generated is committed.

## Tests

- With the MEPS cache: **63 passed**.
- Without it, which is the CI configuration: **48 passed, 15 self-skipped**.
- **Unit tests** use a synthetic table with a deliberate age and prior-stay signal, so the models have something to learn. They cover:
  - the contract's column order and how it handles mismatches;
  - categorical clipping;
  - the temporal split;
  - top-k calculations;
  - evaluation completeness and determinism;
  - an end-to-end `train` run;
  - every way the artifact can be tampered with;
  - percentile edge cases.
- **`test_model_reproduction.py`** checks the PRD tolerance band and the exact match.

## Docs

`milestone-plan.md` M2 now records the verified results. Status is updated to "M1–M2 built, M3 next" in the phase README and `docs/README.md`. `design.md` §1 and §8 and the service README describe the new modules and the model-file layout.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF

M2 is built and passes locally, and it's in **PR #68**: https://github.com/bhaskarcmu/fhir-agent/pull/68. The trained model reproduces the prototype's results exactly, down to the last reported digit, not just within the PRD's allowed tolerance.

| Test panels 26–27 | Comparison model | Main model |
|---|---|---|
| AUROC [95% CI] | 0.708 [0.691, 0.725] | 0.769 [0.754, 0.786] |
| AUPRC [95% CI] | 0.225 [0.206, 0.250] | 0.265 [0.242, 0.290] |
| Survey-weighted AUROC | | 0.780 |

The rest matches too: top-k, all 10 calibration deciles, all 7 subgroups, the feature-importance ranking, and the comparison model's coefficients. Even the confidence intervals match, because the random resampling runs in the same order as in the prototype.

**What was built** (in `outcome-prediction-service/src/outcome_prediction/model/`):
- **One command does training and evaluation.** `python -m outcome_prediction.model.train` writes the evaluation reports and the saved model together, in about 18 seconds. `python -m outcome_prediction.model.evaluate` writes just the reports.
- **Saved model folder.** It holds both models, their metadata and a checksum list. The checksums are checked *before* any model file is loaded, because loading a saved model can run code. A one-byte change to any file, a missing file or an unlisted file is refused; I confirmed this on the real model folder.
- **Repeatable model ID.** The ID comes from the training table's checksum, so the same data always gives the same ID: `gbm-meps25-v1-950d8be12078`. An existing model folder is never overwritten.
- **Honest metrics labels.** The metrics stored with the model are labelled as coming from the validation models trained on panels 21–25. The saved model is retrained on all panels, so its own held-out performance can't be measured.
- **scikit-learn pinned to exactly 1.9.1, the prototype's version.** My first check reported no Python 3.11 wheel for it. That turned out to be a mistake in my query (it used an outdated platform tag); 1.9.1 installs on both 3.11 (CI) and 3.12.

**Validation:**
- With the MEPS data downloaded: 63 tests pass.
- Without it, which is how CI runs: 48 pass and 15 skip.
- No repeated test filenames, and no data or model files committed.

**Branch:** `feature/phase8-m2-training`. **Commit:** `2b75be20`. Docs are updated: the milestone plan records the verified numbers, and the status reads "M1–M2 built, M3 next".

**Known limitations:**
- CI just started. A background watch on the `phase8 (python)` job is running, and I'll report its result when it finishes.
- The model files and reports aren't committed (by design), so anyone else rebuilds them with the two commands above.
- In CI the reproduction tests skip, so only the synthetic-data tests run there. The exact-match check runs only where the MEPS data has been downloaded.

M3 (the `outcome-prediction-lab` experimentation workbench) is next. After PR #68 merges, I'll ask about deleting its branch.

content.text:
## Industry practice

The usual model is that **code lives in git, data lives in versioned object storage, and git holds only small pointers to the data**. "We can always download it again" is not treated as a backup plan.

**1. Keep your own copy of the raw data.**
- Raw inputs are copied once, exactly as received, into versioned object storage you control: S3, GCS or Azure Blob.
- Object versioning is turned on, and often a retention lock as well, so nothing can be silently overwritten or deleted.
- Data platforms call this the "raw" or "bronze" zone, and treat it as permanent.

**2. Put the data's fingerprint in git.**
- Git holds a small manifest of each file: its checksum, size, source URL and date retrieved. It works the way a package lock file does for software dependencies.
- Common tools for this:
  - **DVC:** pointer files in git, data in a storage bucket.
  - **lakeFS:** git-style branches for data stored in object storage.
  - **Delta Lake / Iceberg:** "time travel" back to earlier versions of a table.
  - **Git LFS:** works for medium-sized files, but has quotas and gets awkward at this scale.
- The data itself never goes in git: GitHub rejects files over 100 MB, and the repo would bloat permanently.

**3. Keep the documentation with the data.** The codebook and documentation pages matter as much as the files. Without them, nobody can tell what a variable like `IPDISY2` means later.

**4. Follow the 3-2-1 rule.** Three copies, on two kinds of storage, one of them off-site. For a few dozen MB, two cloud locations is plenty.

**5. Public archives are for publishing, not backup.** Zenodo, Dataverse and Figshare give a dataset a permanent DOI, but they're public, so they're only an option if the licence allows redistribution. For MEPS that's unclear: the same use-terms question as O23. A private bucket avoids the issue.

## How this repo compares

1. **Nothing in git records which data bytes were used.**
   - `checksums.json` sits inside the gitignored `data/` folder, so it never gets committed.
   - The model's metadata does record the raw file checksums, but model files aren't committed either.
   - So if AHRQ quietly re-released a corrected file, which statistical agencies do, a future run would download different bytes and nothing in the repo would show the change. The fix is cheap: commit a small manifest of expected checksums, and have the download step refuse anything that doesn't match.

2. **There is no copy outside this workspace.**
   - If `meps.ahrq.gov` changes its URLs or removes these files, the exact reproduction can't be repeated anywhere except this workspace.
   - The prototype's earlier session already hit one URL quirk: the folder-less download address returns 404.

## What I'd recommend here

The scale is tiny: the original zips total about 38 MB, so storage costs pennies.

1. **Commit a data manifest**, `outcome-prediction-service/meps-manifest.json`, holding the checksums of both the zips and the extracted `.dta` files, plus the URLs. The download step checks against it. This needs no new infrastructure, so it can go in right away.
2. **Mirror the original zips and the documentation pages** into a private GCS bucket, since the repo already uses GCP. Turn on object versioning and a retention lock, and store each file under its checksum, so a changed upstream file can never replace the original.
3. **Have the download step fall back to the mirror.** It tries AHRQ first and then the mirror, and checks the manifest either way. AHRQ stays the primary source, so the mirror is only a backup copy.
4. **Skip DVC for now.** The manifest plus a mirror covers what DVC would provide here, without adding another tool. DVC becomes worth it once the lab starts producing many derived datasets, so it's worth reconsidering at M3 or M10.

Two cautions:
- **Item 2 is an infrastructure change** (a new bucket, with its access and retention settings), so it's your call. It also leaves the bucket's owner holding a copy of MEPS, which only reinforces the open use-terms question (O23). A private bucket is the conservative choice.
- **None of this applies to customer data.** Patient data would need HIPAA-grade storage under a BAA (Business Associate Agreement), which is a Phase 8b problem. MEPS is public and de-identified, so a simple mirror is fine.

If you agree, I'll do item 1 now as a small PR, and record the approach as a new decision (O41). For items 2 and 3, I'd want your go-ahead on the bucket first.

# Root Terraform module for Phase 3 — STUB (design.md §13/§13.1; not applied until
# Phase 3b). This is the deliverable Phase 2 named but never built (docs/phase2/plan.md's
# "Cloud-delivery gap": "no root module to apply — the per-service stubs are unreferenced
# fragments"). Phase 3's milestone plan named this explicitly as its own M7 deliverable
# rather than an implied side-effect of per-service stubs (design.md §13's callout) —
# this file is that deliverable, not a repeat of the gap.
#
# Composes the three per-service stubs already built and individually `terraform
# validate`-d in M2/M3/M5, plus the pieces Phase 2's gap analysis named as missing
# (Artifact Registry, Secret Manager) and the wiring between them. Two things this
# deliberately does NOT provision, named rather than silently omitted:
#
#   - No Cloud SQL instance. Postgres is Neon (external SaaS), exactly matching how
#     fhir-service already handles it in Phase 1/2 (NEON_*/SPRING_DATASOURCE_URL env
#     vars, no Terraform-managed database resource anywhere in this repo — checked, not
#     assumed). The Secret Manager secret below holds the Neon connection string; the
#     value itself is set out-of-band (e.g. `gcloud secrets versions add`), same as how
#     NEON_* values are already handled for Phase 1/2 — never committed to Terraform state.
#   - No VPC connector. Neon is reached over its public endpoint with TLS, not a private
#     network path — a Serverless VPC Access connector is only needed to reach resources
#     inside a VPC (e.g. a private Cloud SQL instance), which doesn't apply here. Cloud
#     Run's `ingress = internal` on each service already provides the internal-only
#     reachability posture (design.md §9, §12.1) without one.
#
# provider-mcp-server is intentionally NOT composed as a Cloud Run Service here — see its
# own infra/main.tf (decisions.md P16): an stdio-only process has no $PORT listener, so a
# Cloud Run Service resource for it would validate cleanly while being undeployable.

terraform {
  required_providers {
    google = { source = "hashicorp/google", version = "~> 5.0" }
  }
}

provider "google" {
  project = var.project_id
  region  = var.region
}

variable "project_id" {
  type = string
}

variable "region" {
  type    = string
  default = "us-central1"
}

# ── Shared secret — the Neon connection string, value set out-of-band ───────────────────
resource "google_secret_manager_secret" "database_url" {
  secret_id = "provider-registry-database-url"
  replication {
    auto {}
  }
}

# ── Compose the per-service stubs ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# provider-mcp-server's module owns the ONE shared Artifact Registry repo (it already
# declared one in M5); the other two modules' images publish into that same repo via its
# output, rather than each declaring — and potentially duplicating — their own. Composed
# first so its output is available to the other two.
module "provider_mcp_server" {
  source        = "../../provider-mcp-server/infra"
  project_id    = var.project_id
  region        = var.region
  repository_id = "provider-search"
}

locals {
  image_base = "${var.region}-docker.pkg.dev/${var.project_id}/${module.provider_mcp_server.repository_id}"
}

module "provider_registry_service" {
  source              = "../../provider-registry-service/infra"
  project_id          = var.project_id
  region              = var.region
  image               = "${local.image_base}/provider-registry-service:latest"
  database_url_secret = google_secret_manager_secret.database_url.secret_id
}

module "provider_ingest_job" {
  source              = "../../data/scripts/provider_ingest/infra"
  project_id          = var.project_id
  region              = var.region
  image               = "${local.image_base}/provider-ingest:latest"
  database_url_secret = google_secret_manager_secret.database_url.secret_id
  states              = "NC,CA,MT" # the full curated set (M3/M4), not the single-state default
}

# provider-curation-agent and provider-search-agent are run-once CLIs, like claims-agent —
# no Cloud Run resource for either (same reasoning as Phase 2's claims-agent, which also
# has no Cloud Run config). They're built as images (Dockerfiles exist) for local/CI use,
# not deployed as standing services.

output "artifact_registry_repository" {

"""The committed MEPS data manifest (docs/phase8/decisions.md O41, O42).

``outcome-prediction-service/meps-manifest.json`` is committed to git — like a lock file for
data. For every MEPS file it records the source URLs and the SHA-256 of the original zip, the
extracted .dta, and the documentation snapshot (doc page + codebook PDF). The data itself is
never committed; the manifest is what makes "the same data" checkable years later.

``download.fetch`` refuses any bytes that don't match the manifest — from AHRQ or a mirror.
Adopting a new AHRQ release is therefore a deliberate, reviewed change:

    python -m outcome_prediction.meps.manifest snapshot                  # record (first time)
    python -m outcome_prediction.meps.manifest snapshot --accept-change  # re-record after AHRQ changed a file

Snapshot also keeps the original zips and documentation in the local archive
(<data>/raw/meps/archive/) so they can be pushed to the private mirrors (meps.mirror).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import hashlib
import json
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

from outcome_prediction.meps import LONGITUDINAL_PANELS
from outcome_prediction.settings import SERVICE_ROOT, meps_cache_dir

MANIFEST_PATH = SERVICE_ROOT / "meps-manifest.json"
DATA_URL = "https://meps.ahrq.gov/data_files/pufs/h{n}/h{n}dta.zip"
DOC_URL = "https://meps.ahrq.gov/data_stats/download_data/pufs/h{n}/h{n}doc.shtml"
CODEBOOK_URL = "https://meps.ahrq.gov/data_stats/download_data/pufs/h{n}/h{n}cb.pdf"


class ManifestChange(RuntimeError):
    """AHRQ now serves different data bytes than the manifest records."""


def archive_dir() -> Path:
    return meps_cache_dir() / "archive"


def sha256(data: bytes) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()


def load_manifest(path: Path | None = None) -> dict:
    path = path or MANIFEST_PATH
    return json.loads(path.read_text()) if path.exists() else {"files": {}}


def save_manifest(manifest: dict, path: Path | None = None) -> None:
    (path or MANIFEST_PATH).write_text(json.dumps(manifest, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n")


def entry_for(manifest: dict, file_number: int) -> dict | None:
    return manifest.get("files", {}).get(f"h{file_number}")


def _panel_for(file_number: int) -> int | None:
    return next((p for p, n in LONGITUDINAL_PANELS.items() if n == file_number), None)


def snapshot(file_number: int, manifest: dict, *, accept_change: bool = False,
             archive: Path | None = None, fetch_bytes=None) -> dict:
    """Download the original zip, doc page and codebook; archive them; return the manifest
    entry. Raises ManifestChange if the data differs from an existing entry, unless accepted."""
    from outcome_prediction.meps.download import _extract_dta, _fetch_zip

    fetch_bytes = fetch_bytes or _fetch_zip
    archive = archive or archive_dir()
    archive.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    zip_name, dta_name = f"h{file_number}dta.zip", f"h{file_number}.dta"
    zip_bytes = fetch_bytes(DATA_URL.format(n=file_number))
    dta_bytes = _extract_dta(zip_bytes, dta_name)
    data = {"url": DATA_URL.format(n=file_number), "zip_name": zip_name,
            "zip_sha256": sha256(zip_bytes), "zip_bytes": len(zip_bytes),
            "dta_name": dta_name, "dta_sha256": sha256(dta_bytes), "dta_bytes": len(dta_bytes)}

    previous = entry_for(manifest, file_number)
    if previous and not accept_change and (
            previous["data"]["zip_sha256"], previous["data"]["dta_sha256"]) != (
            data["zip_sha256"], data["dta_sha256"]):
        raise ManifestChange(
            f"AHRQ now serves different bytes for {zip_name} than the manifest records "
            f"(zip {previous['data']['zip_sha256'][:12]}… -> {data['zip_sha256'][:12]}…). "
            f"Investigate the release notes; re-run with --accept-change to adopt it.")

    docs = []
    for url in (DOC_URL.format(n=file_number), CODEBOOK_URL.format(n=file_number)):
        body = fetch_bytes(url)
        name = url.rsplit("/", 1)[1]
        (archive / name).write_bytes(body)
        docs.append({"url": url, "name": name, "sha256": sha256(body), "bytes": len(body)})
    (archive / zip_name).write_bytes(zip_bytes)

    return {"panel": _panel_for(file_number),
            "kind": "longitudinal" if _panel_for(file_number) else "other",
            "retrieved_at": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="seconds"),
            "data": data, "documentation": docs}


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    parser.add_argument("command", choices=["snapshot"])
    parser.add_argument("files", nargs="*", type=int,
                        help="MEPS file numbers (default: all two-year longitudinal panels)")
    parser.add_argument("--accept-change", action="store_true",
                        help="adopt data that differs from the manifest (a deliberate, reviewed change)")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    manifest = load_manifest()
    manifest.setdefault("files", {})
    manifest["description"] = (
        "MEPS public-use files used by Phase 8, by SHA-256. Data is never committed; "
        "download.fetch refuses bytes that don't match. See docs/phase8/decisions.md O41-O42.")
    for n in args.files or LONGITUDINAL_PANELS.values():
        entry = snapshot(n, manifest, accept_change=args.accept_change)
        manifest["files"][f"h{n}"] = entry
        d = entry["data"]
        print(f"h{n}: zip {d['zip_bytes']:>11,} B {d['zip_sha256'][:12]}…  "
              f"dta {d['dta_bytes']:>12,} B {d['dta_sha256'][:12]}…  "
              f"docs {sum(x['bytes'] for x in entry['documentation']):>11,} B")
    save_manifest(manifest)
    print(f"wrote {MANIFEST_PATH}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""FR-D1: download MEPS Stata files, verify them, and cache them.

Each file arrives as https://meps.ahrq.gov/data_files/pufs/h{n}/h{n}dta.zip containing
h{n}.dta (the folder-less URL form returns 404).

**Files in the committed manifest** (meps-manifest.json — decisions.md O41, O42) are verified

Each file arrives as https://meps.ahrq.gov/data_files/pufs/h{n}/h{n}dta.zip containing
h{n}.dta (the folder-less URL form returns 404). The extracted .dta's SHA-256 is recorded
in <cache>/checksums.json on first download and verified on every later use, so a
silently changed or corrupted file fails loudly instead of shifting the numbers.

Usage:
    python -m outcome_prediction.meps.download            # all longitudinal panels
    python -m outcome_prediction.meps.download 252 241    # specific file numbers
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import hashlib
import io
import json
import urllib.request
import zipfile
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

from outcome_prediction.meps import LONGITUDINAL_PANELS
from outcome_prediction.settings import meps_cache_dir

URL = "https://meps.ahrq.gov/data_files/pufs/h{n}/h{n}dta.zip"
CHECKSUMS = "checksums.json"
TIMEOUT_S = 120


class ChecksumMismatch(RuntimeError):
    """A cached file no longer matches the checksum recorded when it was downloaded."""


def _sha256(data: bytes) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()


def _load_checksums(cache: Path) -> dict:
    path = cache / CHECKSUMS
    return json.loads(path.read_text()) if path.exists() else {}


def _save_checksums(cache: Path, checksums: dict) -> None:
    (cache / CHECKSUMS).write_text(json.dumps(checksums, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n")


def _fetch_zip(url: str) -> bytes:
    with urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=TIMEOUT_S) as resp:
        return resp.read()


def _extract_dta(zip_bytes: bytes, member: str) -> bytes:
    """Read one named member's bytes. Never ZipFile.extract(): we write to a path we choose,
    so a hostile member name can't escape the cache directory."""
    with zipfile.ZipFile(io.BytesIO(zip_bytes)) as zf:
        names = {name.lower(): name for name in zf.namelist()}
        if member.lower() not in names:
            raise FileNotFoundError(f"{member} not in archive (found: {sorted(zf.namelist())})")
        return zf.read(names[member.lower()])


def fetch(file_number: int, cache: Path | None = None) -> Path:
    """Return the path to h{n}.dta, downloading it if absent; verify its checksum either way."""
    cache = cache or meps_cache_dir()
    cache.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    name = f"h{file_number}.dta"
    path = cache / name
    checksums = _load_checksums(cache)

    if path.exists():
        recorded = checksums.get(name, {}).get("sha256")
        actual = _sha256(path.read_bytes())
        if recorded is None:
            # Present but never recorded (e.g. copied in by hand): record it now.
            checksums[name] = {"sha256": actual, "source_url": None, "recorded_at": _now()}
            _save_checksums(cache, checksums)
        elif recorded != actual:
            raise ChecksumMismatch(
                f"{path} has sha256 {actual}, but {recorded} was recorded when it was "
                f"downloaded. Delete the file to re-download, or investigate the change."
            )
        return path

    url = URL.format(n=file_number)
    data = _extract_dta(_fetch_zip(url), name)
    tmp = path.with_suffix(".dta.part")
    tmp.write_bytes(data)
    tmp.replace(path)
    checksums[name] = {"sha256": _sha256(data), "source_url": url, "recorded_at": _now()}
    _save_checksums(cache, checksums)
    return path


def _now() -> str:
    return datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="seconds")


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    parser.add_argument("files", nargs="*", type=int,
                        help="MEPS file numbers (default: all two-year longitudinal panels)")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    for n in args.files or LONGITUDINAL_PANELS.values():
        path = fetch(n)
        print(f"h{n}.dta  {path.stat().st_size:>12,} bytes  {path}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Data provenance and preservation (decisions.md O41, O42): the committed manifest, write-once
private mirrors, and the download fallback order. Fully offline — AHRQ is faked."""
from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import io
import re
import zipfile

import pytest

from outcome_prediction.meps import LONGITUDINAL_PANELS, download
from outcome_prediction.meps.download import ChecksumMismatch, SourceUnavailable, fetch
from outcome_prediction.meps.manifest import (
    MANIFEST_PATH, ManifestChange, load_manifest, snapshot,
)
from outcome_prediction.meps.mirror import (
    LocalMirror, MirrorError, from_uri, object_key, push, put, verify,
)

N = 999


def _zip(dta: bytes) -> bytes:
    buf = io.BytesIO()
    with zipfile.ZipFile(buf, "w") as zf:
        zf.writestr(f"h{N}.dta", dta)
    return buf.getvalue()


def _sha(b: bytes) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(b).hexdigest()


ORIGINAL_DTA = b"original stata bytes"
ORIGINAL_ZIP = _zip(ORIGINAL_DTA)


def _manifest() -> dict:
    return {"files": {f"h{N}": {
        "panel": None, "kind": "other", "retrieved_at": "2026-10-17T00:00:00+00:00",
        "data": {"url": f"https://example.invalid/h{N}dta.zip", "zip_name": f"h{N}dta.zip",
                 "zip_sha256": _sha(ORIGINAL_ZIP), "zip_bytes": len(ORIGINAL_ZIP),
                 "dta_name": f"h{N}.dta", "dta_sha256": _sha(ORIGINAL_DTA),
                 "dta_bytes": len(ORIGINAL_DTA)},
        "documentation": [{"url": "https://example.invalid/doc", "name": f"h{N}doc.shtml",
                           "sha256": _sha(b"doc"), "bytes": 3}],
    }}}


@pytest.fixture
def ahrq(monkeypatch):
    """What 'AHRQ' serves: bytes, or an exception to raise."""
    state = {"serve": ORIGINAL_ZIP, "calls": 0}

    def fake(url):
        state["calls"] += 1
        if isinstance(state["serve"], Exception):
            raise state["serve"]
        return state["serve"]

    monkeypatch.setattr(download, "_fetch_zip", fake)
    return state


@pytest.fixture
def mirror(tmp_path):
    m = LocalMirror(tmp_path / "mirror")
    put(m, object_key(_sha(ORIGINAL_ZIP), f"h{N}dta.zip"), ORIGINAL_ZIP)
    return m


# ── The committed manifest ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────


def test_committed_manifest_pins_every_longitudinal_panel():
    files = load_manifest(MANIFEST_PATH)["files"]
    assert set(files) == {f"h{n}" for n in LONGITUDINAL_PANELS.values()}
    for key, entry in files.items():
        assert entry["panel"] == {f"h{n}": p for p, n in LONGITUDINAL_PANELS.items()}[key]
        assert re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{64}", entry["data"]["zip_sha256"])
        assert re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{64}", entry["data"]["dta_sha256"])
        assert {d["name"] for d in entry["documentation"]} == {f"{key}doc.shtml", f"{key}cb.pdf"}


def test_committed_manifest_matches_the_local_cache(meps_cache):
    """Where the real data is present, it is exactly what the manifest pins."""
    for key, entry in load_manifest(MANIFEST_PATH)["files"].items():
        path = meps_cache / entry["data"]["dta_name"]
        assert _sha(path.read_bytes()) == entry["data"]["dta_sha256"], key


# ── Fallback order and verification ──────────────────────────────────────────────────


def test_ahrq_first_and_original_zip_archived(tmp_path, ahrq):
    path = fetch(N, cache=tmp_path, manifest=_manifest(), mirrors=[])
    assert path.read_bytes() == ORIGINAL_DTA
    assert (tmp_path / "archive" / f"h{N}dta.zip").read_bytes() == ORIGINAL_ZIP


def test_archived_zip_is_reused_without_network(tmp_path, ahrq):
    fetch(N, cache=tmp_path, manifest=_manifest(), mirrors=[])
    (tmp_path / f"h{N}.dta").unlink()
    fetch(N, cache=tmp_path, manifest=_manifest(), mirrors=[])
    assert ahrq["calls"] == 1


def test_mirror_used_when_ahrq_is_down(tmp_path, ahrq, mirror):
    ahrq["serve"] = OSError("connection refused")
    assert fetch(N, cache=tmp_path, manifest=_manifest(), mirrors=[mirror]).read_bytes() == ORIGINAL_DTA


def test_changed_upstream_bytes_are_rejected_and_the_mirror_original_used(tmp_path, ahrq, mirror):
    ahrq["serve"] = _zip(b"a quietly corrected re-release")
    assert fetch(N, cache=tmp_path, manifest=_manifest(), mirrors=[mirror]).read_bytes() == ORIGINAL_DTA
    assert (tmp_path / "archive" / f"h{N}dta.zip").read_bytes() == ORIGINAL_ZIP


def test_no_matching_source_fails_loudly_and_caches_nothing(tmp_path, ahrq):
    ahrq["serve"] = _zip(b"different")
    with pytest.raises(SourceUnavailable) as exc:
        fetch(N, cache=tmp_path, manifest=_manifest(), mirrors=[LocalMirror(tmp_path / "empty")])
    message = str(exc.value)
    assert "AHRQ: served sha256" in message and "rejected" in message
    assert "empty" in message                                   # the mirror attempt is reported
    assert not (tmp_path / f"h{N}.dta").exists()
    assert not (tmp_path / "archive" / f"h{N}dta.zip").exists()


def test_missing_mirror_configuration_is_named_in_the_error(tmp_path, ahrq):
    ahrq["serve"] = OSError("down")
    with pytest.raises(SourceUnavailable, match="no private mirrors configured"):
        fetch(N, cache=tmp_path, manifest=_manifest(), mirrors=[])


def test_cached_dta_not_matching_manifest_is_refused(tmp_path, ahrq):
    (tmp_path / f"h{N}.dta").write_bytes(b"something else")
    with pytest.raises(ChecksumMismatch, match="meps-manifest.json"):
        fetch(N, cache=tmp_path, manifest=_manifest(), mirrors=[])


def test_unmanifested_files_keep_the_simple_behaviour(tmp_path, ahrq):
    path = fetch(N, cache=tmp_path, manifest={"files": {}}, mirrors=[])
    assert path.read_bytes() == ORIGINAL_DTA
    assert (tmp_path / "checksums.json").exists()


# ── Mirrors are write-once and content-addressed ─────────────────────────────────────


def test_put_is_write_once(tmp_path):
    m = LocalMirror(tmp_path)
    key = object_key(_sha(b"a"), "f.zip")
    assert put(m, key, b"a") is True
    assert put(m, key, b"a") is False                 # identical: no-op
    with pytest.raises(MirrorError, match="refusing to overwrite"):
        put(m, key, b"b")
    assert m.get(key) == b"a"


def test_object_keys_are_content_addressed_and_safe():
    assert object_key("ab" * 32, "h252dta.zip") == f"meps/sha256/{'ab' * 32}/h252dta.zip"
    for bad in ("../x", "a/b", ".hidden"):
        with pytest.raises(ValueError):
            object_key("ab" * 32, bad)


def test_from_uri(tmp_path):
    assert isinstance(from_uri(f"file://{tmp_path}"), LocalMirror)
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        from_uri("s3://bucket")


def test_push_verifies_against_manifest_then_uploads_everything(tmp_path):
    archive = tmp_path / "archive"
    archive.mkdir()
    (archive / f"h{N}dta.zip").write_bytes(ORIGINAL_ZIP)
    (archive / f"h{N}doc.shtml").write_bytes(b"doc")
    m = LocalMirror(tmp_path / "mirror")

    log = push(_manifest(), archive, [m])

    assert len(log) == 2 and all(line.startswith("uploaded") for line in log)
    assert verify(_manifest(), [m]) == []
    assert all(line.startswith("present") for line in push(_manifest(), archive, [m]))


def test_push_refuses_archive_bytes_that_dont_match_the_manifest(tmp_path):
    archive = tmp_path / "archive"
    archive.mkdir()
    (archive / f"h{N}dta.zip").write_bytes(b"tampered")
    with pytest.raises(MirrorError, match="does not match the manifest"):
        push(_manifest(), archive, [LocalMirror(tmp_path / "mirror")])


def test_verify_reports_missing_and_corrupted_objects(tmp_path, mirror):
    key = object_key(_sha(ORIGINAL_ZIP), f"h{N}dta.zip")
    (mirror.root / key).write_bytes(b"bit rot")
    problems = verify(_manifest(), [mirror])
    assert any("bit rot" not in p and "!= manifest" in p for p in problems)   # corrupted zip
    assert any("unreadable" in p for p in problems)                          # doc never pushed


# ── Snapshot: adopting changed data is deliberate ────────────────────────────────────


def _fake_fetch(zip_bytes):
    return lambda url: zip_bytes if url.endswith("dta.zip") else f"doc for {url}".encode()


def test_snapshot_records_data_and_documentation(tmp_path):
    entry = snapshot(N, {"files": {}}, archive=tmp_path, fetch_bytes=_fake_fetch(ORIGINAL_ZIP))
    assert entry["data"]["zip_sha256"] == _sha(ORIGINAL_ZIP)
    assert entry["data"]["dta_sha256"] == _sha(ORIGINAL_DTA)
    assert [d["name"] for d in entry["documentation"]] == [f"h{N}doc.shtml", f"h{N}cb.pdf"]
    assert (tmp_path / f"h{N}dta.zip").read_bytes() == ORIGINAL_ZIP


def test_snapshot_refuses_changed_data_unless_accepted(tmp_path):
    changed = _fake_fetch(_zip(b"re-release"))
    with pytest.raises(ManifestChange, match="--accept-change"):
        snapshot(N, _manifest(), archive=tmp_path, fetch_bytes=changed)
    entry = snapshot(N, _manifest(), archive=tmp_path, fetch_bytes=changed, accept_change=True)
    assert entry["data"]["dta_sha256"] == _sha(b"re-release")

def test_no_matching_source_fails_loudly_and_caches_nothing(tmp_path, ahrq):

def test_put_is_write_once(tmp_path):
    m = LocalMirror(tmp_path)
    key = object_key(_sha(b"a"), "f.zip")
    assert put(m, key, b"a") is True
    assert put(m, key, b"a") is False                 # identical: no-op
    with pytest.raises(MirrorError, match="refusing to overwrite"):

def test_object_keys_are_content_addressed_and_safe():
    assert object_key("ab" * 32, "h252dta.zip") == f"meps/sha256/{'ab' * 32}/h252dta.zip"

def test_from_uri(tmp_path):

def test_push_verifies_against_manifest_then_uploads_everything(tmp_path):
    archive = tmp_path / "archive"
    archive.mkdir()
    (archive / f"h{N}dta.zip").write_bytes(ORIGINAL_ZIP)
    (archive / f"h{N}doc.shtml").write_bytes(b"doc")
    m = LocalMirror(tmp_path / "mirror")

    log = push(_manifest(), archive, [m])

def _fake_fetch(zip_bytes):

    assert [d["name"] for d in entry["documentation"]] == [f"h{N}doc.shtml", f"h{N}cb.pdf"]
    assert (tmp_path / f"h{N}dta.zip").read_bytes() == ORIGINAL_ZIP

    assert entry["data"]["dta_sha256"] == _sha(b"re-release")

Added after the repo owner asked what the industry practice is for keeping data that the code
doesn't store — given that a public source can go down, move, or change. Code in git; data in

owner chose to implement all of it now, with private bucket(s) and without DVC.

|---|---|---|---|
| O41 | **Data is pinned in git and preserved outside it.** A committed manifest, `outcome-prediction-service/meps-manifest.json`, records the URL and SHA-256 of every original MEPS zip, extracted `.dta`, documentation page and codebook. The originals are mirrored, write-once and content-addressed (`meps/sha256/<sha>/<name>`), to **private** GCS bucket(s) with public access prevention enforced and a retention policy; the bucket's Terraform is `outcome-prediction-service/infra/`. `download.fetch` tries the local archive, then AHRQ, then each mirror in `OUTCOME_PREDICTION_MEPS_MIRRORS`, accepting only bytes that match the manifest. **DVC not adopted**, per the repo owner — the manifest plus mirrors cover what it would add here | Accepted (bucket not yet applied — needs GCP credentials this repo doesn't provision) | Before this, nothing in git pinned the data: `checksums.json` lived in the gitignored cache. AHRQ stays the primary source, so the mirror is a backstop, not a redistribution. Private, not a public archive (Zenodo etc.), because redistribution rights are part of the open O23 question. | O42 | **A changed upstream file is rejected, not adopted.** If AHRQ republishes different bytes, `fetch` refuses them and uses a mirror's original; adopting the new release is a deliberate, reviewed change (`manifest snapshot --accept-change`, a git diff of the manifest), followed by re-running the reproduction tests | Accepted | Statistical agencies do re-release corrected files. ## Supersession notes""")])

## 13. Data provenance and preservation (O41, O42)

```
outcome-prediction-service/
  meps-manifest.json          # COMMITTED: per file — URLs, SHA-256 of zip, .dta, doc page, codebook
  infra/main.tf               # private GCS archive bucket (standalone root module; not yet applied)
  src/outcome_prediction/meps/
    manifest.py               # `snapshot`: record originals; `--accept-change` to adopt a re-release
    mirror.py                 # write-once, content-addressed mirrors: gs:// and file://; push / verify
    download.py               # fetch: archive -> AHRQ -> mirrors, manifest-verified
  data/raw/meps/archive/      # gitignored: original zips + docs, the source for `mirror push`
```

**Fetch order** for a manifested file: the original zip in the local archive → AHRQ → each mirror
in `OUTCOME_PREDICTION_MEPS_MIRRORS`. Every candidate is hashed against the manifest; a mismatch
is rejected and recorded in the error, never cached. Unmanifested files (future event files
before they're added) keep the M1 behaviour.

**Mirror layout:** `meps/sha256/<sha256>/<original name>`. Content-addressed keys mean a
re-release lands beside the original rather than replacing it, and `put` refuses to overwrite.

**The bucket** (`infra/main.tf`): private (uniform access, public access prevention enforced),
retention policy (default 10 years, lock is a separate irreversible step), 90-day soft delete,
multi-region `US` by default, `prevent_destroy`, writers create-only. Verified so far: Terraform
`validate`/`fmt` clean; a `file://` mirror of all 21 originals (121 MB) pushed and verified, and
— with AHRQ simulated as unreachable in a fresh workspace — all seven panels restored from it
and the M1 table rebuilt byte-identical (sha256 `950d8be12078…`, the M2 model ID).
"""

## Data manifest and private mirror

Data is never committed, but **`meps-manifest.json` is**: the URL and SHA-256 of every original
zip, extracted `.dta`, documentation page and codebook. `download` accepts only bytes that match
it, trying the local archive, then AHRQ, then each private mirror. If AHRQ republishes a file,
the original still comes from a mirror until the manifest is deliberately updated.
(`docs/phase8/decisions.md` O41, O42; `design.md` §13.)

```bash
# Record the originals (zips + doc pages + codebooks) — first time, or to re-check
python -m outcome_prediction.meps.manifest snapshot
# AHRQ changed a file? Adopting it is a deliberate, reviewed manifest change:
python -m outcome_prediction.meps.manifest snapshot --accept-change

# Copy the originals to every configured mirror (write-once), and audit them
export OUTCOME_PREDICTION_MEPS_MIRRORS=gs://<bucket>,file:///mnt/backup/meps   # tried in order
python -m outcome_prediction.meps.mirror push
python -m outcome_prediction.meps.mirror verify
```

`gs://` mirrors need `pip install -e "outcome-prediction-service[gcs]"` and Application Default
Credentials (`gcloud auth application-default login`). `file://` is any directory — an extra
offline copy (e.g. an external disk).

### Creating the private bucket (once)

`infra/main.tf` is a standalone Terraform root module — private, retention-protected,
multi-region. It hasn't been applied: this repo provisions no GCP credentials.

```bash
cd outcome-prediction-service/infra
terraform init
terraform apply -var project_id=<gcp-project> \
  -var 'writer_members=["user:<you>@<domain>"]' -var 'reader_members=["user:<you>@<domain>"]'
# then: OUTCOME_PREDICTION_MEPS_MIRRORS=$(terraform output -raw mirror_uri) ... mirror push / verify
```

`lock_retention` stays `false` at first: locking makes the retention policy permanent and can't
be undone. Flip it deliberately once `mirror verify` passes.

## Tests

# outcome-prediction-service

Phase 8's machine-learning service: builds the training data from AHRQ MEPS, and (from later
milestones) trains, evaluates and serves the 12-month hospitalization model as FHIR
`RiskAssessment`s. Planning, decisions and status: [`docs/phase8/`](../docs/phase8/README.md).

**Built so far:** M1 (MEPS acquisition, dataset build, variable dictionary) and M2 (training,
evaluation, model artifact). No API or compose service yet.

## Install

```bash
python -m pip install -e "outcome-prediction-service[dev]"
```

## Pipeline stages (one command each)

```bash
# 1. Download + checksum the seven two-year longitudinal panels (~38 MB of zips, ~720 MB extracted)
python -m outcome_prediction.meps.download

# 2. Build the modelling table: 56,360 adults, 4,820 year-2 hospitalizations
python -m outcome_prediction.meps.build
#    -> data/processed/meps_hosp12.csv
#    -> data/processed/meps_hosp12_build_report.json   (per-panel counts, resolved diagnosis columns)

# 3. Variable dictionary for any MEPS file (here HC-252)
python -m outcome_prediction.meps.dictionary 252
#    -> data/processed/h252_dictionary.csv

# 4. Evaluate (temporal test, panels 21-25 -> 26-27), refit on all panels, write the artifact
python -m outcome_prediction.model.train
#    -> models/gbm-meps25-v1-<table sha256[:12]>/   model.joblib, comparison.joblib,
#                                                   metadata.json, MANIFEST.sha256
#    -> data/reports/metrics.json, data/reports/model_report.md

# (evaluation only, no artifact)
python -m outcome_prediction.model.evaluate
```

**Artifacts** (`models/`, gitignored) are never overwritten: the model ID is derived from the
training table's checksum, so rebuilding from the same table means deleting the old artifact
deliberately. `load_artifact()` verifies every file against `MANIFEST.sha256` *before* any
`joblib` deserialisation, and refuses missing, changed or unlisted files. The headline metrics in
`metadata.json` come from the validation models (panels 21–25 → 26–27); the stored models are
refit on all panels, so their own held-out performance is unknown by construction.

`scikit-learn` is pinned to exactly 1.9.1 — pickled models aren't portable across versions.

Everything generated lands under `outcome-prediction-service/data/` (gitignored). Point several
worktrees at one cache with `OUTCOME_PREDICTION_DATA_DIR=/path/to/data`.

**Checksums.** The first download records each `.dta`'s SHA-256 in
`data/raw/meps/checksums.json`; every later run verifies it and stops with `ChecksumMismatch`
if a file changed. Delete the file to re-download deliberately.

## Tests

```bash
pytest outcome-prediction-service/src/outcome_prediction/tests -q -rs
```

Unit tests use tiny synthetic Stata files and a synthetic modelling table.
`test_meps_reproduction.py` and `test_model_reproduction.py` — the M1/M2 acceptance checks
against the prototype's exact numbers — need the real MEPS cache and **self-skip** without it
(as in CI, where the download is deliberately not run).

## Data and licence notes

MEPS public-use files are free US government data; whether their terms allow commercial use
of trained models is unconfirmed (`docs/phase8/decisions.md` O23,
[`data/reference/README.md`](../data/reference/README.md)). No PHI is ever used here.

## Summary

Implements the data-management practice we discussed: **pointers to the data in git, the original files in private storage you control**. DVC is not adopted, at your request. Recorded as decisions **O41** and **O42**.

| Piece | What it does |
|---|---|
| `meps-manifest.json` (committed) | Records the URL and SHA-256 of every original zip, extracted `.dta`, documentation page and codebook for all 7 panels. Works like a lock file, but for data. |
| `meps.manifest snapshot` | Records the originals into a local archive. **Refuses** changed AHRQ data unless `--accept-change` is given, so adopting a re-release shows up as a reviewed change to the manifest in git. |
| `meps.mirror push / verify` | Write-once copies, stored under each file's checksum (`meps/sha256/<sha>/<name>`). `gs://` and `file://` targets are both supported. |
| `meps.download` | Tries sources in order: local archive, then AHRQ, then each mirror listed in `OUTCOME_PREDICTION_MEPS_MIRRORS`. Accepts **only** bytes that match the manifest; anything else is rejected and never cached. |
| `infra/main.tf` | The private GCS bucket's Terraform, standalone. Detailed below. |

### The bucket's protections

- **Private:** public access prevention is enforced, and nothing grants access to `allUsers`.
- **Can't be deleted or overwritten:** a retention policy, defaulting to 10 years. Locking it in place is irreversible, so `lock_retention` defaults to off.
- **Recoverable:** soft delete keeps a deleted object restorable for 90 days.
- **Off-site:** multi-region `US` by default.
- **Least privilege:** writers can only create objects, not read, delete or overwrite them; readers get read-only access.
- **Protected from Terraform:** `prevent_destroy` stops a `terraform destroy` from removing it.

**Object versioning is deliberately off.** Under a retention policy an object can't be overwritten or deleted at all, which is stronger. Content-addressed keys mean there's never a reason to overwrite one.

## ⚠️ Not yet applied: needs your GCP access

This repo provisions no GCP credentials, and none exist in this environment: no `gcloud`, no Application Default Credentials. The module passes `terraform validate` and `fmt`, and is now in the CI validate matrix, but **the bucket does not exist yet**. Steps are in `outcome-prediction-service/README.md` under "Creating the private bucket":

  - the fallback order;
  - rejection of changed upstream bytes, with the mirror's original used instead;
  - all sources failing, reported loudly with nothing cached;
  - write-once mirrors and safe object keys;
  - `push` refusing archive files that don't match the manifest;
  - `verify` catching corrupted and missing objects;
  - `snapshot` requiring `--accept-change`.
- **GCS-specific tests** use an in-memory fake bucket that raises the library's real `PreconditionFailed`. A `gs://` mirror without credentials doesn't block AHRQ; it just shows up as one failed source. These tests live in their own module so they skip cleanly without the `[gcs]` extra. CI now installs `[dev,gcs]`.

## Docs

- `decisions.md`: new decisions O41 and O42.
- `design.md`: new §13.
- Phase README: new "Data that outlives its source" section.
- Service README: the manifest, mirror and bucket steps.
- `data/reference/README.md`: the MEPS catalog row updated.
- Decision ranges updated to O1–O42.

PR #68's branch, `feature/phase8-m2-training`, is deleted on `origin` and locally; only `main` and `ai-chat-history` remain. The data-management work is in **PR #69**: https://github.com/bhaskarcmu/fhir-agent/pull/69. It's all built and tested, except one step that needs your GCP access: the bucket isn't created yet.

**What's in it**
- **`meps-manifest.json`, committed to git.** It records the URL and checksum of every original MEPS zip, data file, documentation page and codebook, like a package lock file but for data. Its checksums match the M1 data and the checksums stored with the M2 model, so it pins exactly the data the reproduced model was trained on.
- **Downloads verify against it.** The download step tries the local archive, then AHRQ, then each private mirror in turn. It accepts only bytes matching the manifest. If AHRQ quietly republishes a file, the new bytes are rejected and the original comes from a mirror.
- **Adopting a re-release has to be deliberate.** `manifest snapshot` records the originals, and `--accept-change` adopts new bytes as a reviewed change in git.
- **Mirrors are write-once.** Each file is stored under its own checksum, so a new release sits beside the original instead of replacing it. Both `gs://` buckets and plain `file://` directories (e.g. an external disk) work, and `mirror verify` re-checks every stored copy.
- **The private bucket is defined in Terraform** (`outcome-prediction-service/infra/`):
  - public access blocked;
  - files can't be deleted or overwritten for 10 years;
  - deleted files recoverable for 90 days;
  - stored across several US regions;
  - uploaders can only add files, not read, change or delete them.

  Since locked files can't be overwritten at all, I left object versioning off. I also left the permanent retention lock off by default, because it can't be undone.

**Tested end to end on the real data**
- All 21 original files (121 MB) went to a local test mirror and passed verification.
- I then simulated AHRQ being unreachable. A fresh workspace restored all seven panels from the mirror and rebuilt the training table byte for byte. Its checksum starts `950d8be12078`, matching the M2 model ID.
- With the MEPS data: 84 tests pass. Without it, as in CI: 68 pass and 16 skip.
- `terraform validate` and `fmt` are clean, and the module is now in CI's validation list.

**Branch:** `feature/phase8-data-provenance`. **Commit:** `f74d30a0`. The decisions are recorded as O41 and O42, with design §13 and the READMEs updated.

**Two limitations:**
- **The bucket hasn't been created, because this environment has no GCP access** (no `gcloud`, no credentials), the same as all the repo's other Terraform. To create and fill it:
  ```bash
  cd outcome-prediction-service/infra && terraform init
  terraform apply -var project_id=<your-project> -var 'writer_members=["user:<you>"]' -var 'reader_members=["user:<you>"]'
  export OUTCOME_PREDICTION_MEPS_MIRRORS=$(terraform output -raw mirror_uri)
  python -m outcome_prediction.meps.mirror push && python -m outcome_prediction.meps.mirror verify
  ```

content.text:
Yes, and both pieces are available: Docker and Compose work here, and the installed GCS client honours `STORAGE_EMULATOR_HOST`. The thing to decide first is what the mimic is for, because it can deliver one of two things.

**1. Running the real GCS code path, without a GCP account: yes.**
- `fake-gcs-server` is a widely used open-source GCS emulator. It would run in Docker under the `phase8` compose profile, the same way this repo already runs Epic, Athena and RxClaim emulators.
- With `STORAGE_EMULATOR_HOST` set, `mirror push`, `verify` and the download fallback would use the real `google-cloud-storage` client against it. That closes the gap I flagged: the `gs://` code has so far only been tested against a fake bucket inside the tests.
- Two caveats:
  - The emulator doesn't enforce retention policies, access rules or public-access prevention. Those exist only in the Terraform, which would stay in the repo, unapplied, for whenever you want the real bucket.
  - I haven't confirmed it honours the "create only if absent" condition that write-once uploads rely on. I'd check that first, and if it doesn't, say so rather than claim it's covered.

**2. Keeping the data safe if AHRQ disappears: no.**
- A mimic stores its files inside this workspace, so it disappears with the workspace. It's a test stand-in, not a backup.
- If you want a real copy without GCP, the cheapest option already works: the `file://` mirror pointed at a directory outside this workspace (an external disk, a NAS, another machine). No new code is needed. Without one of those, the only copies are AHRQ and this workspace.

**My recommendation:** do both, since they solve different problems.
- Add the `fake-gcs-server` mimic for testing, with a CI-runnable check that pushes and verifies through it.
- Record in O41 that the real bucket is deferred, not dropped. The status becomes "local GCS emulator in place; the real bucket is ready to apply when wanted".
- Separately, decide where your off-workspace copy will live, even if it's just a `file://` path on a disk you own.

cat >> docker-compose.yml <<'EOF'

  # ── Phase 8: local GCS emulator for the private MEPS mirror ─────────────────
  # Stands in for the real private bucket (outcome-prediction-service/infra/, not applied)
  # so the gs:// mirror code runs for real against the google-cloud-storage client
  # (docs/phase8/decisions.md O41, O43). A TEST STAND-IN, NOT A BACKUP: its storage lives
  # in this workspace (gitignored outcome-prediction-service/data/gcs-emulator/), and it
  # does not enforce the real bucket's retention policy, IAM or public-access prevention.
  # Point the client at it with STORAGE_EMULATOR_HOST=http://localhost:4443.
  gcs-emulator:
    image: fsouza/fake-gcs-server:1.56.1
    container_name: fhir-agent-gcs-emulator
    profiles: ["phase8"]
    command: ["-scheme", "http", "-port", "4443", "-backend", "filesystem",
              "-filesystem-root", "/storage", "-public-host", "localhost:4443"]
    ports:
      - "4443:4443"
    volumes:
      - ./outcome-prediction-service/data/gcs-emulator:/storage
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "wget", "-q", "-O", "/dev/null", "http://localhost:4443/storage/v1/b"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 12
EOF
docker compose config --services | sort | paste -sd' '; docker compose --profile phase8 config --services | grep gcs

"""gs:// mirrors against a real GCS emulator (fake-gcs-server — decisions.md O43): the actual
google-cloud-storage client, HTTP and the generation precondition, end to end.

Self-skips unless STORAGE_EMULATOR_HOST points at a running emulator. Locally:
    docker compose --profile phase8 up -d --wait gcs-emulator
    STORAGE_EMULATOR_HOST=http://localhost:4443 pytest <this file>
CI starts the same image and sets the variable, so this runs on every PR.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import os
import urllib.request
import uuid

import pytest

storage = pytest.importorskip("google.cloud.storage", reason="needs the [gcs] extra")

from outcome_prediction.meps.download import fetch  # noqa: E402
from outcome_prediction.meps.mirror import (  # noqa: E402
    MirrorError, from_uri, object_key, push, put, verify,
)
from outcome_prediction.tests.test_meps_provenance import (  # noqa: E402,F401 — `ahrq` is a fixture
    N, ORIGINAL_DTA, ORIGINAL_ZIP, _manifest, _sha, ahrq,
)


@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
def bucket():
    host = os.environ.get("STORAGE_EMULATOR_HOST")
    if not host:
        pytest.skip("STORAGE_EMULATOR_HOST not set — no GCS emulator to test against")
    try:
        urllib.request.urlopen(f"{host}/storage/v1/b", timeout=3)
    except OSError as exc:
        pytest.skip(f"GCS emulator not reachable at {host} ({exc.__class__.__name__})")
    name = f"phase8-test-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:12]}"
    storage.Client(project="local").create_bucket(name)
    return name


def test_write_once_is_enforced_by_the_server(bucket):
    m = from_uri(f"gs://{bucket}/write-once")
    key = object_key(_sha(b"a"), "f.zip")
    assert put(m, key, b"a") is True
    assert put(m, key, b"a") is False          # server returned 412; content identical
    with pytest.raises(MirrorError, match="refusing to overwrite"):
        put(m, key, b"b")
    assert m.get(key) == b"a"


def test_push_then_verify_round_trip(bucket, tmp_path):
    archive = tmp_path / "archive"
    archive.mkdir()
    (archive / f"h{N}dta.zip").write_bytes(ORIGINAL_ZIP)
    (archive / f"h{N}doc.shtml").write_bytes(b"doc")
    m = from_uri(f"gs://{bucket}/round-trip")

    assert all(line.startswith("uploaded") for line in push(_manifest(), archive, [m]))
    assert verify(_manifest(), [m]) == []
    assert all(line.startswith("present") for line in push(_manifest(), archive, [m]))


def test_verify_reports_objects_missing_from_the_bucket(bucket):
    problems = verify(_manifest(), [from_uri(f"gs://{bucket}/empty-prefix")])
    assert len(problems) == 2 and all("unreadable" in p for p in problems)


def test_fetch_falls_back_to_the_bucket_when_ahrq_is_down(bucket, tmp_path, ahrq):
    m = from_uri(f"gs://{bucket}/fallback")
    put(m, object_key(_sha(ORIGINAL_ZIP), f"h{N}dta.zip"), ORIGINAL_ZIP)
    ahrq["serve"] = OSError("down")
    assert fetch(N, cache=tmp_path, manifest=_manifest(), mirrors=[m]).read_bytes() == ORIGINAL_DTA


def test_fetch_rejects_changed_upstream_and_uses_the_bucket_original(bucket, tmp_path, ahrq):
    import io
    import zipfile
    m = from_uri(f"gs://{bucket}/changed")
    put(m, object_key(_sha(ORIGINAL_ZIP), f"h{N}dta.zip"), ORIGINAL_ZIP)
    buf = io.BytesIO()
    with zipfile.ZipFile(buf, "w") as zf:
        zf.writestr(f"h{N}.dta", b"quiet re-release")
    ahrq["serve"] = buf.getvalue()
    assert fetch(N, cache=tmp_path, manifest=_manifest(), mirrors=[m]).read_bytes() == ORIGINAL_DTA
