# Model card — `er-admit-v2` (round 004-focus-four-readiness)

Production contract meps-portable-v2, records-only tier; income learned-missing and blanked at scoring.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Intended use** | Population-level planning aid for primary-care care management; not a diagnosis, not for emergencies |
| **Outcome** | `admit_via_er_y2` — a hospital admission through the emergency room (year 2 of a MEPS two-year panel) |
| **Population** | US civilian non-institutionalised adults (18+) in MEPS panels 21–27, observed in both years |
| **Training data** | Panels 21–25 (2016–2021); evaluation by leave-one-panel-out cross-validation |
| **Test data** | Panels 26–27 (2021–2023), scored once after a holdout-ledger entry |
| **Inputs** | 5 categorical + 26 numeric features (`portable-v2`); text representations: icd_lsa |
| **Model** | `gbm`, task `binary`, params round-001 tuned |
| **Cross-validated performance** | auroc 0.780, auprc 0.186, brier 0.043, top10_ppv 0.195, top10_sensitivity 0.399, auroc_65plus 0.717 (n = 44,497) |
| **Cross-validated baseline** | auroc 0.735, auprc 0.164, brier 0.044, top10_ppv 0.176, top10_sensitivity 0.360, auroc_65plus 0.679 (n = 44,497) |
| **Test performance** | auroc 0.785, auprc 0.192, brier 0.043, top10_ppv 0.199, top10_sensitivity 0.403, auroc_65plus 0.729 (n = 11,863) |
| **Test baseline** | auroc 0.754, auprc 0.185, brier 0.044, top10_ppv 0.189, top10_sensitivity 0.383, auroc_65plus 0.685 (n = 11,863) |
| **Feature contract** | portable-v2 — production contract meps-portable-v2 (O52) |
| **Missing inputs** | trained with missingness augmentation on povcaty1; scored with povcaty1 blanked, as production will |
| **Outcome observable by a customer** | records (within the health system) or claims (all hospitals) |
| **Data provenance** | manifest sha256 `8467b5410f00…`, code `548f63b5d0c5` |

## Subgroup fairness (test panels)

Full tables: [`fairness/er-admit-v2.md`](../fairness/er-admit-v2.md). Widest gaps among groups with enough events:

| Insurance (year 1) | 0.686–0.752 | 0.89–1.24 | 0%–52% |

## Limitations

- Trained on MEPS **self-reported** survey data; customer records differ (codes, charges vs payments,

- Condition codes are 3-character ICD-10 and only for conditions linked to a year-1 medical event.
- Explanations describe what the model weighed, not causes.

  risk, not who would benefit from outreach.

# Round 004 report — readiness of the four focus predictions

**Status:** complete. **Pre-registration:** [`README.md`](./README.md), written before any run.
**Run through the CLI:** [`configs/`](./configs/), [`runs/`](./runs/). **Test-panel looks:** 5, all
pre-registered and logged in [`../../holdout-ledger.md`](../../holdout-ledger.md): one confirmation
(`er-admit-v2`) and four fairness looks. No 65+ specialist met the bar, so none was looked at.
Decisions: O56–O58.

## 1. Headline

**All four focus predictions now have a production-contract (`meps-portable-v2`) model, a subgroup
fairness report and a 65+ check.** On the untouched test panels (26–27, n = 11,863):

| Prediction | Production model | AUROC (all adults) | AUROC (65+) | 65+ baseline | Calibration (mean predicted vs rate) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Admission through the ER | `004/er-admit-v2` (records only) — **new** | **0.785** | 0.729 | 0.685 | 0.051 vs 0.049 |
| Non-obstetric hospital stay | `003/nonobstetric-v2` | 0.795 | 0.701 | 0.639 | 0.080 vs 0.079 |
| Any ER visit | `003/any-ed-v2` | 0.740 | 0.709 | 0.660 | 0.152 vs 0.155 |
| High-cost patient | `003/high-cost-v2-claims` (claims) | 0.834 | 0.782 | 0.634 | 0.105 vs 0.100 |

All four are scored with household income blanked, as production will be (O53).

## 2. Admission through the ER on the production contract (O56)

Cross-validated (panels 21–25):

| Config | Inputs | CV AUROC |
|---|---|---|
| `er-admit-research` | round-001 research features (spending, CCSR, Multum) | 0.7818 |
| `er-admit-v2` | `meps-portable-v2`, records only | **0.7797** |
| `er-admit-v2-claims` | plus prescription fills, home-health days | 0.7798 |
| baseline | age, prior hospital stays, prior ER visits | 0.7347 |

Same pattern as the other admission target: the contract costs almost nothing (−0.002), and claims
add nothing, so the **records-only** model is the production candidate, as pre-registered. Test AUROC
0.785 (round 001's research model: 0.788); the top 10% of predicted risk holds 40% of ER-origin
admissions, at 20% precision (rate 4.9%).

## 3. Fairness (O57)

Full tables, one per model: [`003 fairness/`](../003-portable-contract/fairness/),
[`004 fairness/`](./fairness/). Groups: race/ethnicity, insurance type (year 1), sex, age band. For
each: AUROC with a bootstrap 95% CI (not computed below 20 events), calibration ratio (mean predicted ÷
observed rate), share flagged by the overall top-10% flag, share of the group's cases caught by it,
and precision.

**What holds up**

- **Calibration by race/ethnicity is close** for the three larger groups (White, Hispanic, Black:
  ratios 0.96–1.12 across all four models). No model systematically under-predicts Black adults.
- **Sex:** AUROC within 0.01–0.04 and calibration within 0.95–1.11 for every model.
- **High cost** discriminates at least as well for every minority group as for White adults (0.82–0.89 vs 0.81).

**What a reviewer must see**

| Finding | Where | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| **Uninsured adults are almost never flagged** — 0–2% flagged; the flag catches 0% (ER admission), 5% (non-obstetric stay), 11% (ER visit) of their cases | all four | Their recorded rates are low (2–9%) because the labels measure **use** of care, not need: uninsured people use less. A use-based score will under-serve people who face access barriers (the Obermeyer et al., 2019 pattern). Any outreach programme must not rely on the flag alone for this group |
| **Calibration bends toward the average by age and insurance:** over-predicts 18–44 (ratio 1.16–1.25) and privately insured (1.16–1.24 for the admission targets); under-predicts public-only (0.89) and 75+ (0.90–0.93) | admissions, ER visit | Absolute risks shown to clinicians are a little too low for the highest-risk groups; ranking is unaffected. Recalibration on customer data (Phase 8b) should check calibration **per group**, not just overall |
| **Black adults: lower AUROC for non-obstetric stay** (0.745 vs 0.787 White; CIs 0.709–0.779 vs 0.763–0.807, barely overlapping) | `nonobstetric-v2` | Same calibration (0.96), so not a level bias, but the model separates risk less well. Monitor; candidate for a targeted look in a later round |
| **Asian adults: wide uncertainty** — 21 events for both admission targets; ER-admission AUROC 0.639 (CI 0.512–0.770) | admission targets | Too few events to conclude anything; not evidence of good or bad performance |
| **The top-10% flag is mostly older and publicly insured adults** (75+: 27–41% flagged; public-only: 18–22%) | all four | Expected from base rates. A practice that wants a flag within each age group needs per-group cutoffs; that is a policy choice, not a model one |

Race/ethnicity is **not a model input** and is never narrated per patient (O50); it appears only in
these aggregate reports.

## 4. Adults 65+ (O58)

**Rule (pre-registered):** adopt a 65+-only specialist only if its CV AUROC on 65+ beats the general
model's CV AUROC on 65+ by ≥ +0.005.

| Prediction | General model, CV AUROC on 65+ | 65+ specialist, CV AUROC | Difference | Decision |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Admission through the ER | 0.7169 | 0.6794 | −0.038 | keep general |
| Non-obstetric hospital stay | 0.6988 | 0.6702 | −0.029 | keep general |
| Any ER visit | 0.6918 | 0.6718 | −0.020 | keep general |
| High-cost patient | 0.7870 | 0.7671 | −0.020 | keep general |

(Training rows for the specialists: 10,500 adults 65+ across panels 21–25.)

**The general models win every time, clearly.** A specialist sees a quarter of the data; what the
general model learns from younger adults about how conditions, prior use and medicines relate to
next-year use carries over to older adults. No specialist was confirmed, so the test panels were not
looked at for them.

**Within 65+, every model is weaker than overall** (test AUROC 0.70–0.78 vs 0.74–0.83). That is expected
and not a 65+ defect: overall AUROC is partly bought by separating young from old, and within one age
band that easy gain is gone (every within-band AUROC is lower — fairness tables, "Age band"). Against
the 65+ baseline the models still add 0.04–0.15. Calibration for 65+: ratios 0.90–1.07 (slight
under-prediction for admissions and ER visits at 75+).

## 5. Limitations

- Fairness numbers are from one test window (2021–2023) on MEPS survey data; customer populations
  differ. They are a starting point for the per-customer fairness check in Phase 8b, not a clearance.
- Groups are the five MEPS race/ethnicity categories; "Other or multiple" and Asian adults have few
  events — conclusions about them are weak in either direction.
- Insurance is year-1 coverage; people switching coverage are classed by year 1.
- Fairness here is about the model's errors; the label itself (use of care) carries the access bias
  noted in §3, which no model change can fix.

All four are scored with household income blanked, as production will be (O53).

## 2. Admission through the ER on the production contract (O56)

Cross-validated (panels 21–25):

| Config | Inputs | CV AUROC |
|---|---|---|
| `er-admit-research` | round-001 research features (spending, CCSR, Multum) | 0.7818 |
| `er-admit-v2` | `meps-portable-v2`, records only | **0.7797** |
| `er-admit-v2-claims` | plus prescription fills, home-health days | 0.7798 |
| baseline | age, prior hospital stays, prior ER visits | 0.7347 |

Same pattern as the other admission target: the contract costs almost nothing (−0.002), and claims
add nothing, so the **records-only** model is the production candidate, as pre-registered. Test AUROC
0.785 (round 001's research model: 0.788); the top 10% of predicted risk holds 40% of ER-origin
admissions, at 20% precision (rate 4.9%).

## 3. Fairness (O57)

Full tables, one per model: [`003 fairness/`](../003-portable-contract/fairness/),
[`004 fairness/`](./fairness/). Groups: race/ethnicity, insurance type (year 1), sex, age band. For
each: AUROC with a bootstrap 95% CI (not computed below 20 events), calibration ratio (mean predicted ÷
observed rate), share flagged by the overall top-10% flag, share of the group's cases caught by it,
and precision.

**What holds up**

- **Calibration by race/ethnicity is close** for the three larger groups (White, Hispanic, Black:
  ratios 0.96–1.12 across all four models). No model systematically under-predicts Black adults.
- **Sex:** AUROC within 0.01–0.04 and calibration within 0.95–1.11 for every model.
- **High cost** discriminates at least as well for every minority group as for White adults (0.82–0.89 vs 0.81).

**What a reviewer must see**

| Finding | Where | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| **Uninsured adults are almost never flagged** — 0–2% flagged; the flag catches 0% (ER admission), 5% (non-obstetric stay), 11% (ER visit) of their cases | all four | Their recorded rates are low (2–9%) because the labels measure **use** of care, not need: uninsured people use less. A use-based score will under-serve people who face access barriers (the Obermeyer et al., 2019 pattern). Any outreach programme must not rely on the flag alone for this group |
| **Calibration bends toward the average by age and insurance:** over-predicts 18–44 (ratio 1.16–1.25) and privately insured (1.16–1.24 for the admission targets); under-predicts public-only (0.89) and 75+ (0.90–0.93) | admissions, ER visit | Absolute risks shown to clinicians are a little too low for the highest-risk groups; ranking is unaffected. Recalibration on customer data (Phase 8b) should check calibration **per group**, not just overall |
| **Black adults: lower AUROC for non-obstetric stay** (0.745 vs 0.787 White; CIs 0.709–0.779 vs 0.763–0.807, barely overlapping) | `nonobstetric-v2` | Same calibration (0.96), so not a level bias, but the model separates risk less well. Monitor; candidate for a targeted look in a later round |
| **Asian adults: wide uncertainty** — 21 events for both admission targets; ER-admission AUROC 0.639 (CI 0.512–0.770) | admission targets | Too few events to conclude anything; not evidence of good or bad performance |
| **The top-10% flag is mostly older and publicly insured adults** (75+: 27–41% flagged; public-only: 18–22%) | all four | Expected from base rates. A practice that wants a flag within each age group needs per-group cutoffs; that is a policy choice, not a model one |

Race/ethnicity is **not a model input** and is never narrated per patient (O50); it appears only in
these aggregate reports.

## 4. Adults 65+ (O58)

**Rule (pre-registered):** adopt a 65+-only specialist only if its CV AUROC on 65+ beats the general
model's CV AUROC on 65+ by ≥ +0.005.

| Prediction | General model, CV AUROC on 65+ | 65+ specialist, CV AUROC | Difference | Decision |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Admission through the ER | 0.7169 | 0.6794 | −0.038 | keep general |
| Non-obstetric hospital stay | 0.6988 | 0.6702 | −0.029 | keep general |
| Any ER visit | 0.6918 | 0.6718 | −0.020 | keep general |
| High-cost patient | 0.7870 | 0.7671 | −0.020 | keep general |

(Training rows for the specialists: 10,500 adults 65+ across panels 21–25.)

**The general models win every time, clearly.** A specialist sees a quarter of the data; what the
general model learns from younger adults about how conditions, prior use and medicines relate to
next-year use carries over to older adults. No specialist was confirmed, so the test panels were not
looked at for them.

**Within 65+, every model is weaker than overall** (test AUROC 0.70–0.78 vs 0.74–0.83). That is expected
and not a 65+ defect: overall AUROC is partly bought by separating young from old, and within one age
band that easy gain is gone (every within-band AUROC is lower — fairness tables, "Age band"). Against
the 65+ baseline the models still add 0.04–0.15. Calibration for 65+: ratios 0.90–1.07 (slight
under-prediction for admissions and ER visits at 75+).

## 5. Limitations

- Fairness numbers are from one test window (2021–2023) on MEPS survey data; customer populations
  differ. They are a starting point for the per-customer fairness check in Phase 8b, not a clearance.
- Groups are the five MEPS race/ethnicity categories; "Other or multiple" and Asian adults have few
  events — conclusions about them are weak in either direction.
- Insurance is year-1 coverage; people switching coverage are classed by year 1.
- Fairness here is about the model's errors; the label itself (use of care) carries the access bias
  noted in §3, which no model change can fix.

the `outcome-prediction-lab` CLI (run / compare / confirm / card / scorecard / promote / explain /
drug-names / notebook check, in CI); every code named in plain language (O49); self-explanatory
per-patient narratives with comparison groups (O50); TF-IDF on code descriptions (no gain for
gradient boosting, +0.002 for a linear model); character n-grams for drug names (72.6% vs 68.4% class
accuracy on unseen names); a drug-class defect fixed (O51). No test look (pre-registered bar not met).

**Iteration 3 done — round 003** (`outcome-prediction-lab/rounds/003-portable-contract/report.md`): the
portable feature contract `meps-portable-v2` (O52) with "drop, don't impute" and missingness
augmentation (O53), and outcome observability (O54); O25 resolved. Production-contract models on the
test panels: non-obstetric admission 0.795, any ER visit 0.740, high cost 0.834 (with claims).
**M6 and M7 now build against `meps-portable-v2`**, not `meps25-v1`.

**Focus (O55, 2026-10-18):** four predictions — admission through the ER, non-obstetric hospital stay,
any ER visit, high-cost patient ([`prediction-targets.md`](./prediction-targets.md)). Remaining M3 work
applies to these four: a production-contract model for **admission through the ER** (not yet built),
fairness metrics and a 65+ check for all four, the person-scored scorecard criteria, and choosing
the first promotion among them (O40). Round 000 stays.
**Not yet built:** round 000.

---

**Short story:** Reproduce the Synthea ETL as-is, then split training from scoring mode and fix
the prescription leak.
**Depends on:** M3.

---

**Short story:** Close the gap to the prototype's targets (AUROC ≥ 0.78; ≥ 0.73 for 65+) for
what M10 chose.

**Long story:** Run under the protocol. FR-D5 (condition/CCSR and drug-class features from
MEPS event files), FR-D6 as a separately reported survey-only experiment, FR-M5 (hyperparameter
search via the lab's panel-grouped CV), FR-M6 (65+), FR-E6 (fairness by race/ethnicity and
insurance). Decide O25 (non-portable features) with numbers. Any feature that can't be derived
from FHIR stays out of the servable contract.

**Deliverable:** Round report; a candidate with model card, recommended for promotion as a new
contract version; O25 recorded in `decisions.md`.

**Depends on:** M10.

# Phase 8 — Patient Outcome Prediction

> ## Canonical status
>
> **🚧 Focus: four predictions (O55)** — admission through the ER, hospital stay not related to
> pregnancy or childbirth, any ER visit, and being a high-cost patient ([`prediction-targets.md`](./prediction-targets.md)).
> **M1–M2 built** (prototype reproduced exactly). **M3 in progress:** rounds 001–003 done — the lab and
> its CLI, nine targets explored, plain-language narratives, and the portable contract
> `meps-portable-v2` (production models: 0.795 / 0.740 / 0.834 test AUROC for three of the four).
> M10/M11 folded into M3 (O45). M4–M13 planned. A research prototype from an earlier session
> was handed over and reconciled with this repo's conventions; what it established is restated
> in `prototype-baseline.md`, and the raw hand-off documents are not kept in the repo (O5). A
> second pass added a permanent **experimentation track** (`outcome-prediction-lab`, O28–O40).
> `prd.md`, `design.md`, `decisions.md` (`O1`–`O55`), `milestone-plan.md` (M1–M13) and
> `experimentation-protocol.md` reflect both passes. Cloud deployment, recalibration and monitoring
> are reserved for **Phase 8b**.
## 2a. The command line

Every step below has a command (`outcome-prediction-lab --help`):

| Step | Command |
|---|---|
| Run configs (CV, training panels only) | `outcome-prediction-lab run <round> <config> [...]` |
| Compare a round's runs | `outcome-prediction-lab compare <round>` (writes `comparison.md`) |
| Confirm a finalist (one logged test look) | `outcome-prediction-lab confirm <round> <config> --record "why"` |
| Model card / target scorecard | `outcome-prediction-lab card` / `scorecard <round> <config> [--criteria person.json]` |
| Promote (needs a decision ID) | `outcome-prediction-lab promote <round> <config> --decision O<n>` |
| Explain patients | `outcome-prediction-lab explain <round> <config> --patient ID / --sample N / --all` |
| Notebook hygiene | `outcome-prediction-lab notebooks-check` (CI) / `notebooks-strip <file>` |

Configs live in `rounds/<round>/configs/<name>.json` and may only say *what* to model (label, task,
features, model, text representations, parameters, baseline inputs); any key naming panels or splits
is refused.
316:| `explain <round> <config>` | Self-explanatory per-patient narratives (O50) | Never shows outcomes |

content.content:
## Summary

The first iteration of **M3**: a new `outcome-prediction-lab` package and **round 001**. M10 and M11 are folded into M3 (O45). Full results are in [`outcome-prediction-lab/rounds/001-what-and-how/report.md`](outcome-prediction-lab/rounds/001-what-and-how/report.md).

**Method:**
- Every choice was made on leave-one-panel-out cross-validation within panels 21–25.
- Test panels 26–27 were scored **once**, for **pre-registered finalists**, each logged in `holdout-ledger.md` before scoring. The code refuses to score any candidate without a ledger entry.

## Results (test panels 26–27)

| | AUROC | AUPRC | Top-10% PPV |
|---|---|---|---|
| Prototype (reproduced exactly) | 0.769 | 0.265 | 29.3% |
| **New, portable** | **0.788** (+0.019, CI +0.011 to +0.027) | **0.307** | **33.1%** |

**Most of the gain comes from code features (TF-IDF compressed with LSA), and mostly from pregnancy codes predicting childbirth admissions.** On non-obstetric admissions, and among men, those features add only about +0.002. So the round recommends **non-obstetric admission** (test AUROC 0.795) as the headline label (O47).

**Seven new targets**, all beating simple baselines on test:

| Target | Model | Baseline |
|---|---|---|
| Non-obstetric admission | AUROC 0.795 | 0.756 |
| Admission via the ER | AUROC 0.788 | 0.754 |
| Any ED visit | AUROC 0.739 | 0.682 |
| ED visit count | Spearman 0.30 | 0.22 |
| High-cost member | AUROC 0.850 | 0.826 |
| Spending | Spearman 0.74 | 0.68 |
| Death (learning only, O48) | AUROC 0.881 | 0.859 |
| Loss of insurance (learning only, O48) | AUROC 0.871 | 0.798 |

**Concept verdicts:**

| Concept | Verdict |
|---|---|
| TF-IDF / LSA code features | **Useful** |
| Autoencoder and denoising autoencoder | About as good as LSA, at 8× the cost |
| Random forest | Same as gradient boosting |
| Knowledge scores (frailty, Charlson, Elixhauser) | Small gain |
| Tuning; monotonic constraints | Negligible |
| Honest missing-value encoding plus **missingness augmentation** | Fully fixes production-like gaps in income and spending |
| SHAP per-patient narratives, traced to the patient's own codes | **Useful** |
| Single decision tree | Costs 0.056 AUROC for readability |

## Data

- **21 more MEPS files** pinned in the manifest:
  - medical conditions and prescribed medicines for each panel's first year (2016–2022);
  - inpatient stays for each panel's second year (2017–2023).
- Each file was verified by its contents: the year-suffixed weight variable and the panels it holds.
- The 2016 prescriptions file exists only as SAS transport, at a URL without the usual folder. `manifest.py` and `download.py` now support this, and file IDs with a letter suffix (e.g. `239a`).

## Bugs found and fixed during the round

- **MEPS person-ID format drift.** Older files use 8 digits; newer ones add a 2-digit panel prefix. Before normalising, Panel 22 silently had no condition or drug codes.
- **A survey instrument change.** Panel 21 used the SF-12v2 rather than the VR-12, so those scores are treated as missing rather than mixed. Adult BMI was dropped: it's absent from four panels.
- **An evaluation bug** in my own code: the missingness hooks weren't passed, which made it look as if hiding values had no effect. Caught because the results were identical to four decimals; fixed and re-run.

## Housekeeping

- The frailty, Charlson and Elixhauser tables are **vendored from comorbidipy** (MIT, attributed in `NOTICE`). The library itself no longer imports under pandas 3.
- **MLflow** uses a local SQLite store and is an optional `tracking` extra (O46). MLflow 3 retired the file store.
- **Service test changes:** the manifest tests and the emulator-bucket fixture are scoped to the 7 longitudinal panels, so CI doesn't download about 95 MB of extra event files.
- **Lab unit tests** are added to the `phase8` CI job and to `pytest.ini`. Install lines updated in `CLAUDE.md` and `.ona`.
- **Docs:** decisions O45–O55; milestone plan and status updated.

## Tests

- Service: **123 passed** (31 new contract tests).
- Lab: **25 passed**, notebook check clean.
- No duplicate test filenames.
- No data, model or tracking-database files committed. The fitted model is in the gitignored `models/`.

## Round 002 (second commit set): CLI, named codes, text experiments, patient narratives

Full results are in [`outcome-prediction-lab/rounds/002-text-and-explanations/report.md`](outcome-prediction-lab/rounds/002-text-and-explanations/report.md). Every run in this round went through the new CLI.

- **CLI `outcome-prediction-lab`**:
  - `run`, `compare`;
  - `confirm`, which refuses without a ledger entry;
  - `card` and `scorecard`;
  - `promote`, which refuses without a confirmation, a model card, a matching model checksum and a recorded decision, and always refuses learning-only targets;
  - `explain` (`--patient`, `--sample`, `--all`), `drug-names`;
  - `notebooks-check` (now run in CI) and `notebooks-strip`.
- **Plain-language names for every code (O49).** They come from AHRQ's own pinned MEPS documentation, with gaps filled from CDC's ICD-10-CM FY2026 release (public domain, pinned by SHA-256).
- **Self-explanatory narratives for each patient (O50):**
  - every code replaced by its full name;
  - comparisons with the observed rate among comparable adults;
  - the marginal-vs-conditional case explained in the text;
  - race and actual outcomes never shown.

  `explain --all` produced narratives for all 11,863 test-panel patients (median 180 words): 0 contain a raw code, 0 mention race.
- **Text experiments** on non-obstetric admission:
  - TF-IDF on code descriptions adds nothing for gradient boosting, and +0.002 for logistic regression.
  - Character n-grams on drug names map pharmacy names first seen in 2021–22 to the right drug class **72.6%** of the time, versus 68.4% for whole words.
  - **No variant met the pre-registered bar, so there was no test-panel look this round.**
- **Drug-class fix (O51).** Classes now use the most specific Multum level. Round 001 used only the third level, which left 34% of fills without a class. The effect on prediction was nil, and round 001 stays reproducible because its script pins the old behaviour.

## Round 003: the portable feature contract `meps-portable-v2` (O52–O54; O25 resolved)

Full results are in [`outcome-prediction-lab/rounds/003-portable-contract/report.md`](outcome-prediction-lab/rounds/003-portable-contract/report.md).

**`outcome_prediction/contract.py`** lists every model input with its FHIR source and how reliably a customer can supply it:
- **Tiers:** always, usually, rarely, claims-only, not portable.
- **Spending is out**: it's dropped, never imputed (O53).
- **MEPS-only codes are replaced by portable equivalents**:
  - CCSR condition groups and Multum drug classes → ICD-10-only codes;
  - CCSR body-system counts → ICD-10 chapter counts;
  - Multum drug-class counts → distinct-medicine counts.
- **Prescription fills and home-health days** are claims-only inputs.
- **Income is optional.** Models are trained with missingness augmentation and scored with income blanked, the way production will run them.

**Test panels**, 3 pre-registered looks:

| Target | Production contract | Round-001 research model |
|---|---|---|
| Non-obstetric admission | **0.795** | 0.795 |
| Any ER visit | **0.740** | 0.739 |
| High cost (with claims) | **0.834** | 0.850 |

All three stay calibrated. High cost needs claims data before a customer can validate it (O54).

## Focus decision (O55)

Phase 8 now focuses on **four predictions only**, unless the repo owner explicitly says otherwise:
1. admission through the ER;
2. hospital stay not related to pregnancy or childbirth;
3. any ER visit;
4. being a high-cost patient.

[`docs/phase8/prediction-targets.md`](docs/phase8/prediction-targets.md) records:
- how we got to this decision, step by step;
- where every **parked** target lives: any hospital stay, ER-visit count, spending, death, loss of insurance;
- the ideas considered and dropped, including "find similar patients".

**Next gap:** admission through the ER doesn't have a production-contract model yet.

## Not yet built (later iterations)

- Round 000.
- The person-scored scorecard criteria. These need a human to fill them in, passed with `--criteria`.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Your three conditions are now met on PR #71, and all 13 CI checks pass.

**1. A production model for admission through the ER.** The new `er-admit-v2` model (records-only, production contract) scores **0.785** AUROC on the test panels, against 0.754 for the simple baseline and 0.788 for the old research model. Its predictions are well calibrated (predicted 5.1% vs actual 4.9%). Adding claims data didn't help, so this model needs only clinical records. All four focus predictions now have a production model (O56).

**2. Fairness metrics for all four (O57).** There's a new `outcome-prediction-lab fairness` command, and it can't run until the look is logged in the holdout ledger. It breaks results down by race/ethnicity, insurance, sex and age band. Every model card now includes these figures. What it found:
- **Race/ethnicity:** predicted and actual rates agree closely for White, Hispanic and Black adults (ratios 0.96–1.12), and the gaps between men and women are small.
- **Uninsured adults are almost never flagged** (0–2%). The outcomes measure *use* of care, not *need*, and uninsured people use less care. Changing the model can't fix that, so outreach for this group shouldn't rely on the flag alone.
- **Calibration by group:** the models over-predict for younger and privately insured adults and slightly under-predict for adults on public insurance only and those 75+. Recalibration in Phase 8b should be checked group by group, not just overall.
- **Black adults, non-obstetric stay:** the model ranks risk less well for Black adults than for White adults (0.745 vs 0.787), though calibration is the same. This one should be monitored.
- **Asian adults:** there are too few events to draw any conclusion.

**3. The 65+ check for all four (O58).** I set the rule before running anything: a model trained only on adults 65+ would be adopted only if it beat the general model by at least 0.005 AUROC on that group. All four lost, by 0.020–0.038, so there's no separate 65+ model and no test-panel look was used on one. Performance for 65+ is lower than overall (0.70–0.78), as expected, because age alone does much of the work across all adults. The models still beat the simple baseline for 65+ by 0.04–0.15.

The test panels were used five times this round (one confirmation and four fairness checks), and all five were set in advance and logged in the ledger.

- **Code:** a new `fairness.py`, plus updates to `runs.py` (a config option that limits a model to an age group, and the fairness section on model cards), `cli.py` and the tests.

### M2 — Training, evaluation, artifact

**Short story:** Reproduce AUROC 0.769 / 0.708 and write the reports.

**Long story:** `model/train.py`, `model/evaluate.py`, `model/artifact.py`, implemented from
`prototype-baseline.md` §4.2–§4.3 and checked against §5.2 (O7). The artifact carries both
models (O18), a SHA-256 manifest (O17), the training score distribution (for percentiles), and
metadata stating that headline metrics come from the validation model, not the release model
(`design.md` §11 defect 5). `scikit-learn` pinned exactly (O12). Training and evaluation are
written as importable functions, not only CLIs — the lab (M3) calls them (O29).

**Deliverable:** Test AUROC in [0.760, 0.778] (GBM) and [0.700, 0.716] (comparison);
`metrics.json` + `model_report.md` covering FR-E1–E5; a tampered manifest is refused.

**Depends on:** M1.

**Verified (M2 built):** with `scikit-learn` 1.9.1 (the prototype's version; wheels confirmed
for Python 3.11 and 3.12), the reproduction is **exact to every reported digit**, not merely
within tolerance: GBM AUROC 0.769 [0.754, 0.786], comparison 0.708 [0.691, 0.725], AUPRC, Brier,
top-k, survey-weighted AUROC 0.780, all ten calibration deciles, all seven subgroups, the
permutation-importance ranking and the comparison coefficients (-4.047, 0.0280, 1.3055) — every
figure in `prototype-baseline.md` §5.2. Bootstrap CIs match because the shared generator is
consumed in the prototype's order. Release artifact `gbm-meps25-v1-950d8be12078` (ID derived from
the training table's checksum); a one-byte change to any file is refused before deserialisation.
`train` + `evaluate` take ~18 s. Tests: 63 pass with the MEPS cache; 48 pass and 15 self-skip
without it (CI).

                  "k6sum2", "phq22", "vpcs2", "vmcs2", "educyr"]
SURVEY_CATEGORICAL = ["empst1", "marryy1x", "hideg"]

def honest_frame(t: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Re-encode MEPS codes without hidden decisions (round 001, concept 4):
    refused / don't know / not ascertained / cannot compute (all negative codes) -> missing,
    never "no" or category 0; yes/no items -> 1/0; the raw diagnosis answers replace the
    prototype's "anything but yes is no" flags."""
    x = t.copy()
    for col in NUMERIC_BASE + CATEGORICAL + SURVEY_NUMERIC + SURVEY_CATEGORICAL:
        if col in x and col not in DX_FLAGS:
            x[col] = x[col].where(x[col] >= 0)
    for col in DX_FLAGS:
        raw = x[f"{col}_raw"]
        x[col] = np.select([raw == 1, raw == 2], [1.0, 0.0], default=np.nan)
    for col in COVERAGE + ["adlhlp1", "iadlhp1", "actlim1"]:
        x[col] = np.select([x[col] == 1, x[col] == 2], [1.0, 0.0], default=np.nan)
    return x

def fitted_path(round_id: str, name: str) -> Path:
    from outcome_prediction.settings import models_dir
    return models_dir() / f"lab-round-{round_id}" / f"{name}.joblib"


def fit_on_training_panels(round_id: str, name: str, frame: pd.DataFrame | None = None):
    cfg = load_config(config_path(round_id, name))
    df = lab_frame() if frame is None else frame
    rows = df.panel.isin(TRAIN_PANELS).to_numpy() & _in_population(df, cfg)
    y, _ = _targets(df[rows], cfg)
    return cfg, _factory(cfg)().fit(df[rows], y)


def confirm(round_id: str, name: str, frame: pd.DataFrame | None = None) -> dict:
    """The ONE path to the test panels: refuses unless the ledger already records this look."""
    holdout.require(round_id, name)
    df = lab_frame() if frame is None else frame
    cfg, model = fit_on_training_panels(round_id, name, df)
    test = df.panel.isin(TEST_PANELS).to_numpy() & _in_population(df, cfg)
    Xt = df[test]
    y, raw = _targets(Xt, cfg)
    proba = cfg["task"] == "binary"
    hook = _scoring_hook(cfg)
    Xs = hook(Xt) if hook else Xt
    pred = model.predict_proba(Xs)[:, 1] if proba else model.predict(Xs)
    result = {"config": cfg, "test": _metrics(cfg, y, pred, raw, Xt.agey1x.to_numpy() if proba else None),
              "provenance": _provenance()}
    if cfg.get("baseline_inputs"):
        train = df.panel.isin(TRAIN_PANELS).to_numpy() & _in_population(df, cfg)
        yb, _ = _targets(df[train], cfg)
        b = _baseline_factory(cfg["task"])().fit(_baseline_X(df[train], cfg["baseline_inputs"]), yb)
        Xb = _baseline_X(Xt, cfg["baseline_inputs"])
        pb = b.predict_proba(Xb)[:, 1] if proba else b.predict(Xb)
        result["test_baseline"] = _metrics(cfg, y, pb, raw, Xt.agey1x.to_numpy() if proba else None)
    path = fitted_path(round_id, name)
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    joblib.dump(model, path)
    result["fitted_model_sha256"] = hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
    (round_dir(round_id) / "runs" / f"{name}.confirm.json").write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2) + "\n")
    return result


# ── model card, scorecard, promotion ─────────────────────────────────────────────────

def _load(round_id, name, kind):
    p = round_dir(round_id) / "runs" / (f"{name}.confirm.json" if kind == "confirm" else f"{name}.json")
    return json.loads(p.read_text()) if p.exists() else None


def _fmt_metrics(m: dict | None) -> str:
    if not m:
        return "_not available_"
    keys = [k for k in ("auroc", "auprc", "brier", "top10_ppv", "top10_sensitivity", "auroc_65plus",
                        "spearman", "poisson_deviance", "r2_log", "top10_share_of_events",
                        "top10_share_of_spend") if k in m]
    return ", ".join(f"{k} {m[k]:.3f}" for k in keys) + f" (n = {m['n']:,})"


def _observability(label: str) -> str:
    from outcome_prediction.contract import LABEL_OBSERVABILITY
    return LABEL_OBSERVABILITY.get(label, "not assessed")


def _fairness_section(round_id: str, name: str) -> str:
    p = round_dir(round_id) / "fairness" / f"{name}.json"
    if not p.exists():
        return "## Subgroup fairness\n\n_Not yet assessed — run `outcome-prediction-lab fairness`._\n"
    rep = json.loads(p.read_text())
    lines = ["## Subgroup fairness (test panels)", "",
             f"Full tables: [`fairness/{name}.md`](../fairness/{name}.md). Widest gaps among groups with enough events:", "",
             "| Dimension | AUROC range | Calibration ratio range | Cases caught by the top-10% flag |", "|---|---|---|---|"]
    for dim, s in rep["summary"].items():
        lines.append(f"| {dim} | {s['auroc_range'][0]:.3f}–{s['auroc_range'][1]:.3f} | "
                     f"{s['calibration_ratio_range'][0]:.2f}–{s['calibration_ratio_range'][1]:.2f} | "
                     f"{s['share_of_cases_flagged_range'][0]:.0%}–{s['share_of_cases_flagged_range'][1]:.0%} |")
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"


def card(round_id: str, name: str) -> Path:
    """A model card in the spirit of TRIPOD+AI: intended use, data, outcome, inputs, performance
    (CV and, if confirmed, test), limitations — generated from the committed run records."""
    r, c = _load(round_id, name, "run"), _load(round_id, name, "confirm")
    if r is None:
        raise ConfigError(f"no run result for {name} — run it first")
    cfg = r["config"]
    cats, nums = FEATURE_SETS[cfg["features"]]
    text = ", ".join(cfg["text"]) if isinstance(cfg.get("text"), list) else (cfg.get("text") or "none")
    md = f"""# Model card — `{name}` (round {round_id})

{cfg.get("description", "")}

| | |
|---|---|
| **Intended use** | {"LEARNING ONLY — not for promotion (decisions.md O48)" if cfg.get("learning_only") else "Population-level planning aid for primary-care care management; not a diagnosis, not for emergencies"} |
| **Outcome** | `{cfg["label"]}` — {cfg.get("outcome_phrase", "see the round report")} (year 2 of a MEPS two-year panel) |
| **Population** | US civilian non-institutionalised adults (18+) in MEPS panels 21–27, observed in both years |
| **Training data** | Panels 21–25 (2016–2021); evaluation by leave-one-panel-out cross-validation |
| **Test data** | Panels 26–27 (2021–2023), scored once after a holdout-ledger entry |
| **Inputs** | {len(cats)} categorical + {len(nums)} numeric features (`{cfg["features"]}`); text representations: {text} |
| **Model** | `{cfg["model"]}`, task `{cfg["task"]}`, params {"round-001 tuned" if cfg.get("params") == "tuned" else (cfg.get("params") or "defaults")} |
| **Cross-validated performance** | {_fmt_metrics(r["cv"])} |
| **Cross-validated baseline** | {_fmt_metrics(r.get("cv_baseline"))} |
| **Test performance** | {_fmt_metrics(c["test"]) if c else "_not confirmed_"} |
| **Test baseline** | {_fmt_metrics(c.get("test_baseline")) if c else "_not confirmed_"} |
| **Feature contract** | {cfg["features"]}{" — production contract meps-portable-v2 (O52)" if cfg["features"].startswith("portable-v2") else " — research features, NOT the production contract"} |
| **Missing inputs** | trained with missingness augmentation on {", ".join(cfg.get("augment_missing") or {}) or "none"}; scored with {", ".join(cfg.get("simulate_missing_at_scoring") or []) or "nothing"} blanked, as production will |
| **Outcome observable by a customer** | {_observability(cfg["label"])} |
| **Data provenance** | manifest sha256 `{r["provenance"]["manifest_sha256"][:12]}…`, code `{(r["provenance"]["git_commit"] or "unknown")[:12]}` |

{_fairness_section(round_id, name)}
## Limitations

- Trained on MEPS **self-reported** survey data; customer records differ (codes, charges vs payments,
  missing income). Recalibrate and validate on customer data before any use (Phase 8b).
- Condition codes are 3-character ICD-10 and only for conditions linked to a year-1 medical event.
- Explanations describe what the model weighed, not causes.
- **Uplift / impactability is not assessable with MEPS** (no intervention data — O37): this model ranks
  risk, not who would benefit from outreach.
"""
    out = round_dir(round_id) / "cards" / f"{name}.md"
    out.parent.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    out.write_text(md)
    return out


CRITERION_NAMES = {"measurable_in_customer_data": "Measurable in customer data", "actionable": "Actionable",
                   "lead_time": "Lead time", "fhir_representability": "FHIR representability",
                   "regulatory_posture": "Regulatory posture"}
HUMAN_CRITERIA = {
    "measurable_in_customer_data": "Can a customer's own FHIR / claims data observe this outcome (needed to validate and recalibrate)?",
    "actionable": "What would a care manager do differently for a flagged patient?",
    "lead_time": "Is there time to act before the outcome happens?",
    "fhir_representability": "Probability -> RiskAssessment natively; count / cost needs a decision revisiting O3 (O35).",
    "regulatory_posture": "Does this change the FDA clinical-decision-support position?",
}


def scorecard(round_id: str, name: str, criteria: Path | None = None) -> Path:
    """The target scorecard (O36): ML criteria filled from the records; non-ML criteria from a
    person's JSON ({criterion: {"score": ..., "rationale": ...}}) — or marked as still owed."""
    r, c = _load(round_id, name, "run"), _load(round_id, name, "confirm")
    if r is None:
        raise ConfigError(f"no run result for {name}")
    human = json.loads(Path(criteria).read_text()) if criteria else {}
    cv, base = r["cv"], r.get("cv_baseline")
    m = c["test"] if c else cv
    lines = [f"# Target scorecard — `{r['config']['label']}` via `{name}` (round {round_id})", "",
             "| Criterion | Source | Assessment |", "|---|---|---|"]
    if "auroc" in m:
        lines += [f"| Discrimination | {'test' if c else 'CV'} | AUROC {m['auroc']:.3f}, AUPRC {m['auprc']:.3f}"
                  + (f" (baseline AUROC {base['auroc']:.3f}, CV)" if base else "") + " |",
                  f"| Calibration | {'test' if c else 'CV'} | Brier {m['brier']:.4f}; mean predicted {m['mean_pred']:.3f} vs rate {m['rate']:.3f} |",
                  f"| Base rate | data | {m['rate']:.1%} |",
                  f"| Worklist value | {'test' if c else 'CV'} | top 10%: {m['top10_ppv']:.0%} have the outcome; they hold {m['top10_sensitivity']:.0%} of all cases |",
                  f"| Adults 65+ | {'test' if c else 'CV'} | AUROC {m.get('auroc_65plus', float('nan')):.3f} |"]
    else:
        lines += [f"| Ranking | {'test' if c else 'CV'} | Spearman {m['spearman']:.3f} |"]
    for key, question in HUMAN_CRITERIA.items():
        entry = human.get(key)
        cell = (f"**{entry['score']}** — {entry['rationale']}" if entry
                else f"_TO BE SCORED BY A PERSON_ — {question}")
        lines.append(f"| {CRITERION_NAMES[key]} | person | {cell} |")
    lines.append("| Uplift / impactability | — | Not assessable with MEPS (no intervention data — O37) |")
    if r["config"].get("learning_only"):
        lines += ["", "**Learning-only target (O48): not eligible for promotion.**"]
    out = round_dir(round_id) / "scorecards" / f"{name}.md"
    out.parent.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    out.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
    return out


def promote(round_id: str, name: str, decision: str) -> Path:
    """Write the promotion record (O33) — only for a confirmed, carded, non-learning-only run whose
    promotion is backed by an existing decisions.md entry."""
    if not re.fullmatch(r"O\d+", decision):
        raise PromotionRefused(f"decision must look like O49, got {decision!r}")
    if f"| {decision} |" not in DECISIONS.read_text():
        raise PromotionRefused(f"{decision} is not in {DECISIONS} — record the decision first")
    r, c = _load(round_id, name, "run"), _load(round_id, name, "confirm")
    if c is None:
        raise PromotionRefused(f"{name} has no test-panel confirmation")
    if r["config"].get("learning_only"):
        raise PromotionRefused(f"{name} is a learning-only target (O48)")
    card_path = round_dir(round_id) / "cards" / f"{name}.md"
    if not card_path.exists():
        raise PromotionRefused(f"{name} has no model card — run `card` first")
    model = fitted_path(round_id, name)
    if hashlib.sha256(model.read_bytes()).hexdigest() != c["fitted_model_sha256"]:
        raise PromotionRefused(f"{model} does not match the model that was confirmed")
    record = {"round": round_id, "run": name, "decision": decision, "label": r["config"]["label"],
              "model_sha256": c["fitted_model_sha256"],
              "model_card_sha256": hashlib.sha256(card_path.read_bytes()).hexdigest(),
              "promoted_at": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="seconds")}
    out = model.with_suffix(".PROMOTION.json")
    out.write_text(json.dumps(record, indent=2) + "\n")
    return out

def _load(round_id, name, kind):
    p = round_dir(round_id) / "runs" / (f"{name}.confirm.json" if kind == "confirm" else f"{name}.json")
    return json.loads(p.read_text()) if p.exists() else None


def _fmt_metrics(m: dict | None) -> str:
    if not m:
        return "_not available_"
    keys = [k for k in ("auroc", "auprc", "brier", "top10_ppv", "top10_sensitivity", "auroc_65plus",
                        "spearman", "poisson_deviance", "r2_log", "top10_share_of_events",
                        "top10_share_of_spend") if k in m]
    return ", ".join(f"{k} {m[k]:.3f}" for k in keys) + f" (n = {m['n']:,})"


def _observability(label: str) -> str:
    from outcome_prediction.contract import LABEL_OBSERVABILITY
    return LABEL_OBSERVABILITY.get(label, "not assessed")


def _fairness_section(round_id: str, name: str) -> str:
    p = round_dir(round_id) / "fairness" / f"{name}.json"
    if not p.exists():
        return "## Subgroup fairness\n\n_Not yet assessed — run `outcome-prediction-lab fairness`._\n"
    rep = json.loads(p.read_text())
    lines = ["## Subgroup fairness (test panels)", "",
             f"Full tables: [`fairness/{name}.md`](../fairness/{name}.md). Widest gaps among groups with enough events:", "",
             "| Dimension | AUROC range | Calibration ratio range | Cases caught by the top-10% flag |", "|---|---|---|---|"]
    for dim, s in rep["summary"].items():
        lines.append(f"| {dim} | {s['auroc_range'][0]:.3f}–{s['auroc_range'][1]:.3f} | "
                     f"{s['calibration_ratio_range'][0]:.2f}–{s['calibration_ratio_range'][1]:.2f} | "
                     f"{s['share_of_cases_flagged_range'][0]:.0%}–{s['share_of_cases_flagged_range'][1]:.0%} |")
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"


def card(round_id: str, name: str) -> Path:
    """A model card in the spirit of TRIPOD+AI: intended use, data, outcome, inputs, performance
    (CV and, if confirmed, test), limitations — generated from the committed run records."""
    r, c = _load(round_id, name, "run"), _load(round_id, name, "confirm")
    if r is None:
        raise ConfigError(f"no run result for {name} — run it first")
    cfg = r["config"]
    cats, nums = FEATURE_SETS[cfg["features"]]
    text = ", ".join(cfg["text"]) if isinstance(cfg.get("text"), list) else (cfg.get("text") or "none")
    md = f"""# Model card — `{name}` (round {round_id})

{cfg.get("description", "")}

| | |
|---|---|
| **Intended use** | {"LEARNING ONLY — not for promotion (decisions.md O48)" if cfg.get("learning_only") else "Population-level planning aid for primary-care care management; not a diagnosis, not for emergencies"} |
| **Outcome** | `{cfg["label"]}` — {cfg.get("outcome_phrase", "see the round report")} (year 2 of a MEPS two-year panel) |
| **Population** | US civilian non-institutionalised adults (18+) in MEPS panels 21–27, observed in both years |
| **Training data** | Panels 21–25 (2016–2021); evaluation by leave-one-panel-out cross-validation |
| **Test data** | Panels 26–27 (2021–2023), scored once after a holdout-ledger entry |
| **Inputs** | {len(cats)} categorical + {len(nums)} numeric features (`{cfg["features"]}`); text representations: {text} |
| **Model** | `{cfg["model"]}`, task `{cfg["task"]}`, params {"round-001 tuned" if cfg.get("params") == "tuned" else (cfg.get("params") or "defaults")} |
| **Cross-validated performance** | {_fmt_metrics(r["cv"])} |
| **Cross-validated baseline** | {_fmt_metrics(r.get("cv_baseline"))} |
| **Test performance** | {_fmt_metrics(c["test"]) if c else "_not confirmed_"} |
| **Test baseline** | {_fmt_metrics(c.get("test_baseline")) if c else "_not confirmed_"} |
| **Feature contract** | {cfg["features"]}{" — production contract meps-portable-v2 (O52)" if cfg["features"].startswith("portable-v2") else " — research features, NOT the production contract"} |
| **Missing inputs** | trained with missingness augmentation on {", ".join(cfg.get("augment_missing") or {}) or "none"}; scored with {", ".join(cfg.get("simulate_missing_at_scoring") or []) or "nothing"} blanked, as production will |
| **Outcome observable by a customer** | {_observability(cfg["label"])} |
| **Data provenance** | manifest sha256 `{r["provenance"]["manifest_sha256"][:12]}…`, code `{(r["provenance"]["git_commit"] or "unknown")[:12]}` |

{_fairness_section(round_id, name)}
## Limitations

- Trained on MEPS **self-reported** survey data; customer records differ (codes, charges vs payments,
  missing income). Recalibrate and validate on customer data before any use (Phase 8b).
- Condition codes are 3-character ICD-10 and only for conditions linked to a year-1 medical event.
- Explanations describe what the model weighed, not causes.
- **Uplift / impactability is not assessable with MEPS** (no intervention data — O37): this model ranks
  risk, not who would benefit from outreach.
"""
    out = round_dir(round_id) / "cards" / f"{name}.md"
    out.parent.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    out.write_text(md)
    return out


CRITERION_NAMES = {"measurable_in_customer_data": "Measurable in customer data", "actionable": "Actionable",
                   "lead_time": "Lead time", "fhir_representability": "FHIR representability",
                   "regulatory_posture": "Regulatory posture"}
HUMAN_CRITERIA = {
    "measurable_in_customer_data": "Can a customer's own FHIR / claims data observe this outcome (needed to validate and recalibrate)?",
    "actionable": "What would a care manager do differently for a flagged patient?",
    "lead_time": "Is there time to act before the outcome happens?",
    "fhir_representability": "Probability -> RiskAssessment natively; count / cost needs a decision revisiting O3 (O35).",
    "regulatory_posture": "Does this change the FDA clinical-decision-support position?",
}


def scorecard(round_id: str, name: str, criteria: Path | None = None) -> Path:
    """The target scorecard (O36): ML criteria filled from the records; non-ML criteria from a
    person's JSON ({criterion: {"score": ..., "rationale": ...}}) — or marked as still owed."""
    r, c = _load(round_id, name, "run"), _load(round_id, name, "confirm")
    if r is None:
        raise ConfigError(f"no run result for {name}")
    human = json.loads(Path(criteria).read_text()) if criteria else {}
    cv, base = r["cv"], r.get("cv_baseline")
    m = c["test"] if c else cv
    lines = [f"# Target scorecard — `{r['config']['label']}` via `{name}` (round {round_id})", "",
             "| Criterion | Source | Assessment |", "|---|---|---|"]
    if "auroc" in m:
        lines += [f"| Discrimination | {'test' if c else 'CV'} | AUROC {m['auroc']:.3f}, AUPRC {m['auprc']:.3f}"
                  + (f" (baseline AUROC {base['auroc']:.3f}, CV)" if base else "") + " |",
                  f"| Calibration | {'test' if c else 'CV'} | Brier {m['brier']:.4f}; mean predicted {m['mean_pred']:.3f} vs rate {m['rate']:.3f} |",
                  f"| Base rate | data | {m['rate']:.1%} |",
                  f"| Worklist value | {'test' if c else 'CV'} | top 10%: {m['top10_ppv']:.0%} have the outcome; they hold {m['top10_sensitivity']:.0%} of all cases |",
                  f"| Adults 65+ | {'test' if c else 'CV'} | AUROC {m.get('auroc_65plus', float('nan')):.3f} |"]
    else:
        lines += [f"| Ranking | {'test' if c else 'CV'} | Spearman {m['spearman']:.3f} |"]
    for key, question in HUMAN_CRITERIA.items():
        entry = human.get(key)
        cell = (f"**{entry['score']}** — {entry['rationale']}" if entry
                else f"_TO BE SCORED BY A PERSON_ — {question}")
        lines.append(f"| {CRITERION_NAMES[key]} | person | {cell} |")
    lines.append("| Uplift / impactability | — | Not assessable with MEPS (no intervention data — O37) |")
    if r["config"].get("learning_only"):
        lines += ["", "**Learning-only target (O48): not eligible for promotion.**"]
    out = round_dir(round_id) / "scorecards" / f"{name}.md"
    out.parent.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    out.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
    return out


def promote(round_id: str, name: str, decision: str) -> Path:
    """Write the promotion record (O33) — only for a confirmed, carded, non-learning-only run whose
    promotion is backed by an existing decisions.md entry."""
    if not re.fullmatch(r"O\d+", decision):
        raise PromotionRefused(f"decision must look like O49, got {decision!r}")
    if f"| {decision} |" not in DECISIONS.read_text():
        raise PromotionRefused(f"{decision} is not in {DECISIONS} — record the decision first")
    r, c = _load(round_id, name, "run"), _load(round_id, name, "confirm")
    if c is None:
        raise PromotionRefused(f"{name} has no test-panel confirmation")
    if r["config"].get("learning_only"):
        raise PromotionRefused(f"{name} is a learning-only target (O48)")
    card_path = round_dir(round_id) / "cards" / f"{name}.md"
    if not card_path.exists():
        raise PromotionRefused(f"{name} has no model card — run `card` first")
    model = fitted_path(round_id, name)
    if hashlib.sha256(model.read_bytes()).hexdigest() != c["fitted_model_sha256"]:
        raise PromotionRefused(f"{model} does not match the model that was confirmed")
    record = {"round": round_id, "run": name, "decision": decision, "label": r["config"]["label"],
              "model_sha256": c["fitted_model_sha256"],
              "model_card_sha256": hashlib.sha256(card_path.read_bytes()).hexdigest(),
              "promoted_at": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="seconds")}
    out = model.with_suffix(".PROMOTION.json")
    out.write_text(json.dumps(record, indent=2) + "\n")
    return out

# Round 000 — reproduce M2's model through the lab

**Type:** tooling proof (milestone-plan M3, FR-X4). Run through the CLI. **Status:** see `report.md`.

Numbered 000 because it is what M3 was specified to start with; it was run after rounds 001–004,
once the lab could call the service's own fitting code (`"model": "meps25-v1"`, O29).

## Question

Does the lab, run through its CLI, reproduce M2's `meps25-v1` models — the service's gradient
boosting model and its age + prior-stay comparison model — **exactly**?

## Configs

- `meps25-v1` — the service's `fit_gbm` on `feature_matrix` (prototype inputs and encoding).
- `meps25-v1-comparison` — the service's `fit_comparison` on `comparison_matrix`.

Both read the lab table without the honest re-encoding (`runs.reference_frame`), because the
prototype's encoding is part of the `meps25-v1` contract.

## Pre-registered test-panel looks

`meps25-v1` and `meps25-v1-comparison`, once each. These re-score test panels whose results M2
already reported, so they reveal nothing new; they are logged anyway, like every look.

**Pass criterion:** test AUROC, AUPRC, Brier and mean predicted equal
`outcome-prediction-service/data/reports/metrics.json` (M2) to 1e-9, on the same 44,497 training and
11,863 test adults.
EOF
for n in meps25-v1 meps25-v1-comparison; do :; done; python3 - <<'EOF'
import json; from pathlib import Path
R = Path("outcome-prediction-lab/rounds/000-baseline-reproduction/configs")
base = {"label": "label_hosp_12m", "task": "binary", "features": "prototype",
        "outcome_phrase": "at least one inpatient discharge (the prototype's label; includes childbirth)"}
cfgs = {"meps25-v1": {**base, "model": "meps25-v1",
                      "description": "M2's reference gradient-boosting model, fitted by the service's own code."},
        "meps25-v1-comparison": {**base, "model": "meps25-v1-comparison",
                      "description": "M2's comparison model (age and any prior stay), fitted by the service's own code."}}
for n, c in cfgs.items():
    (R / f"{n}.json").write_text(json.dumps({"name": n, **c}, indent=2) + "\n")
EOF

ICD10CDX VALUEICD10CDX LABELUNWEIGHTED
-15CANNOT BE COMPUTED1
I50HEART FAILURE9
E11TYPE 2 DIABETES MELLITUS9
CCSR1X VALUECCSR1X LABELCCSR2X VALUECCSR2X LABEL

""" RX_HTML = """
Therapeutic Class CodeDefinition
-1inapplicable
215insulin

> 32 LSA dims t["tokens"] = [" ".join(rng.choice(vocab, 4)) for _ in range(len(t))] t["desc_text"] = t["tokens"].str.replace("icd", "condition ", regex=False) t["drug_names"] = "ASPIRIN | METFORMIN" t["admit_nonobstetric_y2"] = t["label_hosp_12m"] return t @pytest.fixture def lab(tmp_path, monkeypatch): rounds = tmp_path / "rounds" (rounds / "r1" / "configs").mkdir(parents=True) decisions = tmp_path / "decisions.md" decisions.write_text("| O99 | a decision | Accepted | x |\n") monkeypatch.setattr(runs, "ROUNDS", rounds) monkeypatch.setattr(runs, "DECISIONS", decisions) monkeypatch.setenv("OUTCOME_PREDICTION_MODELS_DIR", str(tmp_path / "models")) ledger = tmp_path / "ledger.md" monkeypatch.setattr(holdout, "LEDGER", ledger) monkeypatch.setattr(holdout.require, "__defaults__", (ledger,)) monkeypatch.setattr(holdout.record, "__defaults__", ((26, 27), ledger)) def write(name, **cfg): cfg = {"name": name, "label": "admit_nonobstetric_y2", "task": "binary", "features": "portable+knowledge", "model": "gbm", "params": {"max_iter": 30}, "baseline_inputs": ["agey1x", "ipdisy1"], **cfg} (rounds / "r1" / "configs" / f"{name}.json").write_text(json.dumps(cfg)) return write def test_configs_cannot_name_panels_or_splits(lab): lab("sneaky", test_panels=[26, 27]) with pytest.raises(runs.ConfigError, match="unknown keys"): runs.load_config(runs.config_path("r1", "sneaky")) def test_run_compare_confirm_card_scorecard_promote(lab, tmp_path): frame = _frame() lab("m", text=["lsa"]) def test_configs_may_request_augmentation_and_production_scoring(lab): lab("p", features="portable-v2", augment_missing={"povcaty1": 0.5}, simulate_missing_at_scoring=["povcaty1"]) cfg = runs.load_config(runs.config_path("r1", "p")) assert runs._scoring_hook(cfg)(pd.DataFrame({"povcaty1": [3.0]})).povcaty1.isna().all() # ── population filter and fairness (round 004) ─────────────────────────────────────── def test_population_filter_restricts_training_and_scoring(lab): frame = _frame() lab("old", population={"age_min": 65}) r = runs.run("r1", "old", frame=frame) assert r["cv"]["n"] == int(((frame.agey1x >= 65) & frame.panel.isin([21, 22, 23, 24, 25])).sum()) lab("bad", population={"income_min": 3}) with pytest.raises(runs.ConfigError, match="age_min"): runs.run("r1", "bad", frame=frame) def test_fairness_report_covers_groups_and_flags_small_ones():

# ── round 000: M2's models through the lab ───────────────────────────────────────────

def test_reference_model_is_the_services_own_fit(lab):
    from outcome_prediction.model import LABEL, feature_matrix, split_masks
    from outcome_prediction.model.fit import fit_validation
    from outcome_prediction.tests.conftest import synthetic_table
    table = synthetic_table(per_panel=160, seed=0)
    lab("ref", label=LABEL, features="prototype", model="meps25-v1", params=None, baseline_inputs=None)
    holdout.record("r1", "ref", "test")
    c = runs.confirm("r1", "ref", frame=table)
    _, test = split_masks(table)
    expected = fit_validation(table).gbm.predict_proba(feature_matrix(table)[test])[:, 1]
    from sklearn.metrics import roc_auc_score
    assert c["test"]["auroc"] == roc_auc_score(table[LABEL].to_numpy()[test], expected)
    assert c["test"]["mean_pred"] == pytest.approx(expected.mean(), abs=1e-12)


def test_reference_model_refuses_other_features(lab):
    lab("ref-bad", label="label_hosp_12m", features="portable-v2", model="meps25-v1")
    with pytest.raises(runs.ConfigError, match="M2's fixed model"):
        runs.load_config(runs.config_path("r1", "ref-bad"))
EOF

# Round 000 report — M2's model reproduced through the lab

**Status:** complete — **passed**. **Pre-registration:** [`README.md`](./README.md). **Run through the
CLI:** [`configs/`](./configs/), [`runs/`](./runs/). **Test-panel looks:** 2, pre-registered and logged
in [`../../holdout-ledger.md`](../../holdout-ledger.md); both re-score results M2 had already reported.

## 1. Result

The lab's `confirm` reproduces M2 (`outcome-prediction-service/data/reports/metrics.json`) **bit for
bit** on the same 44,497 training and 11,863 test adults:

| Model | Measure | M2 | Lab (round 000) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `meps25-v1` (gradient boosting) | AUROC | 0.769008189627725 | 0.769008189627725 |
| | AUPRC | 0.2646971976727336 | 0.2646971976727336 |
| | Brier | 0.07247803262282396 | 0.07247803262282396 |
| | Mean predicted | 0.09172567531071446 | 0.09172567531071446 |
| `meps25-v1-comparison` (age + prior stay) | AUROC | 0.7076200378839681 | 0.7076200378839681 |
| | AUPRC | 0.2253834619054936 | 0.2253834619054936 |
| | Brier | 0.0750866564313514 | 0.0750866564313514 |
| | Mean predicted | 0.09024741815655428 | 0.09024741815655428 |

It is exact because the lab doesn't re-implement the model: `"model": "meps25-v1"` calls the service's
own `fit_gbm` / `fit_comparison` and matrices (O29) on the lab table without honest re-encoding.

## 2. The lab's cross-validated numbers (panels 21–25, leave one panel out)

New information M2 couldn't give — M2 has a single train/test split:

| Model | CV AUROC | AUPRC | Brier | AUROC 65+ | Top-10% precision |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `meps25-v1` | 0.768 | 0.262 | 0.0702 | 0.699 | 29% |
| `meps25-v1-comparison` | 0.686 | 0.202 | 0.0734 | 0.647 | 25% |

Consistent with M2's test numbers (0.769 / 0.708): the gradient-boosting model generalises across
panels as it did to the later test panels. The comparison model does a little better on the test
panels than in CV (0.708 vs 0.686) — a two-input model is sensitive to panel-to-panel shifts in how
much prior stays predict.

## 3. What this proves about the tooling

- The CLI path (config → `run` → ledger → `confirm` → `card`) leaves numbers unchanged from the
  service's own path — so every round's results are comparable with the served model.
- The guards are covered by tests that show them refusing: configs naming panels or splits; `confirm`
  and `fairness` without a ledger entry; promotion without confirmation, card, matching checksum or
  decision; a `meps25-v1` config with any other features (`test_lab_tooling.py`).
- Model card for `meps25-v1`: [`cards/meps25-v1.md`](./cards/meps25-v1.md).

`meps25-v1` stays the **reference** model only (O55, `prediction-targets.md` §4): its label includes
childbirth (O47) and its inputs include non-portable spending (O52).
EOF

318:### M12 — First promotion into the service
319-
320-**Short story:** Exercise the promotion path end to end, once, so it's proven before anyone
321-relies on it.
322-
323-**Long story:** `promote.py` writes `PROMOTION.json` (O33, `design.md` §8); the service
324-starts refusing artifacts without it, and the `meps25-v1` artifact gets its retrofitted record.
325-Serve M11's candidate as a new contract/target version beside `meps25-v1`: FHIR extractor and
326-`to_contract.py` extended for its features, `RiskAssessment` outcome coding and window updated
327-for its target, the agent's narration checked against it, M9's acceptance case extended. If M10
328-chose a non-probability form, implement the representation O35 decided.
329-
330-**Deliverable:** Both versions servable; an unpromoted artifact is refused (tested); the e2e
331-suite passes for the new version.
332-
333-**Depends on:** M7 (service), M11 (candidate).
334-
335----
336-
337-### M13 — Versioned clinical code lists
338-
339-**Short story:** Replace description regexes with reviewed ICD-10-CM code lists.
340-
they apply. Round-3 items excluded or tested separately (FR-D7). Re-run the 18–44 sex check that
exposed the childbirth problem (7.4% vs 2.2%). Every serious candidate gets a full scorecard
(O36) — including measurability in FHIR/claims, actionability, FHIR representability (O35),
and the explicit uplift gap (O37). Confirmation on the test panels only for the named
finalists, through the ledger.

**Deliverable:** Round report with scorecards and model cards; O40 decided — which
outcome(s) and form(s) to take forward — as a new `decisions.md` entry; for any
non-probability form chosen, the O35 representation decision too.

**Depends on:** M3.

Still open: O23 (MEPS commercial use, a legal question), O24 (qualitative bands), O25
(non-portable features), O26 (FHIR vs claims as primary customer input), O27 (code-list
sign-off), O40 (which outcome(s) and form(s) to promote first — decided by M10's scorecards,
which also settles any-stay vs unplanned-stay as the headline label). Carried over unchanged
from the prototype's plan: which cloud hosts production (Phase 8b).

M3 is finished and closed, and PR #71 is updated with all 13 CI checks passing. The only blockers were your three decisions (the scorecard scores, which prediction to promote first, and closing M3), which you've answered.

**Round 000 (M3's original deliverable).** I ran M2's two models through the lab's command line, and the test results match M2's to every digit. That includes AUROC 0.769008189627725 for the main model and 0.7076200378839681 for the comparison model, plus AUPRC, Brier and mean predicted. It matches exactly because the lab now calls the service's own fitting code instead of a copy. Two new config options do this, and they only accept M2's fixed inputs. Cross-validation, which M2 never had, gives 0.768 and 0.686. Both models now have a model card. Re-scoring the test panels counted as two more logged looks, though M2 had already reported those results.

**Scorecards.** The scores a person has to give are now recorded for all four focus models in each round's `criteria/` folder, marked as drafted by me and adopted by you. The main point they carry: high cost is scored "finance, not need" and must never be used alone to decide who gets care.

- **O59** settles O40: the first prediction to promote is the hospital stay not related to pregnancy or childbirth (`nonobstetric-v2`).
- **O60** closes M3. The lab stays available for new rounds whenever you want one.

I did not run `promote`. That step belongs to M12, which builds the promotion record and makes the service refuse models that haven't been promoted.

I also fixed a small bug: `confirm` failed if the round had no `runs/` folder yet.

# ML concepts used in Phase 8 so far

I've grouped them roughly the way a data science / ML course usually orders them. Each one says what it is, where we used it and what happened. I don't know the exact MIT syllabus, so match these to your modules by topic name.

## 1. Framing the problem: supervised classification
- **Binary classification with probabilities.** Every focus prediction answers "how likely is this adult to have event X in the next 12 months?" We needed a calibrated probability, not just a yes/no, because the output goes into a FHIR `RiskAssessment`.
- **Choosing the label (target engineering).** This was the most important lesson of the phase. The prototype predicted "any hospital stay", and it turned out that much of what the model learned was simply that pregnant people give birth. Changing the label to non-obstetric stays gave a model that means what a care manager means.
  - *Review topic:* problem formulation; the label is a modelling choice.
- **Other prediction forms we tried:**
  - *count regression* for the number of ER visits (Poisson);
  - *cost regression* on log-spending;
  - *binarising at a threshold* for "high cost" (the top 10%).

## 2. Models
- **Logistic regression.** Used as the interpretable baseline: the "simple rule" each model must beat, such as age plus prior stays.
- **Gradient-boosted trees (HistGradientBoosting).** Our workhorse: an ensemble of shallow trees, each correcting the previous ones' errors.
- **Random forest.** Bagged trees, compared against boosting. It was about the same.
- **A single decision tree.** Fully readable, but it lost about 0.056 AUROC. This is the classic accuracy-versus-interpretability trade-off.
- **Hyperparameter tuning.** We tuned learning rate, tree size, minimum leaf size and regularisation by cross-validation. The gain was small, a reminder that defaults are often close.
- **Monotonic constraints.** We built in domain knowledge, for example "more prior stays should never lower risk". There was no accuracy cost, and the model became more trustworthy.

## 3. Feature engineering and representation
- **Missing values, handled honestly.** "Refused" or "don't know" became *missing*, not "no". Trees can learn from the fact that a value is missing.
- **Missingness augmentation.** During training we randomly hid income for half the rows, so the model learned to work without it. Production rarely has income, and this kept predictions calibrated.
  - *Review topics:* missing-data mechanisms (MCAR, MAR, MNAR); train/serve skew.
- **Drop, don't impute, for inputs production never has.** An imputed value is just a function of the other inputs, so it adds no information, only miscalibration risk.
- **Text as features:**
  - **Bag-of-words and TF-IDF** on diagnosis and drug codes treated as "documents".
  - **LSA (truncated SVD)** compressed the sparse TF-IDF matrix into 32 dense dimensions. This is dimensionality reduction, closely related to PCA.
  - **Character n-grams** handled messy drug names: they recognise "METFORMIN HCL" as close to "metformin".
  - *Review topics:* NLP basics; SVD/PCA; dimensionality reduction.
- **Autoencoders and denoising autoencoders.** Small neural networks that learn a compressed code from the input. They matched LSA but cost about 8× more, so the simpler method won.
  - *Review topics:* neural networks; representation learning; unsupervised learning.
- **Expert-derived features.** Charlson and Elixhauser comorbidity scores and the hospital frailty score gave a small gain. This is domain knowledge as features.

## 4. Evaluation methodology (where most of the rigour went)
- **Train/test split by time.** We trained on earlier survey panels and tested on later ones, which simulates deploying a model into the future.
- **Grouped cross-validation (leave-one-panel-out).** Each fold holds out a whole panel, never random rows, which avoids leakage between related records.
- **Holdout discipline.** The test set is looked at only after the look is pre-registered and logged. This guards against overfitting to the test set, sometimes called the garden of forking paths.
- **Discrimination metrics:**
  - **AUROC:** ranking quality.
  - **AUPRC:** more informative when events are rare.
  - **Top-10% precision and sensitivity:** the practical "worklist" view.
- **Calibration metrics:** **Brier score**, mean predicted versus observed rate, and calibration by decile.
- **Uncertainty:** **bootstrap confidence intervals** and a **paired bootstrap** to compare two models on the same people.
- **Baselines.** Every model must beat a simple rule. Lift over the baseline matters more than raw AUROC.

## 5. Explainability
- **Permutation importance.** Global: how much worse the model gets when a feature is scrambled.
- **SHAP values (TreeExplainer).** Local: how much each feature pushed one patient's prediction up or down. These feed the plain-language, per-patient explanations.
- **Surrogate models.** A simple tree trained to imitate the complex model.
- **The marginal-versus-conditional caveat.** An explanation describes what the model weighed, not what causes the outcome.
  - *Review topics:* interpretability; correlation versus causation.

## 6. Fairness, subgroups and robustness
- **Subgroup evaluation** by race/ethnicity, insurance, sex and age. For each group we looked at:
  - AUROC with confidence intervals;
  - calibration ratio;
  - equal opportunity: the share of each group's cases the flag catches.
- **Label bias.** Outcomes that measure *use* of care rather than *need* under-flag people with poor access, such as the uninsured. This is the well-known Obermeyer et al. (2019) result about cost-based risk scores.
- **Specialist versus general model.** A 65+-only model lost to the general one. More data, even from younger adults, beat a narrower population.
- **Distribution shift and portability.** Models were retrained using only inputs a real customer's records can supply. This touches on domain adaptation and train/serve skew.

## 7. Causal limits
- **Prediction is not uplift.** Our models rank risk; they can't say who would *benefit* from outreach. That needs intervention data, which this survey (MEPS) doesn't have.
  - *Review topics:* causal inference; treatment effects.

## 8. MLOps and reproducibility
- **Pipelines that refit inside each cross-validation fold.** No preprocessing leaks from test folds into training.
- **Experiment tracking** with MLflow.
- **Pinned data with checksums**, and model cards in the spirit of the TRIPOD+AI reporting guideline.
- **Exact reproduction of a baseline.** Round 000 matched M2 to every digit before anything was changed.

---

- **Fairness and the 65+ check:** round 004 in [outcome-prediction-lab/rounds/004-focus-four-readiness/report.md](outcome-prediction-lab/rounds/004-focus-four-readiness/report.md).
