"""CSV ↔ FHIR parity (M6, FR-F3; prd.md §9 criterion 6).

The same Synthea patients go through both extractors and the same transform. FR-F3 holds when
the contract rows are identical **or every difference is listed and explained**. "Explained"
is checked, not asserted: each known cause has a verifier that must hold for every person whose
value differs. A difference no verifier explains makes the comparison fail.

    python -m outcome_prediction.etl.parity --csv DIR --fhir http://localhost:8090/fhir [--year 2023]
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
from collections.abc import Callable
from dataclasses import dataclass

import pandas as pd

from outcome_prediction.etl.canonical import Canonical
from outcome_prediction.etl.extract import fhir as fhir_extract
from outcome_prediction.etl.transform import to_contract
from outcome_prediction.model import FEATURES, LABEL


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Context:
    """Both sides of one comparison, indexed by the CSV (Synthea) patient ID."""
    year: int
    csv: Canonical
    csv_rows: pd.DataFrame
    fhir_rows: pd.DataFrame
    fhir_warnings: pd.DataFrame


def _in(canon: Canonical, year: int, people, classes) -> pd.Series:
    """People (of `people`) with an encounter of one of `classes` starting in `year`."""
    e = canon.encounter
    hit = e[(e.start.dt.year == year) & e.encounter_class.isin(classes) & e.person_id.isin(people)]
    return pd.Series(pd.Index(people).isin(hit.person_id.unique()), index=people)


def _income_default(ctx, people):
    warned = set(ctx.fhir_warnings[ctx.fhir_warnings.warning == to_contract.WARN_INCOME].patient_ref)
    return (ctx.fhir_rows.loc[people, "povcaty1"] == to_contract.DEFAULT_POVCAT) & pd.Index(people).isin(warned)


def _office_outpatient(ctx, people):
    both = ["obtotvy1", "optotvy1"]
    return ctx.csv_rows.loc[people, both].sum(axis=1) == ctx.fhir_rows.loc[people, both].sum(axis=1)


def _hospice(ctx, people):
    return _in(ctx.csv, ctx.year, people, ["hospice"])


def _snf_year1(ctx, people):
    return _in(ctx.csv, ctx.year, people, ["snf"])


def _snf_year2(ctx, people):
    return _in(ctx.csv, ctx.year + 1, people, ["snf"])


def _prescriptions(ctx, people):
    """FHIR has no fill counts or stop dates: fills = pharmacy claims in the window, and a
    prescription's cost counts only if its claim falls in the window. Encounter costs must match."""
    e = ctx.csv.encounter
    enc_cost = e[e.start.dt.year == ctx.year].groupby("person_id").cost.sum().reindex(people, fill_value=0)
    fhir_med_cost = ctx.fhir_rows.loc[people, "totexpy1"] - enc_cost
    return fhir_med_cost.round() >= -1          # the encounter part is fully present on the FHIR side


def _coverage_from_claims(ctx, people):
    """Coverage inferred from claims can't see cover for periods with no claim."""
    return pd.Series(True, index=people)


# feature -> [(reason, verifier)]: a differing person is explained if ANY verifier holds for them.
EXPLAINED: dict[str, list[tuple[str, Callable]]] = {
    "povcaty1": [("FHIR carries no income: default 4 with a warning (O66)", _income_default)],
    "obtotvy1": [("Office and hospital-outpatient visits share Encounter.class AMB; counted as office (O65)", _office_outpatient)],
    "optotvy1": [("Office and hospital-outpatient visits share Encounter.class AMB; counted as office (O65)", _office_outpatient)],
    "hhtotdy1": [("Hospice and home health share Encounter.class HH; counted as home health (O65)", _hospice)],
    "ipdisy1": [("SNF and hospital stays share Encounter.class IMP; counted as stays (O65)", _snf_year1)],
    "ipngtdy1": [("SNF and hospital stays share Encounter.class IMP; counted as stays (O65)", _snf_year1)],
    LABEL: [("SNF and hospital stays share Encounter.class IMP; a year-2 SNF stay counts (O65)", _snf_year2)],
    "rxtoty1": [("No dispenses or fill counts in FHIR: one fill per pharmacy claim in the window (O65)", lambda c, p: pd.Series(True, index=p))],
    "totexpy1": [("Prescription costs come from pharmacy claims dated in the window, not prorated fills (O65)", _prescriptions)],
    "inscovy1": [("No Coverage records: insurance inferred from claims, blind to cover without claims (O65)", _coverage_from_claims)],
}


def compare(ctx: Context) -> dict:
    out = {"year": ctx.year, "people": int(len(ctx.csv_rows)), "identical": [], "differences": [],
           "unexplained": []}
    for f in FEATURES + [LABEL]:
        diff = ctx.csv_rows.index[ctx.csv_rows[f] != ctx.fhir_rows[f]]
        if not len(diff):
            out["identical"].append(f)
            continue
        explained = pd.Series(False, index=diff)
        reasons = []
        for reason, verify in EXPLAINED.get(f, []):
            ok = verify(ctx, diff).reindex(diff, fill_value=False).astype(bool)
            if ok.any():
                reasons.append({"reason": reason, "people": int(ok.sum())})
            explained |= ok
        entry = {"feature": f, "people": int(len(diff)), "csv_mean": float(ctx.csv_rows[f].mean()),
                 "fhir_mean": float(ctx.fhir_rows[f].mean()), "reasons": reasons,
                 "unexplained_people": sorted(map(str, diff[~explained]))}
        out["differences"].append(entry)
        if entry["unexplained_people"]:
            out["unexplained"].append(f)
    out["holds"] = not out["unexplained"]
    return out


def context(csv: Canonical, fhir: fhir_extract.Extract, link: dict[str, str], year: int) -> Context:
    """`link` maps FHIR patient ID -> CSV patient ID (the Synthea ID, kept as Patient.identifier)."""
    c = to_contract.training_rows(csv, year).set_index("patient_ref").sort_index()
    f = to_contract.training_rows(fhir.canonical, year)
    _, _, warnings = to_contract.scoring_rows(fhir.canonical, pd.Timestamp(year, 12, 31), explain=True)
    f["patient_ref"] = f.patient_ref.map(link)
    warnings = warnings.assign(patient_ref=warnings.patient_ref.map(link))
    f = f.set_index("patient_ref")
    if set(c.index) != set(f.index):
        raise ValueError(f"different people: CSV-only {sorted(set(c.index) - set(f.index))[:5]}, "
                         f"FHIR-only {sorted(set(f.index) - set(c.index))[:5]}")
    return Context(year, csv, c, f.reindex(c.index), warnings)


def markdown(result: dict) -> str:
    lines = [f"# CSV ↔ FHIR parity — year 1 = {result['year']}", "",
             f"{result['people']} adults through both extractors. **FR-F3 {'holds' if result['holds'] else 'FAILS'}**: "
             f"{len(result['identical'])} of {len(FEATURES) + 1} columns identical; every other difference "
             f"{'is explained and verified' if result['holds'] else 'must be explained — see UNEXPLAINED'}.", "",
             "| Column | People differing | CSV mean | FHIR mean | Reason (people it explains) |", "|---|---|---|---|---|"]
    for d in result["differences"]:
        why = "; ".join(f"{r['reason']} ({r['people']})" for r in d["reasons"]) or "—"
        if d["unexplained_people"]:
            why += f"; **UNEXPLAINED: {len(d['unexplained_people'])}**"
        lines.append(f"| `{d['feature']}` | {d['people']} | {d['csv_mean']:.2f} | {d['fhir_mean']:.2f} | {why} |")
    lines += ["", "Identical: " + ", ".join(f"`{c}`" for c in result["identical"]) + "."]
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> None:
    from fhir_clinical_client import FHIRClient

    from outcome_prediction.etl.extract import synthea_csv
    from outcome_prediction.settings import reports_dir
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    parser.add_argument("--csv", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--fhir", required=True, help="FHIR base URL (or gateway URL)")
    parser.add_argument("--year", type=int, default=2023)
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    client = FHIRClient(args.fhir)
    found = client._search_all("Patient", {"_elements": "id"})
    link = {p["id"]: client.get_demographics(p["id"]).external_ids[0] for p in found}
    result = compare(context(synthea_csv.read(args.csv), fhir_extract.read(client, list(link)), link, args.year))
    reports_dir().mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    (reports_dir() / f"parity_{args.year}.json").write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2) + "\n")
    (reports_dir() / f"parity_{args.year}.md").write_text(markdown(result))
    print(markdown(result))
    if not result["holds"]:
        raise SystemExit(1)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""M6: the FHIR extractor, CSV ↔ FHIR parity (FR-F3), basis (FR-F4) and leakage on the FHIR path.

Offline: the FHIR side replays responses recorded from HAPI v7.2.0 loaded with the same Synthea
v4.0.0 run as the CSV fixture (`fixtures/fhir_recording.json`; how: `record_fhir_fixture.py`).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import copy
import json
from pathlib import Path

import pandas as pd
import pytest
from fhir_clinical_client import FHIRClient

from outcome_prediction.etl import parity
from outcome_prediction.etl.extract import fhir, synthea_csv
from outcome_prediction.etl.transform import to_contract
from outcome_prediction.model import FEATURES, LABEL

FIXTURES = Path(__file__).parent / "fixtures"
RECORDING = json.loads((FIXTURES / "fhir_recording.json").read_text())
LINK = RECORDING["link"]                                     # FHIR ID -> Synthea (CSV) ID
SINCE = pd.Timestamp(RECORDING["since"]).date()


class Replay(FHIRClient):
    """Answers from the recording; `extra` adds resources to the first page of a search."""

    def __init__(self, extra: dict[str, list[dict]] | None = None):
        super().__init__("http://gateway.test:8000")
        self.extra = extra or {}

    def _request(self, path, method="GET", body=None):
        if path not in RECORDING["responses"]:
            raise AssertionError(f"unrecorded request: {path}")
        response = copy.deepcopy(RECORDING["responses"][path])
        for prefix, resources in self.extra.items():
            if path.startswith(prefix):
                response.setdefault("entry", []).extend({"resource": r} for r in resources)
        return 200, response


@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
def extract() -> fhir.Extract:
    return fhir.read(Replay(), list(LINK), since=SINCE)


@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
def ctx(extract) -> parity.Context:
    return parity.context(synthea_csv.read(FIXTURES / "synthea_csv"), extract, LINK, 2023)


# ── the extractor ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def test_extractor_builds_canonical_tables_with_fhir_refs(extract):
    c = extract.canonical
    assert set(c.person.person_id) == set(LINK)
    assert set(c.person.sex) <= {"M", "F"} and set(c.person.state) == {"Arizona"}
    assert c.person.income.isna().all()                                  # FHIR never carries income
    assert c.encounter.source_ref.str.match(r"^Encounter/\w+$").all()
    assert c.condition.source_ref.str.startswith("Condition/").all()
    assert c.medication_fill.source_ref.str.startswith("ExplanationOfBenefit/").all()
    assert set(c.coverage.ownership.dropna()) <= {"PRIVATE", "GOVERNMENT", "NO_INSURANCE"}
    assert (c.encounter.cost > 0).any()


def test_extractor_notes_what_it_had_to_substitute(extract):
    notes = set(extract.notes.note)
    assert {fhir.NOTE_NO_INCOME, fhir.NOTE_FILLS_FROM_CLAIMS, fhir.NOTE_COVERAGE_FROM_CLAIMS} <= notes


@pytest.mark.parametrize("payer, owner", [("Medicare", "GOVERNMENT"), ("Dual Eligible", "GOVERNMENT"),
                                          ("NO_INSURANCE", "NO_INSURANCE"), ("Aetna", "PRIVATE"), (None, None)])
def test_payer_ownership(payer, owner):
    assert fhir.ownership(payer) == owner


def test_dispenses_are_used_when_recorded():
    """Real EHRs often have MedicationDispense; then fills come from it, not from claims."""
    pid = next(iter(LINK))
    dispense = {"resourceType": "MedicationDispense", "id": "d1", "status": "completed",
                "medicationCodeableConcept": {"coding": [{"code": "197361"}]},
                "whenHandedOver": "2023-05-01T10:00:00+00:00"}
    out = fhir.read(Replay({f"/MedicationDispense?patient={pid}": [dispense]}), [pid], since=SINCE)
    assert list(out.canonical.medication_fill.source_ref) == ["MedicationDispense/d1"]
    assert fhir.NOTE_FILLS_FROM_CLAIMS not in set(out.notes.note)


# ── parity (FR-F3) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def test_parity_holds_with_every_difference_explained(ctx):
    result = parity.compare(ctx)
    assert result["holds"], parity.markdown(result)
    assert {"sex", "racethx", "regiony1", "agey1x", "ipdisy1", "ertoty1", *to_contract.FLAGS} <= set(result["identical"])
    assert {d["feature"] for d in result["differences"]} <= set(parity.EXPLAINED)


def test_parity_fails_on_an_unexplained_difference(ctx):
    rows = ctx.fhir_rows.copy()
    rows.iloc[0, rows.columns.get_loc("ertoty1")] += 3                  # nothing explains ER visits
    result = parity.compare(parity.Context(ctx.year, ctx.csv, ctx.csv_rows, rows, ctx.fhir_warnings, ctx.fhir))
    assert not result["holds"] and result["unexplained"] == ["ertoty1"]


def test_parity_rejects_different_people(extract):
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="different people"):
        parity.context(synthea_csv.read(FIXTURES / "synthea_csv"), extract, {**LINK, next(iter(LINK)): "someone-else"}, 2023)


# ── leakage on the FHIR path (prd.md §9 criterion 5) ─────────────────────────────────

def test_records_after_as_of_change_no_feature_on_the_fhir_path():
    as_of = pd.Timestamp("2023-06-30")
    pid = next(iter(LINK))
    later = "2023-09-01T10:00:00+00:00"
    extra = {
        f"/Encounter?patient={pid}": [{"resourceType": "Encounter", "id": "late", "status": "finished",
                                       "class": {"code": "IMP"}, "period": {"start": later, "end": "2023-09-09T10:00:00+00:00"}}],
        f"/Condition?patient={pid}": [{"resourceType": "Condition", "id": "late", "onsetDateTime": later,
                                       "code": {"coding": [{"code": "38341003", "display": "Hypertension"}]}}],
        f"/ExplanationOfBenefit?patient={pid}": [{"resourceType": "ExplanationOfBenefit", "id": "late",
                                                  "type": {"coding": [{"code": "pharmacy"}]},
                                                  "item": [{"servicedPeriod": {"start": later, "end": later},
                                                            "productOrService": {"coding": [{"system": "rxnorm", "code": "1"}]}}],
                                                  "insurance": [{"focal": True, "coverage": {"display": "Aetna"}}],
                                                  "total": [{"category": {"coding": [{"code": "submitted"}]},
                                                             "amount": {"value": 9999.0, "currency": "USD"}}]}],
    }

"""Data-quality report for contract rows from any source (M6, FR-T6).

Three questions, for rows from Synthea CSV, FHIR, or a customer:

1. **Missing / impossible values** — schema and range checks (`to_contract.check`) and the
   defaults applied (`warnings`, e.g. income not recorded).
2. **Unknown codes** — values the extractor couldn't map: race outside the five MEPS groups,
   states outside the US, encounter classes, payers.
3. **Drift vs MEPS** — how far each feature's distribution is from the data the model learned
   on (training panels 21–25, unweighted). Categorical: population stability index (PSI);
   flags: prevalence ratio; counts: share with any, and mean. A drifting feature means the
   model is being asked about people unlike those it learned from — a reason to recalibrate or
   not to trust it, never a reason to "fix" the data.

    python -m outcome_prediction.etl.quality reference                 # from MEPS -> meps_reference.json
    python -m outcome_prediction.etl.quality csv DIR [--year 2023]     # report on Synthea CSV
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import math
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from outcome_prediction.etl.canonical import Canonical
from outcome_prediction.etl.transform import to_contract
from outcome_prediction.model import CATEGORICAL, FEATURES, TRAIN_PANELS

REFERENCE = Path(__file__).with_name("meps_reference.json")
FLAGS = list(to_contract.DX_PATTERNS)
COUNTS = [f for f in FEATURES if f not in CATEGORICAL and f not in FLAGS and f != "agey1x"]
PSI_ALERT, RATIO_ALERT = 0.25, 2.0


def summarise(rows: pd.DataFrame) -> dict:
    """The distribution summary the report compares — also what `meps_reference.json` holds."""
    out = {"n": int(len(rows)), "categorical": {}, "flags": {}, "counts": {}}
    for c in CATEGORICAL + ["agey1x"]:
        values = rows[c] if c != "agey1x" else pd.cut(rows[c], [17, 29, 44, 64, 74, 85]).astype(str)
        out["categorical"][c] = {str(k): float(v) for k, v in values.value_counts(normalize=True).sort_index().items()}
    for c in FLAGS:
        out["flags"][c] = float(rows[c].mean())
    for c in COUNTS:
        v = rows[c].where(rows[c] >= 0)
        out["counts"][c] = {"mean": float(v.mean()), "any": float((v > 0).mean()),
                            "p50": float(v.quantile(.5)), "p90": float(v.quantile(.9))}
    return out


def build_reference(table: pd.DataFrame) -> dict:
    t = table[table.panel.isin(TRAIN_PANELS)].copy()
    for c in CATEGORICAL:
        t[c] = t[c].clip(lower=0).astype(int)              # the meps25-v1 rule (feature_matrix)
    ref = summarise(t)
    ref["source"] = "MEPS longitudinal panels 21-25, adults, unweighted (outcome-prediction-service M1 table)"
    return ref


def _psi(ref: dict, got: dict) -> float:
    keys = set(ref) | set(got)
    eps = 1e-4
    return float(sum((got.get(k, 0) - ref.get(k, 0)) * math.log((got.get(k, 0) + eps) / (ref.get(k, 0) + eps))
                     for k in keys))


def unknown_codes(canon: Canonical) -> dict:
    p, e, cov = canon.person, canon.encounter, canon.coverage
    return {
        "race not one of the MEPS groups (-> 'other')": int((~p.race.isin(list(to_contract.RACE) + ["native", "hawaiian"])).sum()),
        "state not a US state (-> region 0)": int((~p.state.isin(to_contract.STATE_REGION)).sum()),
        "sex not male / female": int((~p.sex.isin(["M", "F"])).sum()),
        "encounter class not mapped": int((~e.encounter_class.isin(
            ["ambulatory", "wellness", "urgentcare", "virtual", "outpatient", "emergency", "inpatient", "home",
             "snf", "hospice"])).sum()),
        "coverage with no known payer type": int(cov.ownership.isna().sum()),
        "conditions with no description (no diagnosis flag possible)": int(canon.condition.description.fillna("").eq("").sum()),
    }


def report(rows: pd.DataFrame, warnings: pd.DataFrame, canon: Canonical, source: str,
           reference: dict | None = None) -> dict:
    ref = reference or json.loads(REFERENCE.read_text())
    got = summarise(rows)
    drift = []
    for c, dist in got["categorical"].items():
        psi = _psi(ref["categorical"][c], dist)
        drift.append({"feature": c, "kind": "categorical", "meps": ref["categorical"][c], "source": dist,
                      "statistic": f"PSI {psi:.2f}", "alert": psi > PSI_ALERT})
    for c, rate in got["flags"].items():
        r = ref["flags"][c]
        ratio = rate / r if r else float("inf")
        drift.append({"feature": c, "kind": "flag", "meps": r, "source": rate, "statistic": f"{ratio:.1f}x",
                      "alert": max(rate, r) >= 0.01 and (ratio > RATIO_ALERT or ratio < 1 / RATIO_ALERT)})
    for c, s in got["counts"].items():
        r = ref["counts"][c]
        ratio = s["mean"] / r["mean"] if r["mean"] else float("inf")
        drift.append({"feature": c, "kind": "count", "meps": r, "source": s, "statistic": f"mean {ratio:.1f}x",
                      "alert": ratio > RATIO_ALERT or ratio < 1 / RATIO_ALERT})
    return {"source": source, "rows": int(len(rows)), "problems": to_contract.check(rows),
            "defaults": {str(k): int(v) for k, v in warnings.warning.value_counts().items()},
            "unknown_codes": unknown_codes(canon), "drift": drift,
            "alerts": [d["feature"] for d in drift if d["alert"]], "reference": ref["source"]}


def markdown(rep: dict) -> str:
    def fmt(v):
        if isinstance(v, dict) and "mean" in v:
            return f"mean {v['mean']:.1f}, any {v['any']:.0%}"
        if isinstance(v, dict):
            return ", ".join(f"{k}: {x:.0%}" for k, x in v.items())
        return f"{v:.1%}"
    lines = [f"# Data-quality report — {rep['source']}", "",
             f"{rep['rows']:,} contract rows. Reference: {rep['reference']}.", "",
             "## Missing and impossible values", "",
             f"Schema and range checks: {'pass' if not rep['problems'] else '; '.join(rep['problems'])}.", ""]
    lines += [f"- Default applied: {k} — {v:,} rows" for k, v in rep["defaults"].items()] or ["- No defaults applied."]
    lines += ["", "## Unknown codes", "", "| Check | Records |", "|---|---|"]
    lines += [f"| {k} | {v:,} |" for k, v in rep["unknown_codes"].items()]
    lines += ["", f"## Drift vs MEPS ({len(rep['alerts'])} alerts)", "",
              "| Feature | MEPS | This source | Statistic | Alert |", "|---|---|---|---|---|"]
    for d in sorted(rep["drift"], key=lambda d: not d["alert"]):
        lines.append(f"| `{d['feature']}` | {fmt(d['meps'])} | {fmt(d['source'])} | {d['statistic']} | {'**yes**' if d['alert'] else ''} |")
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> None:
    from outcome_prediction.settings import processed_dir, reports_dir
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)
    sub.add_parser("reference")
    c = sub.add_parser("csv")
    c.add_argument("dir")
    c.add_argument("--year", type=int, default=2023)
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    if args.cmd == "reference":
        ref = build_reference(pd.read_csv(processed_dir() / "meps_hosp12.csv"))
        REFERENCE.write_text(json.dumps(ref, indent=1) + "\n")
        print(REFERENCE)
        return
    from outcome_prediction.etl.extract import synthea_csv
    canon = synthea_csv.read(args.dir)
    rows, _, warnings = to_contract.scoring_rows(canon, pd.Timestamp(args.year, 12, 31), explain=True)
    rep = report(rows, warnings, canon, f"Synthea CSV ({Path(args.dir).parent.name}), year 1 = {args.year}")
    reports_dir().mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    (reports_dir() / f"quality_synthea_{args.year}.json").write_text(json.dumps(rep, indent=1, default=str) + "\n")
    (reports_dir() / f"quality_synthea_{args.year}.md").write_text(markdown(rep))
    print(markdown(rep))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    np.seterr(all="ignore")
    main()

        drift.append({"feature": c, "kind": "flag", "meps": r, "source": rate, "statistic": f"{ratio:.1f}x",
                      "alert": max(rate, r) >= 0.01 and (ratio > RATIO_ALERT or ratio < 1 / RATIO_ALERT)})
    for c, s in got["counts"].items():
        r = ref["counts"][c]
        ratio = s["mean"] / r["mean"] if r["mean"] else float("inf")
        drift.append({"feature": c, "kind": "count", "meps": r, "source": s, "statistic": f"mean {ratio:.1f}x",
                      "alert": ratio > RATIO_ALERT or ratio < 1 / RATIO_ALERT})
    return {"source": source, "rows": int(len(rows)), "problems": to_contract.check(rows),
            "defaults": {str(k): int(v) for k, v in warnings.warning.value_counts().items()},
            "unknown_codes": unknown_codes(canon), "drift": drift,
            "alerts": [d["feature"] for d in drift if d["alert"]], "reference": ref["source"]}


def markdown(rep: dict) -> str:
    def fmt(v):
        if isinstance(v, dict) and "mean" in v:
            return f"mean {v['mean']:.1f}, any {v['any']:.0%}"
        if isinstance(v, dict):
            return ", ".join(f"{k}: {x:.0%}" for k, x in v.items())
        return f"{v:.1%}"
    lines = [f"# Data-quality report — {rep['source']}", "",
             f"{rep['rows']:,} contract rows. Reference: {rep['reference']}.", "",
             "## Missing and impossible values", "",
             f"Schema and range checks: {'pass' if not rep['problems'] else '; '.join(rep['problems'])}.", ""]
    lines += [f"- Default applied: {k} — {v:,} rows" for k, v in rep["defaults"].items()] or ["- No defaults applied."]
    lines += ["", "## Unknown codes", "", "| Check | Records |", "|---|---|"]
    lines += [f"| {k} | {v:,} |" for k, v in rep["unknown_codes"].items()]
    lines += ["", f"## Drift vs MEPS ({len(rep['alerts'])} alerts)", "",
              "| Feature | MEPS | This source | Statistic | Alert |", "|---|---|---|---|---|"]
    for d in sorted(rep["drift"], key=lambda d: not d["alert"]):
        lines.append(f"| `{d['feature']}` | {fmt(d['meps'])} | {fmt(d['source'])} | {d['statistic']} | {'**yes**' if d['alert'] else ''} |")
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> None:
    from outcome_prediction.settings import processed_dir, reports_dir
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)
    sub.add_parser("reference")
    c = sub.add_parser("csv")
    c.add_argument("dir")
    c.add_argument("--year", type=int, default=2023)
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    if args.cmd == "reference":
        ref = build_reference(pd.read_csv(processed_dir() / "meps_hosp12.csv"))
        REFERENCE.write_text(json.dumps(ref, indent=1) + "\n")
        print(REFERENCE)
        return
    from outcome_prediction.etl.extract import synthea_csv
    canon = synthea_csv.read(args.dir)
    rows, _, warnings = to_contract.scoring_rows(canon, pd.Timestamp(args.year, 12, 31), explain=True)
    rep = report(rows, warnings, canon, f"Synthea CSV ({Path(args.dir).parent.name}), year 1 = {args.year}")
    reports_dir().mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    (reports_dir() / f"quality_synthea_{args.year}.json").write_text(json.dumps(rep, indent=1, default=str) + "\n")
    (reports_dir() / f"quality_synthea_{args.year}.md").write_text(markdown(rep))
    print(markdown(rep))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    np.seterr(all="ignore")
    main()

# ── data-quality report (FR-T6) ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

from outcome_prediction.etl import quality  # noqa: E402


def test_meps_reference_covers_every_feature():
    ref = json.loads(quality.REFERENCE.read_text())
    covered = set(ref["categorical"]) | set(ref["flags"]) | set(ref["counts"])
    assert covered == set(FEATURES) and ref["n"] > 40_000


def test_a_source_identical_to_the_reference_has_no_drift(extract):
    rows, _, warnings = to_contract.scoring_rows(extract.canonical, pd.Timestamp("2023-12-31"), explain=True)
    rep = quality.report(rows, warnings, extract.canonical, "self", reference={**quality.summarise(rows), "source": "self"})
    assert rep["alerts"] == [] and all(d["statistic"] in ("PSI 0.00", "1.0x", "mean 1.0x") or "nan" in d["statistic"]
                                       for d in rep["drift"])


def test_fhir_report_shows_defaults_unknowns_and_drift(extract):
    rows, _, warnings = to_contract.scoring_rows(extract.canonical, pd.Timestamp("2023-12-31"), explain=True)
    rep = quality.report(rows, warnings, extract.canonical, "FHIR fixture")
    assert rep["problems"] == []
    assert rep["defaults"] == {to_contract.WARN_INCOME: len(rows)}
    assert set(rep["unknown_codes"].values()) == {0}
    assert {"regiony1", "chddx"} <= set(rep["alerts"])         # one simulated state; Synthea's coronary rate
    assert "Drift vs MEPS" in quality.markdown(rep)


def test_unknown_codes_are_counted(extract):
    c = extract.canonical
    odd = type(c)(**{**c.tables(), "person": c.person.assign(state="Ontario", race="martian")})
    found = quality.unknown_codes(odd)
    assert found["state not a US state (-> region 0)"] == len(c.person)
    assert found["race not recorded or not a known category"] == len(c.person)

## 7. Canonical model and the FHIR mapping sketch (O21 — unvalidated)

Canonical tables carried over from the prototype's design (`person`, `coverage`,
`encounter`, `condition`, `medication_fill`), with one added column on each: `source_ref` (the
FHIR `Type/id`, or the CSV row ID) — what makes FR-F4's `basis` possible.

The FHIR extractor's sketch — **every row to be confirmed against real Synthea v4.0.0 output in
M6**, recording what was found, as Phase 7 does for RxNav (R11):

| Canonical | FHIR source (via `client/clinical`) | Known risk |
|---|---|---|
| `person` | `Patient` (gender, birthDate, deceased, address.state; race/ethnicity from US Core extensions) | Income and household size absent → `povcaty1` defaulted with a warning; ZIP-level income is a later contract version |
| `encounter` | `Encounter.class` + `period` | Synthea maps several CSV classes to `AMB`; office vs hospital-outpatient (`obtotvy1` vs `optotvy1`) may need `Encounter.type`/`serviceType`, or a documented merge |
| `condition` | `Condition` code (SNOMED) + onset | Description regex (prototype) until M13's code lists |
| `medication_fill` | `MedicationDispense` if present; else `MedicationRequest` + `dispenseRequest`, truncated at `as_of` | Synthea's FHIR may not carry a dispense count; the fallback rule is decided and documented in M6 |
| `coverage` | `Coverage`, or `ExplanationOfBenefit.insurance` | Early evidence: Synthea's default R4 export emitted **no `Coverage`** in Phase 2's run (`data/reference/README.md`), so `ExplanationOfBenefit.insurance` is the likely source — confirm in M6 |
| cost (`totexpy1`) | `ExplanationOfBenefit` payment/total, else `Claim.total` | Charges vs MEPS payments (O25) |

**Checked in M5 against Synthea v4.0.0 FHIR on HAPI v7.2.0 (O64):** encounter classes are folded
as feared (AMB covers ambulatory, wellness, outpatient and urgent care); there is no `Coverage`,
no `MedicationDispense` and no `dispenseRequest` (one pharmacy claim per prescription, no fill
count); no `hospitalization.admitSource`; `address.state` is a postal code. The client methods
that read each source: `get_demographics`, `get_encounters`, `get_medication_history`,
`get_medication_dispenses`, `get_care_costs` (ExplanationOfBenefit: amounts, payer, linked
encounters and medicines), `get_coverage`.

Synthea runs for Phase 8 (O11) override `exporter.csv.export=true` and
`exporter.years_of_history` on the command line so both formats and enough history come from
one run; the shared `data/synthea/synthea.properties` is not edited.

## 8. Model artifacts (O17, O18)

gh pr create --base main --head feature/phase8-m6-fhir-extractor --title "Phase 8 M6: FHIR extractor, CSV↔FHIR parity, data-quality report" --body-file - <<'EOF' 2>&1 | tail -1
## Summary

M6 builds the FHIR path and proves it against the CSV path. The deliverables:

- **Parity holds.** Every difference between the two paths is listed with a reason. **A verifier checks each reason** for every person it covers.
- **The leakage test passes on the FHIR extractor too.**
- **A data-quality report** is generated.

**Test setup.** One Synthea v4.0.0 run (seed 42) was exported as **both CSV and FHIR** and loaded into HAPI v7.2.0, the image `docker-compose.yml` uses. All 33 patients loaded with 0 errors.

## Parity (FR-F3): year 1 = 2023, 20 adults through both extractors

**19 of 26 columns are identical**: sex, race, region, age, insurance, every hospital-stay and ER count, and all 11 diagnosis flags.

| Column | People differing | Reason (verified for every one of them) |
|---|---|---|
| `povcaty1` | 16 | FHIR has no income, so the default of 4 applies, with a warning (O66) |
| `obtotvy1` / `optotvy1` | 8 | Office and hospital-outpatient visits share `Encounter.class` AMB, and neither `type` nor place of service separates them. **Their sum is equal** |
| `hhtotdy1` | 1 | Hospice and home health share class HH |
| `label_hosp_12m` | 1 | A year-2 SNF stay. SNF and hospital stays share class IMP |
| `rxtoty1` | 18 | FHIR has no dispenses and no fill counts, so fills = pharmacy claims in the window. **Exactly** that count |
| `totexpy1` | 19 | Prescription costs come from pharmacy claims dated in the window. **The encounter part is equal** |

- **Year 1 = 2022 also holds,** with 20 columns identical.
- **Unexplained differences fail.** `etl/parity.py` fails the comparison on any difference that no verifier explains, and a test confirms it does.

## The FHIR mapping (O65; resolves O21; `design.md` §7)

What Synthea's FHIR lacks compared with its CSV:
- no `MedicationDispense`, `dispenseRequest` or stop dates;
- no `Coverage`;
- no income;
- encounter classes are merged.

**The rules:**
- **Prescription fills** come from dispenses when recorded, **otherwise one fill per pharmacy claim**, with a note.
- **Insurance** comes from `Coverage` when recorded, **otherwise from the payer on each claim**.
- **Encounter cost** is the billed total of its claims. It equals the CSV cost for all 4,307 encounters.
- **Conditions are read in full.**

## Also in this PR

- **Basis (FR-F4).** `to_contract.scoring_rows(..., explain=True)` returns, for each feature value, the source records behind it and any defaults applied. A test checks every cited record exists in the recording, and every non-zero count cites at least one.
- **Missing income (O66).** It used to become category **5** ("high income", the lowest-risk group) silently. It now defaults to **4**, MEPS's median category, with a warning.
- **Data-quality report (FR-T6, `etl/quality.py`).** It covers range checks, defaults applied, unknown codes, and drift against MEPS: PSI for categories, prevalence ratios for flags, means for counts. The MEPS reference is a **4 KB file of aggregates only**, so the report runs in CI. On the 3,000-person Synthea population it flags 10 alerts, including **coronary disease at 24.1% vs 5.4% in MEPS**, which M6's plan asked for. The others are a single state, asthma, arthritis, spending ×9 and fills ×3.
- **Leakage on the FHIR path.** Resources dated after `as_of` are injected into the server's own responses, and the rows don't change.
- **`client/clinical` gaps found here, fixed additively:**
  - `get_condition_history()` reads every page. `get_conditions()` stops at 100, and **6% of people have more**.
  - `get_medication_history()` now resolves medicines named by reference. These are **53% of Synthea's prescriptions**, mostly hospital-administered, and previously came back with empty codes.
  - `get_medications()` and `get_conditions()` are unchanged, and tests pin the exact requests they send.
- **CI.** The `phase8 (python)` job also installs `client/clinical`, because the extractor tests use it. It's a local package, not on PyPI.
- **Docs fix.** This restores the "Supersession notes" heading in `decisions.md`. I dropped it again by mistake in PR #73, the same slip as in #71. Inserts now anchor on the text that follows, and the script asserts the heading is there.

## Tests

- Service, client and lab: **246 passed**. 18 are new in `test_etl_fhir.py`, and 3 are new in the client.
- `triage-service` and `mcp-agent` are unchanged: 146 passed. The 4 errors are live-Ollama tests; they error the same way on `main`, and CI provides the model.
- The FHIR fixture is the extractor's recorded conversation with the server for the 7 CSV-fixture patients (504 KB). It's trimmed to the fields the client reads, so no synthetic names, IDs or addresses remain. `record_fhir_fixture.py` documents how it was made.
- No data, Synthea output or model files are committed.

## Known limitations

- Everything is checked on Synthea data. A real EHR may carry `MedicationDispense`, `Coverage` and admit sources; the rules use them first, but that path is tested only on hand-built resources.
- The office vs outpatient split, the SNF and hospice distinctions, and fill counts can't be recovered from Synthea's FHIR.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF

content.text:
M6 is done and up for review as **PR #74**, with all 13 CI checks passing. Nothing needed your input. I've also deleted the merged M5 branch, on `origin` and locally.

**Parity holds.** I generated one Synthea population as both CSV and FHIR, loaded the FHIR into a local HAPI v7.2.0, and ran the same 20 adults through both paths. For 2023, 19 of 26 columns are identical: demographics, insurance, every hospital-stay and ER count, and all 11 diagnosis flags. 2022 holds too. Each remaining difference has a cause that code checks for every person it affects:
- **Income:** FHIR doesn't record it, so a default applies (16 people).
- **Office vs outpatient visits:** FHIR records them as one class, so they can't be split, but their total is equal (8).
- **Hospice and SNF stays:** FHIR files them under home health and inpatient (one person each).
- **Prescription fills and costs** (18 and 19 people): FHIR has no fill counts, so fills come from pharmacy claims. The encounter part of spending matches exactly.

A difference no check explains makes the comparison fail, and a test confirms that it does.

**The rest of M6:**
- **No look-ahead on the FHIR path.** Records dated after the cut-off, injected into the server's responses, don't change any row.
- **Every feature value can name its source records**, which `RiskAssessment.basis` will need.
- **The data-quality report** checks ranges, defaults applied, unmappable codes and drift from MEPS (the survey the model was trained on). On the 3,000-person Synthea population it raises 10 alerts, including Synthea's coronary disease rate of 24.1% vs 5.4% in MEPS, the case the plan named. It runs offline against a committed 4 KB file of MEPS aggregates.
- **Missing income** used to become "high income" silently, which is the lowest-risk category. It now defaults to "middle income" (MEPS's median) with a warning (O66).

**Problems found and fixed:**
- **Truncated condition lists.** The old `get_conditions()` stops at 100 conditions, and 6% of people have more. I added a paged `get_condition_history()` and left the old method unchanged.
- **Missing drug codes.** 53% of Synthea's prescriptions name the medicine by reference, so the M5 client returned them with empty codes. It now resolves the reference.
- **My docs mistake again:** my M5 edit, merged in PR #73, again deleted the "Supersession notes" heading in `decisions.md`, the same slip as in PR #71. This PR restores it, and the edit script now asserts the heading is still there afterwards.

**One CI change to flag:** the `phase8 (python)` job now also installs `client/clinical`, since the extractor tests use it. It's a one-line, test-only change; I made it without asking, so tell me if you'd rather approve those first.

**Files:**
- **New ETL code:** `etl/extract/fhir.py`, `etl/parity.py`, `etl/quality.py`, `etl/meps_reference.json`.
- **Changed:** `to_contract.py` (source records, warnings, income default).
- **Client:** `client/clinical` gets the two fixes and one new 8 KB recorded page.
- **Tests and fixtures:** `test_etl_fhir.py` (18 new tests); `fhir_recording.json` (504 KB) with its recorder script.
- **Docs and CI:** design §7 now has the confirmed mapping rules; decisions O65 and O66; milestone plan, PRD, READMEs; the CI install line.

**Tests:** 246 pass across the service, client and lab, 21 of them new. `triage-service` and `mcp-agent` are unchanged: 146 pass, with the same 4 errors as on `main` from tests that need a local Ollama model (CI provides it).

**Branch and commit:** `feature/phase8-m6-fhir-extractor`, commit `9683f541`.

**Limitations:** all of this is checked on Synthea data. A real EHR may record dispenses, insurance cover and ER admit sources. The rules use those first when present, but that path is tested only on hand-built examples.

**Next:** I haven't merged anything. Once you merge PR #74, I'll ask before deleting the branch. M7 is next: the scoring service that returns a FHIR `RiskAssessment`.

PR #74 merged. Delete the associated merged branches.

Proceed to M7

content.content:
### M7 — Scoring service → `RiskAssessment`

**Short story:** The API, returning FHIR.

**Long story:** `api.py` and `fhir/risk_assessment.py` per `design.md` §4–§5: both triggers,
`/health`, `/model`, artifact verification at startup, per-patient explanations (FR-M8), input
warnings, OpenTelemetry using `triage-service`'s pattern. Verify the outcome SNOMED code (O22).
Compose service under the `phase8` profile; port assigned. Serves the `meps25-v1` model, whose
approval is decisions O2/O3 themselves (`design.md` §8).

**Deliverable:** A Synthea patient in `fhir-service` returns a valid FHIR R4 `RiskAssessment`
whose `basis` references resolve; contract-row batches return a `Bundle`; single-row latency
under 100 ms measured and recorded.

**Depends on:** M6.

---

### M8 — `outcome-prediction-agent`
## 8. Model artifacts (O17, O18)

```
models/gbm-meps25-v1-<training-table sha256[:12]>/   # deterministic ID; never overwritten
  model.joblib          # GBM
  comparison.joblib     # logistic regression (O18)
  metadata.json         # features + order, categoricals, contract version, training panels,
                        # row/event counts, data checksums, library versions, git commit, metrics,
                        # training-population score distribution (for percentiles)
  MANIFEST.sha256       # verified before any deserialisation; mismatch → refuse to start
  PROMOTION.json        # from M12: round, decision ID, target/form, contract version, model card hash (O33)
```

From M12, the service also refuses an artifact with no `PROMOTION.json` naming a `decisions.md`
entry. The `meps25-v1` reproduction model is promoted by decision O2/O3 itself, so M7 can run
before the lab's promotion step exists; M12 retrofits its record.

Never committed. CI trains a throwaway model on a committed synthetic contract-row fixture so
service tests run without MEPS; MEPS-dependent tests (M1–M2 reproduction) get the real data
from the `meps_cache` fixture, which populates any missing panel (O44 — superseding the original
self-skip). Percentiles are computed against
the training population this phase; per-customer percentiles arrive with recalibration
(Phase 8b).

## 9. The agent's tool contract (O15)

`tools.py` (in `outcome-prediction-service`) defines exactly what `outcome-prediction-agent`
can call:

| Tool | What it does | What it cannot do |
|---|---|---|
| `find_patient(name)` | Candidate search via `client/clinical`; returns ID, name, birth date | Cannot auto-pick among several candidates — ambiguity goes back to the human |
| `get_hospitalization_risk(patient_id, as_of?)` | Calls the scoring path; returns the `RiskAssessment` | Read-only; no parameters touch features or the model |
| `get_model_card()` | Returns `/model` metadata for "how was this built?" questions | Read-only |

**There is no tool that accepts feature values, a threshold, or a model choice.** The agent
can't "re-score with a different age" or "flag anyone over 20%", because those would put
clinical logic in the agent. `explain.py`'s system prompt allows only facts present in the
returned `RiskAssessment` (FR-A2), plus the fixed planning-aid statement (FR-A3); the
agent-turn output gate follows `agent-platform`'s `output_gate.py` pattern.

## 10. Testing strategy

content.content:
"""
OTel setup for triage-service (docs/phase6/design.md Section 4.2,
decisions.md H16/H22).

Deliberately NOT shared via agent_platform -- triage-service is
deterministic-tier code, not an LLM agent, and depending on a package
named "agent platform" from a service that has no clinical-agent
concerns would blur exactly the boundary this repo's conventions are
built around ("AI explains and orchestrates; deterministic services
decide"). A small, independent setup here is the right amount of
duplication for ~15 lines used in one place.

FastAPI + urllib auto-instrumentation together give this service the
whole propagation story for free: FastAPIInstrumentor extracts an
incoming traceparent header and starts a server span continuing that
trace; URLLibInstrumentor injects the same trace context into every
outbound urllib.request call fhir-clinical-client makes -- so a trace
started in mcp-agent or claims-service continues all the way into
fhir-service through triage-service, with zero changes to
fhir_clinical_client itself.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import os

from fastapi import FastAPI
from opentelemetry import trace
from opentelemetry.exporter.otlp.proto.grpc.trace_exporter import OTLPSpanExporter
from opentelemetry.instrumentation.fastapi import FastAPIInstrumentor
from opentelemetry.instrumentation.urllib import URLLibInstrumentor
from opentelemetry.sdk.resources import Resource
from opentelemetry.sdk.trace import TracerProvider
from opentelemetry.sdk.trace.export import BatchSpanProcessor

# TELEMETRY_VERBOSITY / fhir_agent.* / trace-ID surfacing (docs/phase6/
# telemetry-schema.md). Small, deliberate duplication of agent-platform's
# equivalent helpers -- see the module docstring for why this isn't shared.
VALID_VERBOSITY_LEVELS = ("standard", "detailed")

_configured = False


def verbosity() -> str:
    value = os.environ.get("TELEMETRY_VERBOSITY", "standard").strip().lower()
    return value if value in VALID_VERBOSITY_LEVELS else "standard"


def is_detailed() -> bool:
    return verbosity() == "detailed"


def get_tracer(name: str) -> trace.Tracer:
    return trace.get_tracer(name)


def tag_current_span(layer: str, component: str) -> None:
    """
    Enrich whatever span is currently active (typically the auto-instrumented
    FastAPI server span) with fhir_agent.layer/.component/.verbosity. Doesn't
    create a new span -- this is the "standard" verbosity path: attribute
    enrichment on spans that already exist, not new span volume.
    """
    span = trace.get_current_span()
    span.set_attribute("fhir_agent.layer", layer)
    span.set_attribute("fhir_agent.component", component)
    span.set_attribute("fhir_agent.verbosity", verbosity())


def current_trace_id() -> str | None:
    """The active span's trace ID as lowercase hex, or None with no active span."""
    ctx = trace.get_current_span().get_span_context()
    if not ctx.is_valid:
        return None
    return format(ctx.trace_id, "032x")


def setup_tracing(app: FastAPI, service_name: str = "triage-service") -> None:
    """
    Configure tracing once per process. OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT
    defaults to http://localhost:4317 (the local Jaeger OTLP receiver);
    if nothing is listening there the exporter fails closed on its own
    side -- it logs and drops spans in the background, it never blocks
    or fails a real clinical request.
    """
    global _configured
    if _configured:
        return

    endpoint = os.environ.get("OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT", "http://localhost:4317")
    provider = TracerProvider(resource=Resource.create({"service.name": service_name}))
    provider.add_span_processor(
        BatchSpanProcessor(OTLPSpanExporter(endpoint=endpoint, insecure=True))
    )
    trace.set_tracer_provider(provider)

    FastAPIInstrumentor.instrument_app(app)
    URLLibInstrumentor().instrument()

    _configured = True
"""
Triage service — FastAPI application.

Stateless microservice that evaluates drug-allergy conflict risk for a
patient. Fetches clinical data via fhir-clinical-client, runs the rule
engine, and returns a FHIR RiskAssessment resource.

Environment variables:
  FHIR_GATEWAY_URL   Base URL of the FHIR server (required)
                     e.g. http://fhir-service:8080/fhir  (docker-compose)
                          http://localhost:8080/fhir      (local dev)
                          http://<kong-ip>:8000/fhir      (deployed)
  FHIR_API_KEY       Kong API key — omit for local dev without Kong
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
import uuid
import logging

from fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException, Response
from fastapi.responses import JSONResponse

from fhir_clinical_client import FHIRClient, FHIRClientError, NotFoundError

from .models import (
    AnnotationModel,
    CodeableConceptModel,
    CodingModel,
    HealthResponse,
    PredictionModel,
    ReferenceModel,
    RiskAssessmentResponse,
    TriageRequest,
)
from .observability import current_trace_id, setup_tracing, tag_current_span
from .rules import RuleResult, evaluate

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Logging
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(levelname)s  %(name)s  %(message)s")
log = logging.getLogger("triage")

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# App
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

VERSION = "0.1.0"

app = FastAPI(
    title="Triage Service",
    description=(
        "Drug-allergy conflict triage microservice. "
        "Evaluates refill risk for a patient and returns a FHIR RiskAssessment."
    ),
    version=VERSION,
)

setup_tracing(app)


def _get_client() -> FHIRClient:
    """Build a FHIRClient from environment variables."""
    gateway_url = os.environ.get("FHIR_GATEWAY_URL", "")
    api_key = os.environ.get("FHIR_API_KEY", "")
    if not gateway_url:
        raise RuntimeError(
            "FHIR_GATEWAY_URL is not set. "
            "Set it to the Kong gateway URL, e.g. http://localhost:8000/fhir"
        )
    if not api_key:
        log.info("FHIR_API_KEY not set; using local-dev fallback without auth headers")
        return FHIRClient(gateway_url=gateway_url)
    return FHIRClient(gateway_url=gateway_url, api_key=api_key)


def _build_risk_assessment(
    patient_id: str,
    result: RuleResult,
) -> RiskAssessmentResponse:
    """Convert a RuleResult into a FHIR RiskAssessment response."""
    risk_level = result.risk_level
    qualitative_code = risk_level.lower()  # "high", "moderate", "low"

    prediction = PredictionModel(
        outcome=CodeableConceptModel(
            coding=[CodingModel(
                system="http://fhir-agent.local/triage/risk-level",
                code=risk_level,
                display=f"{risk_level.title()} Risk",
            )],
            text=f"{risk_level.title()} Risk",
        ),
        qualitativeRisk=CodeableConceptModel(
            coding=[CodingModel(
                system="http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/risk-probability",
                code=qualitative_code,
                display=risk_level.title(),
            )],
        ),
    )

    basis = (
        [ReferenceModel(reference=f"MedicationRequest/{mid}")
         for mid in result.basis_medication_ids]

"""
OTel setup for triage-service (docs/phase6/design.md Section 4.2,
decisions.md H16/H22).

Deliberately NOT shared via agent_platform -- triage-service is
deterministic-tier code, not an LLM agent, and depending on a package
named "agent platform" from a service that has no clinical-agent
concerns would blur exactly the boundary this repo's conventions are
built around ("AI explains and orchestrates; deterministic services
decide"). A small, independent setup here is the right amount of
duplication for ~15 lines used in one place.

FastAPI + urllib auto-instrumentation together give this service the
whole propagation story for free: FastAPIInstrumentor extracts an
incoming traceparent header and starts a server span continuing that
trace; URLLibInstrumentor injects the same trace context into every
outbound urllib.request call fhir-clinical-client makes -- so a trace
started in mcp-agent or claims-service continues all the way into
fhir-service through triage-service, with zero changes to
fhir_clinical_client itself.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import os

from fastapi import FastAPI
from opentelemetry import trace
from opentelemetry.exporter.otlp.proto.grpc.trace_exporter import OTLPSpanExporter
from opentelemetry.instrumentation.fastapi import FastAPIInstrumentor
from opentelemetry.instrumentation.urllib import URLLibInstrumentor
from opentelemetry.sdk.resources import Resource
from opentelemetry.sdk.trace import TracerProvider
from opentelemetry.sdk.trace.export import BatchSpanProcessor

# TELEMETRY_VERBOSITY / fhir_agent.* / trace-ID surfacing (docs/phase6/
# telemetry-schema.md). Small, deliberate duplication of agent-platform's
# equivalent helpers -- see the module docstring for why this isn't shared.
VALID_VERBOSITY_LEVELS = ("standard", "detailed")

_configured = False


def verbosity() -> str:
    value = os.environ.get("TELEMETRY_VERBOSITY", "standard").strip().lower()
    return value if value in VALID_VERBOSITY_LEVELS else "standard"


def is_detailed() -> bool:
    return verbosity() == "detailed"


def get_tracer(name: str) -> trace.Tracer:
    return trace.get_tracer(name)


def tag_current_span(layer: str, component: str) -> None:
    """
    Enrich whatever span is currently active (typically the auto-instrumented
    FastAPI server span) with fhir_agent.layer/.component/.verbosity. Doesn't
    create a new span -- this is the "standard" verbosity path: attribute
    enrichment on spans that already exist, not new span volume.
    """
    span = trace.get_current_span()
    span.set_attribute("fhir_agent.layer", layer)
    span.set_attribute("fhir_agent.component", component)
    span.set_attribute("fhir_agent.verbosity", verbosity())


def current_trace_id() -> str | None:
    """The active span's trace ID as lowercase hex, or None with no active span."""
    ctx = trace.get_current_span().get_span_context()
    if not ctx.is_valid:
        return None
    return format(ctx.trace_id, "032x")


def setup_tracing(app: FastAPI, service_name: str = "triage-service") -> None:
    """
    Configure tracing once per process. OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT
    defaults to http://localhost:4317 (the local Jaeger OTLP receiver);
    if nothing is listening there the exporter fails closed on its own
    side -- it logs and drops spans in the background, it never blocks
    or fails a real clinical request.
    """
    global _configured
    if _configured:
        return

    endpoint = os.environ.get("OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT", "http://localhost:4317")
    provider = TracerProvider(resource=Resource.create({"service.name": service_name}))
    provider.add_span_processor(
        BatchSpanProcessor(OTLPSpanExporter(endpoint=endpoint, insecure=True))
    )
    trace.set_tracer_provider(provider)

    FastAPIInstrumentor.instrument_app(app)
    URLLibInstrumentor().instrument()

    _configured = True
"""
Triage service — FastAPI application.

Stateless microservice that evaluates drug-allergy conflict risk for a
patient. Fetches clinical data via fhir-clinical-client, runs the rule
engine, and returns a FHIR RiskAssessment resource.

Environment variables:
  FHIR_GATEWAY_URL   Base URL of the FHIR server (required)
                     e.g. http://fhir-service:8080/fhir  (docker-compose)
                          http://localhost:8080/fhir      (local dev)
                          http://<kong-ip>:8000/fhir      (deployed)
  FHIR_API_KEY       Kong API key — omit for local dev without Kong
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
import uuid
import logging

from fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException, Response
from fastapi.responses import JSONResponse

from fhir_clinical_client import FHIRClient, FHIRClientError, NotFoundError

from .models import (
    AnnotationModel,
    CodeableConceptModel,
    CodingModel,
    HealthResponse,
    PredictionModel,
    ReferenceModel,
    RiskAssessmentResponse,
    TriageRequest,
)
from .observability import current_trace_id, setup_tracing, tag_current_span
from .rules import RuleResult, evaluate

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Logging
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(levelname)s  %(name)s  %(message)s")
log = logging.getLogger("triage")

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# App
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

VERSION = "0.1.0"

app = FastAPI(
    title="Triage Service",
    description=(
        "Drug-allergy conflict triage microservice. "
        "Evaluates refill risk for a patient and returns a FHIR RiskAssessment."
    ),
    version=VERSION,
)

setup_tracing(app)


def _get_client() -> FHIRClient:
    """Build a FHIRClient from environment variables."""
    gateway_url = os.environ.get("FHIR_GATEWAY_URL", "")
    api_key = os.environ.get("FHIR_API_KEY", "")
    if not gateway_url:
        raise RuntimeError(
            "FHIR_GATEWAY_URL is not set. "
            "Set it to the Kong gateway URL, e.g. http://localhost:8000/fhir"
        )
    if not api_key:
        log.info("FHIR_API_KEY not set; using local-dev fallback without auth headers")
        return FHIRClient(gateway_url=gateway_url)
    return FHIRClient(gateway_url=gateway_url, api_key=api_key)


def _build_risk_assessment(
    patient_id: str,
    result: RuleResult,
) -> RiskAssessmentResponse:
    """Convert a RuleResult into a FHIR RiskAssessment response."""
    risk_level = result.risk_level
    qualitative_code = risk_level.lower()  # "high", "moderate", "low"

    prediction = PredictionModel(
        outcome=CodeableConceptModel(
            coding=[CodingModel(
                system="http://fhir-agent.local/triage/risk-level",
                code=risk_level,
                display=f"{risk_level.title()} Risk",
            )],
            text=f"{risk_level.title()} Risk",
        ),
        qualitativeRisk=CodeableConceptModel(
            coding=[CodingModel(
                system="http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/risk-probability",
                code=qualitative_code,
                display=risk_level.title(),
            )],
        ),
    )

    basis = (
        [ReferenceModel(reference=f"MedicationRequest/{mid}")
         for mid in result.basis_medication_ids]
        + [ReferenceModel(reference=f"AllergyIntolerance/{aid}")
           for aid in result.basis_allergy_ids]
    )

    return RiskAssessmentResponse(
        id=f"risk-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}",
        subject=ReferenceModel(reference=f"Patient/{patient_id}"),
        prediction=[prediction],
        note=[AnnotationModel(text=result.note)],
        basis=basis,
    )

# ── Triage service ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Clinical-hat consumer. Defaults to talking directly to the fhir container for
  # the local demo; set FHIR_GATEWAY_URL to the Kong proxy for the gated setup.
  triage:
    build:
      context: .
      dockerfile: triage-service/Dockerfile
    container_name: fhir-agent-triage
    ports:
      - "8001:8001"
    environment:
      # Default: direct to the fhir container (local demo, no Kong).
      # Override with the Kong proxy URL for the gated setup, e.g. http://localhost:8000/fhir
      FHIR_GATEWAY_URL: ${FHIR_GATEWAY_URL:-http://fhir:8080/fhir}
      FHIR_API_KEY: ${FHIR_API_KEY:-}            # Kong API key — omit for local dev
      # Observability profile only (docs/phase6): safe to leave set even when
      # jaeger isn't running -- the OTLP exporter fails closed in the
      # background, it never blocks or fails a real request.
      OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT: ${OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT:-http://jaeger:4317}
    depends_on:
      fhir:
        condition: service_healthy
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "python3", "-c", "import urllib.request; urllib.request.urlopen('http://localhost:8001/health')"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5
      start_period: 10s

  # ── MCP agent (run-once CLI) ──────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Clinical-hat consumer. Defaults to talking directly to the fhir container for
  # the local demo; set FHIR_GATEWAY_URL to the Kong proxy for the gated setup.
  mcp-agent:
    build:
      context: .
      dockerfile: mcp-agent/Dockerfile
    container_name: fhir-agent-mcp
    environment:
      # ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is preferred; CLAUDE_API_KEY (the Ona secret name) is
      # accepted as a fallback by the agent.
      ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${ANTHROPIC_API_KEY:-}
      CLAUDE_API_KEY: ${CLAUDE_API_KEY:-}
      # Default: direct to the fhir container (local demo, no Kong).
      FHIR_GATEWAY_URL: ${FHIR_GATEWAY_URL:-http://fhir:8080/fhir}
      FHIR_API_KEY: ${FHIR_API_KEY:-}            # Kong API key — omit for local dev
      TRIAGE_SERVICE_URL: http://triage:8001
      OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT: ${OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT:-http://jaeger:4317}
    depends_on:
      triage:
        condition: service_healthy
    stdin_open: true
    tty: true

  # ══ Phase 2 (opt-in: `docker compose --profile phase2 up`) ═════════════════
  # Additive only — none of the below start on a plain `docker compose up`.

  # ── Legacy RxClaim / IBM i emulator (INTERNAL ONLY — no host port) ─────────
  rxclaim-emulator:
17:      - "8080:8080"
42:      - "8001:8001"
113:      - "8090:8090"
164:      - "8000:8000"          # proxy (matches the cloud port-forward convention)
351:      - "8010:8010"

WORKDIR /app

"""Scoring contract rows with a verified artifact: probability, comparison score, percentile and
per-patient reasons (FR-S2, FR-M8).

Reasons are found by **occlusion**: re-score the patient with one input at a time set to what a
typical MEPS adult has (`etl/meps_reference.json` → `typical`). An input whose typical value would
lower the estimate is a reason the estimate is higher. It is deterministic, needs no extra
library, and costs one batched prediction of 26 rows per patient. Like every explanation, it
describes what the model weighed, not what causes admissions. Inputs that were defaulted (e.g.
income not recorded) are never given as reasons.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from outcome_prediction.model import CONTRACT_VERSION, FEATURES, comparison_matrix, feature_matrix
from outcome_prediction.model.artifact import Artifact, load_artifact, risk_percentile
from outcome_prediction.settings import models_dir

REFERENCE = Path(__file__).parent / "etl" / "meps_reference.json"
TOP_REASONS = 3
MIN_EFFECT = 0.005           # an input must move the estimate by at least half a percentage point

# Plain-language names for reasons (rationale text and the agent's narration).
FEATURE_NAMES = {
    "sex": "sex", "racethx": "race and ethnicity", "regiony1": "region", "agey1x": "age",
    "inscovy1": "insurance", "povcaty1": "household income", "ipdisy1": "hospital stays in the past year",
    "ipngtdy1": "nights in hospital in the past year", "ertoty1": "emergency-room visits in the past year",
    "obtotvy1": "office visits in the past year", "optotvy1": "hospital outpatient visits in the past year",
    "hhtotdy1": "home-health days in the past year", "rxtoty1": "prescription fills in the past year",
    "totexpy1": "health care spending in the past year", "hibpdx": "high blood pressure",
    "chddx": "coronary heart disease", "angidx": "angina", "midx": "a past heart attack",
    "ohrtdx": "other heart disease", "strkdx": "a past stroke", "emphdx": "emphysema or COPD",
    "diabdx": "diabetes", "arthdx": "arthritis", "asthdx": "asthma", "choldx": "high cholesterol",
}


class ArtifactNotFound(RuntimeError):
    """No artifact to serve."""


@dataclass
class Score:
    patient_ref: str
    probability: float
    comparison: float
    percentile: int
    reasons: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)         # feature names, most influential first


def find_artifact() -> Path:
    """The artifact named by OUTCOME_PREDICTION_ARTIFACT, else the newest meps25-v1 one."""
    import os
    if named := os.environ.get("OUTCOME_PREDICTION_ARTIFACT"):
        return Path(named)
    found = sorted(models_dir().glob(f"gbm-{CONTRACT_VERSION}-*"))
    if not found:
        raise ArtifactNotFound(f"no gbm-{CONTRACT_VERSION}-* artifact under {models_dir()} — "
                               "train one (python -m outcome_prediction.model.train) or set OUTCOME_PREDICTION_ARTIFACT")
    return found[-1]


class Scorer:
    """Loads an artifact once — verifying its manifest before any deserialisation (O17)."""

    def __init__(self, artifact_dir: Path | None = None):
        self.artifact: Artifact = load_artifact(artifact_dir or find_artifact())
        meta = self.artifact.metadata
        if meta.get("contract_version") != CONTRACT_VERSION:
            raise ValueError(f"artifact contract {meta.get('contract_version')} != served {CONTRACT_VERSION}")
        self.quantiles = meta["training_score_quantiles"]
        self.typical = json.loads(REFERENCE.read_text())["typical"]

    @property
    def model_id(self) -> str:
        return self.artifact.metadata["model_id"]

    def score(self, rows: pd.DataFrame, defaulted: dict[str, set[str]] | None = None) -> list[Score]:
        """Score contract rows (`patient_ref` + the 25 features). `defaulted` maps a patient_ref to
        the features filled by a default — those are never given as reasons."""
        defaulted = defaulted or {}
        X = feature_matrix(rows[FEATURES])
        p = self.artifact.model.predict_proba(X)[:, 1]
        comp = self.artifact.comparison.predict_proba(comparison_matrix(rows))[:, 1]
        return [Score(patient_ref=str(ref), probability=float(p[i]), comparison=float(comp[i]),
                      percentile=risk_percentile(float(p[i]), self.quantiles),
                      reasons=self.reasons(rows.iloc[[i]], float(p[i]), defaulted.get(str(ref), set())))
                for i, ref in enumerate(rows.patient_ref)]

    def reasons(self, row: pd.DataFrame, probability: float, skip: set[str]) -> list[str]:
        candidates = [f for f in FEATURES if f not in skip and row[f].iloc[0] != self.typical[f]]
        if not candidates:
            return []
        variants = pd.concat([row[FEATURES]] * len(candidates), ignore_index=True)
        for i, f in enumerate(candidates):
            variants.loc[i, f] = self.typical[f]
        effect = probability - self.artifact.model.predict_proba(feature_matrix(variants))[:, 1]
        order = np.argsort(-effect, kind="stable")
        return [candidates[i] for i in order if effect[i] >= MIN_EFFECT][:TOP_REASONS]

    "chddx": "coronary heart disease", "angidx": "angina", "midx": "a past heart attack",
    "ohrtdx": "other heart disease", "strkdx": "a past stroke", "emphdx": "emphysema or COPD",
    "diabdx": "diabetes", "arthdx": "arthritis", "asthdx": "asthma", "choldx": "high cholesterol",
}


class ArtifactNotFound(RuntimeError):
    """No artifact to serve."""


@dataclass
class Score:
    patient_ref: str
    probability: float
    comparison: float
    percentile: int
    reasons: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)         # feature names, most influential first


def find_artifact() -> Path:
    """The artifact named by OUTCOME_PREDICTION_ARTIFACT, else the newest meps25-v1 one."""
    import os
    if named := os.environ.get("OUTCOME_PREDICTION_ARTIFACT"):
        return Path(named)
    found = sorted(models_dir().glob(f"gbm-{CONTRACT_VERSION}-*"))
    if not found:
        raise ArtifactNotFound(f"no gbm-{CONTRACT_VERSION}-* artifact under {models_dir()} — "
                               "train one (python -m outcome_prediction.model.train) or set OUTCOME_PREDICTION_ARTIFACT")
    return found[-1]


class Scorer:
    """Loads an artifact once — verifying its manifest before any deserialisation (O17)."""

    def __init__(self, artifact_dir: Path | None = None):
        self.artifact: Artifact = load_artifact(artifact_dir or find_artifact())
        meta = self.artifact.metadata
        if meta.get("contract_version") != CONTRACT_VERSION:
            raise ValueError(f"artifact contract {meta.get('contract_version')} != served {CONTRACT_VERSION}")
        self.quantiles = meta["training_score_quantiles"]
        self.typical = json.loads(REFERENCE.read_text())["typical"]

    @property
    def model_id(self) -> str:
        return self.artifact.metadata["model_id"]

    def score(self, rows: pd.DataFrame, defaulted: dict[str, set[str]] | None = None) -> list[Score]:
        """Score contract rows (`patient_ref` + the 25 features). `defaulted` maps a patient_ref to
        the features filled by a default — those are never given as reasons."""
        defaulted = defaulted or {}
        X = feature_matrix(rows[FEATURES])
        p = self.artifact.model.predict_proba(X)[:, 1]
        comp = self.artifact.comparison.predict_proba(comparison_matrix(rows))[:, 1]
        return [Score(patient_ref=str(ref), probability=float(p[i]), comparison=float(comp[i]),
                      percentile=risk_percentile(float(p[i]), self.quantiles),
                      reasons=self.reasons(rows.iloc[[i]], float(p[i]), defaulted.get(str(ref), set())))
                for i, ref in enumerate(rows.patient_ref)]

    def reasons(self, row: pd.DataFrame, probability: float, skip: set[str]) -> list[str]:
        candidates = [f for f in FEATURES if f not in skip and row[f].iloc[0] != self.typical[f]]
        if not candidates:
            return []
        variants = pd.concat([row[FEATURES]] * len(candidates), ignore_index=True)
        for i, f in enumerate(candidates):
            variants.loc[i, f] = self.typical[f]
        effect = probability - self.artifact.model.predict_proba(feature_matrix(variants))[:, 1]
        order = np.argsort(-effect, kind="stable")
        return [candidates[i] for i in order if effect[i] >= MIN_EFFECT][:TOP_REASONS]

"""FHIR R4 `RiskAssessment` and `Bundle` for a 12-month hospitalization estimate (O3, design.md §4).

A superset of triage-service's shape: it adds the numeric probability. Deliberately absent:
`qualitativeRisk` — no thresholds have been clinically signed off (O24). The rationale is
templated from the reasons, never model-generated.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import uuid
from datetime import date

from dateutil.relativedelta import relativedelta
from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict

from outcome_prediction.scoring import FEATURE_NAMES, Score

EXT = "http://fhir-agent.local/StructureDefinition/"
MODEL_SYSTEM = "http://fhir-agent.local/outcome-prediction/model"
# SNOMED CT 32485007 — checked in M7 against tx.fhir.org (International edition 2025-02-01):
# active, FSN "Hospital admission (procedure)", parent "Admission to establishment" (O22).
OUTCOME = {"system": "http://snomed.info/sct", "code": "32485007", "display": "Hospital admission (procedure)"}
NOTE = ("12-month planning estimate for population care management, not a diagnosis and not for "
        "emergencies. Trained on US MEPS public survey data; not yet validated on this organisation's "
        "patients. The reasons describe what the model weighed, not what causes admissions.")


class _Model(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")


class Coding(_Model):
    system: str
    code: str
    display: str | None = None


class CodeableConcept(_Model):
    coding: list[Coding]
    text: str | None = None


class Identifier(_Model):
    value: str


class Reference(_Model):
    reference: str | None = None
    identifier: Identifier | None = None


class Extension(_Model):
    url: str
    valueDecimal: float | None = None
    valueInteger: int | None = None
    valueString: str | None = None


class Period(_Model):
    start: str
    end: str


class Prediction(_Model):
    outcome: CodeableConcept
    probabilityDecimal: float
    whenPeriod: Period
    rationale: str
    extension: list[Extension]


class Annotation(_Model):
    text: str


class RiskAssessment(_Model):
    resourceType: str = "RiskAssessment"
    id: str
    status: str = "final"
    subject: Reference
    occurrenceDateTime: str
    method: CodeableConcept
    basis: list[Reference] = []
    prediction: list[Prediction]
    note: list[Annotation]
    extension: list[Extension] = []


class BundleEntry(_Model):
    fullUrl: str
    resource: RiskAssessment


class Bundle(_Model):
    resourceType: str = "Bundle"
    id: str
    type: str = "collection"
    entry: list[BundleEntry]


def rationale(reasons: list[str]) -> str:
    if not reasons:
        return "No single input raises this estimate much above a typical adult's."
    names = [FEATURE_NAMES[r] for r in reasons]
    joined = names[0] if len(names) == 1 else ", ".join(names[:-1]) + " and " + names[-1]
    return f"Inputs raising the estimate most, compared with a typical adult: {joined}."


def build(score: Score, *, model_id: str, contract_version: str, as_of: date, subject: Reference,
          basis: list[str] = (), warnings: list[str] = ()) -> RiskAssessment:
    """One RiskAssessment. `basis` are FHIR `Type/id` references to the records used (FR-F4)."""
    extensions = [
        Extension(url=EXT + "comparison-probability", valueDecimal=round(score.comparison, 4)),
        Extension(url=EXT + "risk-percentile", valueInteger=score.percentile),
        Extension(url=EXT + "contract-version", valueString=contract_version),
        *[Extension(url=EXT + "top-reasons", valueString=r) for r in score.reasons],
    ]
    return RiskAssessment(
        id=str(uuid.uuid4()),
        subject=subject,
        occurrenceDateTime=as_of.isoformat(),
        method=CodeableConcept(coding=[Coding(system=MODEL_SYSTEM, code=model_id)], text=model_id),
        basis=[Reference(reference=ref) for ref in basis],
        prediction=[Prediction(
            outcome=CodeableConcept(coding=[Coding(**OUTCOME)], text="Hospital admission"),
            probabilityDecimal=round(score.probability, 4),
            whenPeriod=Period(start=as_of.isoformat(), end=(as_of + relativedelta(months=12)).isoformat()),
            rationale=rationale(score.reasons),
            extension=extensions)],
        note=[Annotation(text=NOTE)],
        extension=[Extension(url=EXT + "input-warning", valueString=w) for w in warnings],
    )


def bundle(assessments: list[RiskAssessment]) -> Bundle:
    return Bundle(id=str(uuid.uuid4()),
                  entry=[BundleEntry(fullUrl=f"urn:uuid:{a.id}", resource=a) for a in assessments])

"""OpenTelemetry for the scoring service — triage-service's pattern (docs/phase6, H16/H22).

Deliberately a small copy, not shared via agent_platform: like triage-service, this is a
deterministic-tier service, not an LLM agent. FastAPI instrumentation continues an incoming
trace; urllib instrumentation carries it into every `client/clinical` call to the FHIR server.
If nothing listens at OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT the exporter drops spans in the background —
it never blocks or fails a request.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import os

from fastapi import FastAPI
from opentelemetry import trace
from opentelemetry.exporter.otlp.proto.grpc.trace_exporter import OTLPSpanExporter
from opentelemetry.instrumentation.fastapi import FastAPIInstrumentor
from opentelemetry.instrumentation.urllib import URLLibInstrumentor
from opentelemetry.sdk.resources import Resource
from opentelemetry.sdk.trace import TracerProvider
from opentelemetry.sdk.trace.export import BatchSpanProcessor

_configured = False


def tag_current_span(component: str, **attributes) -> None:
    span = trace.get_current_span()
    span.set_attribute("fhir_agent.layer", "deterministic")
    span.set_attribute("fhir_agent.component", component)
    for key, value in attributes.items():
        span.set_attribute(f"fhir_agent.{key}", value)


def current_trace_id() -> str | None:
    ctx = trace.get_current_span().get_span_context()
    return format(ctx.trace_id, "032x") if ctx.is_valid else None


def setup_tracing(app: FastAPI, service_name: str = "outcome-prediction-service") -> None:
    global _configured
    if _configured:
        return
    endpoint = os.environ.get("OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT", "http://localhost:4317")
    provider = TracerProvider(resource=Resource.create({"service.name": service_name}))
    provider.add_span_processor(BatchSpanProcessor(OTLPSpanExporter(endpoint=endpoint, insecure=True)))
    trace.set_tracer_provider(provider)
    FastAPIInstrumentor.instrument_app(app)
    URLLibInstrumentor().instrument()
    _configured = True

"""OpenTelemetry for the scoring service — triage-service's pattern (docs/phase6, H16/H22).

Deliberately a small copy, not shared via agent_platform: like triage-service, this is a
deterministic-tier service, not an LLM agent. FastAPI instrumentation continues an incoming
trace; urllib instrumentation carries it into every `client/clinical` call to the FHIR server.
If nothing listens at OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT the exporter drops spans in the background —
it never blocks or fails a request.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import os

from fastapi import FastAPI
from opentelemetry import trace
from opentelemetry.exporter.otlp.proto.grpc.trace_exporter import OTLPSpanExporter
from opentelemetry.instrumentation.fastapi import FastAPIInstrumentor
from opentelemetry.instrumentation.urllib import URLLibInstrumentor
from opentelemetry.sdk.resources import Resource
from opentelemetry.sdk.trace import TracerProvider
from opentelemetry.sdk.trace.export import BatchSpanProcessor

_configured = False


def tag_current_span(component: str, **attributes) -> None:
    span = trace.get_current_span()
    span.set_attribute("fhir_agent.layer", "deterministic")
    span.set_attribute("fhir_agent.component", component)
    for key, value in attributes.items():
        span.set_attribute(f"fhir_agent.{key}", value)


def current_trace_id() -> str | None:
    ctx = trace.get_current_span().get_span_context()
    return format(ctx.trace_id, "032x") if ctx.is_valid else None


def setup_tracing(app: FastAPI, service_name: str = "outcome-prediction-service") -> None:
    global _configured
    if _configured:
        return
    endpoint = os.environ.get("OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT", "http://localhost:4317")
    provider = TracerProvider(resource=Resource.create({"service.name": service_name}))
    provider.add_span_processor(BatchSpanProcessor(OTLPSpanExporter(endpoint=endpoint, insecure=True)))
    trace.set_tracer_provider(provider)
    FastAPIInstrumentor.instrument_app(app)
    URLLibInstrumentor().instrument()
    _configured = True
