## Overview

This project builds a platform where clinicians can describe healthcare workflows in natural language, and an **agentic orchestration layer** (powered by LLMs and MCP) generates, deploys, and maintains FHIR-based automations. The goal is to replace traditional SaaS development with AI-driven orchestration, giving healthcare organisations custom tools without needing a full-time software development team.

**First workflow:** *Prescription Refill Risk Triage* — an agent that assesses drug-allergy conflicts, interactions, and fulfilment risks, producing triage recommendations with confidence scores and audit trails.

---

## Architecture

The platform is built as a collection of microservices, designed to be cloud-agnostic and fully compatible with FHIR R4.

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    Agentic Orchestration                        │
│                (MCP Agent — LLM-powered)                       │
│   - Interprets user intents                                     │
│   - Discovers and composes MCP tools                           │
│   - Executes workflows, logs decisions                         │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                              │
                              ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                       MCP Tool Servers                         │
│   - FHIR Tools (Patient, Medication, Allergy)                  │
│   - Safety Tools (drug-allergy, interactions)                  │
│   - Workflow Tools (submit triage, escalate)                   │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                              │
                              ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                        FHIR Servers                            │
│   - Generic FHIR R4 server (development & testing)            │
│   - Future: EHR sandboxes (Epic, Athena) or emulators         │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Microservices

| Service | Purpose | Status |
|---|---|---|
| **fhir-service** | Generic FHIR R4 server (HAPI JPA). Used for local development and as the FHIR data source for the MCP agent. | ✅ Running (H2 local, Neon PostgreSQL cloud) |
| **epic-emulator** | Placeholder — will add Epic-specific customisations (auth stubs, custom profiles, proprietary extensions). | ⏳ Not yet implemented |
| **athena-emulator** | Placeholder — will add Athena-specific customisations. | ⏳ Not yet implemented |
| **triage-service** | FastAPI drug-allergy rule engine → FHIR `RiskAssessment` (HIGH/MODERATE/LOW) with audit trail. | ✅ Running (local + Docker Compose) |
| **mcp-agent** | LLM-powered orchestration layer that composes FHIR + triage tools. Self-hosted Ollama by default (no API key, no cost); Anthropic and other OpenAI-compatible providers available via explicit opt-in (`docs/phase6/decisions.md` H45). | ✅ Running (local + Docker Compose) |

| **claims-service** *(Phase 2)* | Spring Boot claims-adjudication façade: anti-corruption layer + layered rules engine + Decision Contract; persists a FHIR decision graph. | ✅ Running (`--profile phase2`) |
| **claims-agent** *(Phase 2)* | Non-authoritative agent that explains adjudication decisions in plain language. | ✅ Running (`--profile phase2`) |
| **provider-registry-service** *(Phase 3)* | FastAPI façade over the real, curated NPPES/NUCC provider registry: taxonomy resolution + haversine proximity search. Internal-only. | ✅ Running (`--profile phase3`) |
| **provider-mcp-server** *(Phase 3)* | The platform's first real, hand-built MCP server — genuine `initialize`/`tools/list`/`tools/call`, stdio transport. Thin adapter over `provider-registry-service`. | ✅ Running (local child process; no compose service — see [`docs/phase3/README.md`](docs/phase3/README.md)) |
| **provider-curation-agent** *(Phase 3)* | Non-authoritative agent that orchestrates real NPPES/NUCC/ZCTA ingestion and narrates the run. | ✅ Running (`--profile phase3`) |
| **provider-search-agent** *(Phase 3)* | Real MCP client/host: turns a natural-language clinical request into ranked, traceable providers by discovering and calling `provider-mcp-server`'s tools live. | ✅ Running (`--profile phase3`) |

## Current Status

**This section covers Phase 1 (the original walking skeleton) specifically.** Phase 2
(claims adjudication) and Phase 3 (provider search) are also complete and run locally —
see their own sections below, or [Status & future work](#status--future-work) for the
full picture across all three.

The end-to-end walking skeleton runs locally and via Docker Compose:
**mcp-agent → triage-service → fhir-service**. A natural-language clinician query
resolves a patient, evaluates drug-allergy risk, and returns a structured
recommendation (see [Quick demo](#quick-demo)).

The FHIR R4 server is built on the **official HAPI FHIR JPA starter (8.8.0)**. It supports:

- All FHIR R4 resource endpoints (`Patient`, `MedicationRequest`, `AllergyIntolerance`, etc.)
- Local development with an in-memory H2 database (`./mvnw spring-boot:run`)
- Cloud deployment with Neon serverless PostgreSQL (environment-variable-based configuration)
- FHIR `CapabilityStatement` at `GET /fhir/metadata`

The server is intentionally generic — it does not emulate any specific EHR. The agent and MCP tooling are built against a standard FHIR R4 endpoint first, ensuring portability. EHR-specific authentication, profiles, and extensions will be added later in the emulator modules.

---

## Phase 2 — Claims Adjudication Modernisation Slice

Phase 2 extends the platform into **prescription claim adjudication**, wrapping a simulated
legacy RxClaim / IBM i core with modern services — an **API façade**, an **anti-corruption
layer**, a deterministic **rules engine**, an auditable **FHIR decision graph**, and a
plain-language **explanation agent**. Design, requirements, and architecture live in
[`docs/phase2/`](docs/phase2/README.md).

Request flow (opt-in `phase2` profile):

```
claims-agent ──▶ claims-service ──┬──▶ rxclaim-emulator   (legacy pricing/SOR, internal only)
 (explains)        (façade + ACL   ├──▶ triage-service     (clinical safety, reused Phase 1)
                    + rules engine) └──▶ fhir-service       (Claim/ClaimResponse/Task/Provenance)
```

The legacy core is **wrapped, not rewritten** (strangler pattern): the modern layer owns the
rules, experience, and audit trail; pricing and the member system-of-record remain "legacy".
Decisions are **deterministic** and **idempotent** — the same claim yields the same decision
and never double-writes its artefacts.

### Run the Phase 2 demo

```bash
# Bring up the full stack (Phase 1 services start automatically as dependencies)
docker compose --profile phase2 up --build -d

# Seed the FHIR fixtures and drive the six golden paths
# (approved / pended / routed / denied / multi-reason / clinical-safety)
python3 data/scripts/seed_claims_demo.py

# Explain a decision in plain language (deterministic without an API key)
docker compose --profile phase2 run --rm claims-agent \
  --no-llm --claim '{"claimId":"C1","memberId":"000000001","planId":"COM-SILVER","rxcui":"1991302","ndc":"63552-200","drugName":"semaglutide","quantity":1,"daysSupply":28,"dateOfService":"2026-06-01","prescriberNpi":"1234567890","coverageEffective":"2026-01-01","coverageTermination":"2026-12-31","priorAuthOnFile":false,"stepTherapyMet":false}'
```

A plain `docker compose up` (no profile) still runs **only** the Phase 1 stack — Phase 2 is
strictly additive.

> **The demo FHIR server is in-memory**, so it boots empty every time, and adjudication **fails
> closed** — a member with no clinical record pends rather than approving. Always run the seeder
> (it seeds fixtures *and* drives the paths). See the
> [demo prep checklist](docs/demo-guide.md#1-before-any-demo).

### Tests

```bash
pytest                                      # all Python suites (config in pytest.ini)
mvn -f claims-service/pom.xml test          # Phase 2 façade: unit + contract tests
mvn -f rxclaim-emulator/pom.xml test        # simulated legacy core
pytest e2e/                                 # golden paths (needs the phase2 stack up; else skips)
```

CI (`.github/workflows/tests.yml`) runs a **Phase-1-only** job (proving independence) plus the
Phase 2 suites. It does **not** run the e2e suite — that gap, and everything else that is and
isn't covered, is documented in the [testing guide](docs/testing-guide.md).

---

## Phase 3 — Provider Search & Referral

Phase 3 answers the question Phase 1/2 don't: *"who can this patient actually see?"* Given a
patient's location and a clinical need, it returns a ranked, explained list of **real**
providers — sourced from authoritative public data (NPPES), not a paid third-party directory
API — with full lineage back to the source record. **M1–M7 complete; Phase 3b (live cloud
deployment) not started.** Full design, milestone history, and every architectural decision
(with status tracking): [`docs/phase3/`](docs/phase3/README.md).

It's also this platform's **first genuine Model Context Protocol integration**. Prior "agent
tools" (`mcp-agent/src/agent/tools.py`) are in-process Python function dispatch; Phase 3 builds
a real, hand-built MCP server and a real MCP client/host, talking the actual protocol
(`initialize` → `tools/list` → `tools/call`) — not a simulation of it.

Request flow (opt-in `phase3` profile):

```
provider-search-agent ──(MCP: stdio)──▶ provider-mcp-server ──(HTTP)──▶ provider-registry-service ──▶ Postgres
  (NL request, real MCP        (real MCP server —              (taxonomy resolution +
   client/host, discovers       genuine protocol                haversine proximity search;
   tools live via tools/list)   boundary)                       internal-only, never on Kong edge)

provider-curation-agent ──▶ data/scripts/provider_ingest/*.py ──▶ Postgres
  (orchestrates + narrates       (real NPPES/NUCC/Census ingestion —
   a run; NOT an MCP client)      curated to NC/CA/MT, 12,582 real providers)
```

Real, not synthetic, on the provider side: 12,582 real providers across three curated states
(NC/CA/MT), pulled live from the NPPES NPI Registry and NUCC taxonomy sources, with lineage
from every registry record back to its ingestion run. (Patients stay synthetic, as elsewhere in
this repo — Phase 3 is about *finding* a provider, not about patient data.)

### Run the Phase 3 demo

```bash
# Bring up Postgres + the registry service (Phase 1/2 services start automatically as
# dependencies if you also pass their profiles; phase3 alone is self-contained)
docker compose --profile phase3 up --build -d postgres provider-registry

# Seed real data (NC only — fast; add CA,MT for the full curated set, ~1-2 min)
docker compose --profile phase3 run --rm -T provider-curation-agent --states NC --no-llm

# Ask a real question (needs ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or CLAUDE_API_KEY in .env — this agent has
# no deterministic fallback, unlike claims-agent: its whole job is NL understanding)
docker compose --profile phase3 run --rm provider-search-agent \
  --query "find an endocrinologist near 27514"
```

> **Use `-T` with `docker compose run` for any Phase 3 CLI agent** (`provider-curation-agent`,
> `provider-search-agent`) if you're scripting it non-interactively — some environments
> silently swallow stdout without it. `docker run -d ... && docker logs <container>` is a
> reliable fallback if output still doesn't show up. See [`docs/phase3/README.md`](docs/phase3/README.md).

A plain `docker compose up` (no profile) still runs **only** the Phase 1 stack — Phase 3 is
strictly additive, same guarantee as Phase 2.

### Tests

```bash
pytest                                      # all Python suites, including Phase 3 (config in pytest.ini)
```

CI (`.github/workflows/tests.yml`) runs `phase3-python` (the full Phase 3 suite against a
**real Postgres service container** — DB-backed tests execute for real in CI, not just
locally) and `phase3-terraform` (`terraform validate`, matrix across all four Phase 3
Terraform directories — deliberately `validate`, not `plan`, since `plan` needs live GCP
credentials this project doesn't provision). The real, billed-API-call groundedness eval
self-skips in CI (no key secret configured) — a deliberate cost-conscious choice.

## Getting Started

### Prerequisites

- **Java 21** (JDK — required; pom.xml targets Java 21)
- **Maven 3.8+** (or use the included Maven wrapper `./mvnw`)
- **Docker** (optional — required for integration tests using Testcontainers)
- **Neon** account (optional — required for cloud PostgreSQL profile)

### Clone the repository

```bash
git clone https://github.com/bhaskarcmu/fhir-agent.git
cd fhir-agent
```

### Run the FHIR server locally (H2)

```bash
cd fhir-service
./mvnw spring-boot:run
```

The server starts on `http://localhost:8080`. Visit `http://localhost:8080/fhir/metadata` to see the FHIR `CapabilityStatement`.

### Run with Neon PostgreSQL (cloud)

1. Create a [Neon](https://neon.tech) account and database.
2. Get your connection string from the Neon dashboard (format: `postgresql://user:‹redacted:url-credentials›host/db?sslmode=require`).
3. Convert it to JDBC format: `jdbc:postgresql://host/db?user=user&password=‹redacted:url-query-password›&sslmode=require`
4. Run:

```bash
cd fhir-service
SPRING_DATASOURCE_URL="jdbc:postgresql://host/db?user=user&password=‹redacted:url-query-password›&sslmode=require" \
SPRING_DATASOURCE_DRIVER_CLASS_NAME="org.postgresql.Driver" \
HIBERNATE_DIALECT="ca.uhn.fhir.jpa.model.dialect.HapiFhirPostgresDialect" \
./mvnw spring-boot:run -Dspring-boot.run.profiles=neon -Dmaven.test.skip=true
```

## Development Environment

The project uses a **devcontainer** to ensure a consistent environment across all contributors. The `.devcontainer/` directory defines:

- `Dockerfile` — Java 21, Python 3, Node.js, Maven, Docker-in-Docker, kubectl, Helm, Terraform
- VS Code extensions — Java, Spring Boot, Python, GitHub Copilot, Continue, Roo Code
- Post-start automation — configures AI tools (Claude Code, Continue, Roo Code) using secrets stored in Ona

**Opening the project:**

- **Local (Docker Desktop):** Open the folder in VS Code and click *Reopen in Container*
- **Cloud (Ona):** The container builds automatically on first launch

### Build and test before committing

```bash
# Python packages (editable installs + test tooling via the [dev] extras)
python -m pip install -e "client/clinical[dev]" -e "agent-platform[dev]" -e "triage-service[dev]" -e "mcp-agent[dev]"
pytest                              # runs all Python suites (config in pytest.ini)
pytest agent-platform/tests -q      # separate invocation -- see pytest.ini's own comment on why

# FHIR service (Java).
# NOTE: unset any SPRING_DATASOURCE_URL / NEON_* env vars first, so the tests use
# the in-memory H2 default. Otherwise MdmTest boots the full app against a live
# database and fails on auth — a config/env issue, not a code failure.
cd fhir-service && ./mvnw clean verify
```

61	## Overview
62	
63	This project builds a platform where clinicians can describe healthcare workflows in natural language, and an **agentic orchestration layer** (powered by LLMs and MCP) generates, deploys, and maintains FHIR-based automations. The goal is to replace traditional SaaS development with AI-driven orchestration, giving healthcare organisations custom tools without needing a full-time software development team.
64	
65	**First workflow:** *Prescription Refill Risk Triage* — an agent that assesses drug-allergy conflicts, interactions, and fulfilment risks, producing triage recommendations with confidence scores and audit trails.
66

69	## Architecture
70	
71	The platform is built as a collection of microservices, designed to be cloud-agnostic and fully compatible with FHIR R4.
72	
73	```
74	┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
75	│                    Agentic Orchestration                        │
76	│                (MCP Agent — LLM-powered)                       │
77	│   - Interprets user intents                                     │
78	│   - Discovers and composes MCP tools                           │
79	│   - Executes workflows, logs decisions                         │
80	└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
81	                              │
82	                              ▼
83	┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
84	│                       MCP Tool Servers                         │
85	│   - FHIR Tools (Patient, Medication, Allergy)                  │
86	│   - Safety Tools (drug-allergy, interactions)                  │
87	│   - Workflow Tools (submit triage, escalate)                   │
88	└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
89	                              │
90	                              ▼
91	┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
92	│                        FHIR Servers                            │
93	│   - Generic FHIR R4 server (development & testing)            │
94	│   - Future: EHR sandboxes (Epic, Athena) or emulators         │
95	└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
96	```
97	
98	### Microservices
99	
100	| Service | Purpose | Status |
101	|---|---|---|
102	| **fhir-service** | Generic FHIR R4 server (HAPI JPA). Used for local development and as the FHIR data source for the MCP agent. | ✅ Running (H2 local, Neon PostgreSQL cloud) |
103	| **epic-emulator** | Placeholder — will add Epic-specific customisations (auth stubs, custom profiles, proprietary extensions). | ⏳ Not yet implemented |
104	| **athena-emulator** | Placeholder — will add Athena-specific customisations. | ⏳ Not yet implemented |
105	| **triage-service** | FastAPI drug-allergy rule engine → FHIR `RiskAssessment` (HIGH/MODERATE/LOW) with audit trail. | ✅ Running (local + Docker Compose) |
106	| **mcp-agent** | LLM-powered orchestration layer that composes FHIR + triage tools. Self-hosted Ollama by default (no API key, no cost); Anthropic and other OpenAI-compatible providers available via explicit opt-in (`docs/phase6/decisions.md` H45). | ✅ Running (local + Docker Compose) |
107	| **rxclaim-emulator** *(Phase 2)* | Simulated legacy IBM i / RxClaim adjudication core: fixed-width DDS-style records, DB2/SQL400-style tables, RPG/CL-style `ADJRXCLM`. Internal-only. | ✅ Running (`--profile phase2`) |
108	| **claims-service** *(Phase 2)* | Spring Boot claims-adjudication façade: anti-corruption layer + layered rules engine + Decision Contract; persists a FHIR decision graph. | ✅ Running (`--profile phase2`) |
109	| **claims-agent** *(Phase 2)* | Non-authoritative agent that explains adjudication decisions in plain language. | ✅ Running (`--profile phase2`) |
110	| **provider-registry-service** *(Phase 3)* | FastAPI façade over the real, curated NPPES/NUCC provider registry: taxonomy resolution + haversine proximity search. Internal-only. | ✅ Running (`--profile phase3`) |
111	| **provider-mcp-server** *(Phase 3)* | The platform's first real, hand-built MCP server — genuine `initialize`/`tools/list`/`tools/call`, stdio transport. Thin adapter over `provider-registry-service`. | ✅ Running (local child process; no compose service — see [`docs/phase3/README.md`](docs/phase3/README.md)) |
112	| **provider-curation-agent** *(Phase 3)* | Non-authoritative agent that orchestrates real NPPES/NUCC/ZCTA ingestion and narrates the run. | ✅ Running (`--profile phase3`) |
113	| **provider-search-agent** *(Phase 3)* | Real MCP client/host: turns a natural-language clinical request into ranked, traceable providers by discovering and calling `provider-mcp-server`'s tools live. | ✅ Running (`--profile phase3`) |

117	## Current Status
118	
119	**This section covers Phase 1 (the original walking skeleton) specifically.** Phase 2
120	(claims adjudication) and Phase 3 (provider search) are also complete and run locally —
121	see their own sections below, or [Status & future work](#status--future-work) for the
122	full picture across all three.
123	
124	The end-to-end walking skeleton runs locally and via Docker Compose:
125	**mcp-agent → triage-service → fhir-service**. A natural-language clinician query
126	resolves a patient, evaluates drug-allergy risk, and returns a structured
127	recommendation (see [Quick demo](#quick-demo)).
128	
129	The FHIR R4 server is built on the **official HAPI FHIR JPA starter (8.8.0)**. It supports:
130	
131	- All FHIR R4 resource endpoints (`Patient`, `MedicationRequest`, `AllergyIntolerance`, etc.)
132	- Local development with an in-memory H2 database (`./mvnw spring-boot:run`)
133	- Cloud deployment with Neon serverless PostgreSQL (environment-variable-based configuration)
134	- FHIR `CapabilityStatement` at `GET /fhir/metadata`
135	
136	The server is intentionally generic — it does not emulate any specific EHR. The agent and MCP tooling are built against a standard FHIR R4 endpoint first, ensuring portability. EHR-specific authentication, profiles, and extensions will be added later in the emulator modules.

140	## Phase 2 — Claims Adjudication Modernisation Slice
141	
142	Phase 2 extends the platform into **prescription claim adjudication**, wrapping a simulated
143	legacy RxClaim / IBM i core with modern services — an **API façade**, an **anti-corruption
144	layer**, a deterministic **rules engine**, an auditable **FHIR decision graph**, and a
145	plain-language **explanation agent**. Design, requirements, and architecture live in
146	[`docs/phase2/`](docs/phase2/README.md).
147	
148	Request flow (opt-in `phase2` profile):
149	
150	```
151	claims-agent ──▶ claims-service ──┬──▶ rxclaim-emulator   (legacy pricing/SOR, internal only)
152	 (explains)        (façade + ACL   ├──▶ triage-service     (clinical safety, reused Phase 1)
153	                    + rules engine) └──▶ fhir-service       (Claim/ClaimResponse/Task/Provenance)
154	```
155	
156	The legacy core is **wrapped, not rewritten** (strangler pattern): the modern layer owns the
157	rules, experience, and audit trail; pricing and the member system-of-record remain "legacy".
158	Decisions are **deterministic** and **idempotent** — the same claim yields the same decision
159	and never double-writes its artefacts.
160	
161	### Run the Phase 2 demo
162	
163	```bash
164	# Bring up the full stack (Phase 1 services start automatically as dependencies)
165	docker compose --profile phase2 up --build -d
166	
167	# Seed the FHIR fixtures and drive the six golden paths
168	# (approved / pended / routed / denied / multi-reason / clinical-safety)
169	python3 data/scripts/seed_claims_demo.py
170	
171	# Explain a decision in plain language (deterministic without an API key)
172	docker compose --profile phase2 run --rm claims-agent \
173	  --no-llm --claim '{"claimId":"C1","memberId":"000000001","planId":"COM-SILVER","rxcui":"1991302","ndc":"63552-200","drugName":"semaglutide","quantity":1,"daysSupply":28,"dateOfService":"2026-06-01","prescriberNpi":"1234567890","coverageEffective":"2026-01-01","coverageTermination":"2026-12-31","priorAuthOnFile":false,"stepTherapyMet":false}'
174	```
175	
176	A plain `docker compose up` (no profile) still runs **only** the Phase 1 stack — Phase 2 is
177	strictly additive.
178	
179	> **The demo FHIR server is in-memory**, so it boots empty every time, and adjudication **fails
180	> closed** — a member with no clinical record pends rather than approving. Always run the seeder
181	> (it seeds fixtures *and* drives the paths). See the
182	> [demo prep checklist](docs/demo-guide.md#1-before-any-demo).
183	
184	### Tests
185	
186	```bash
187	pytest                                      # all Python suites (config in pytest.ini)
188	mvn -f claims-service/pom.xml test          # Phase 2 façade: unit + contract tests
189	mvn -f rxclaim-emulator/pom.xml test        # simulated legacy core
190	pytest e2e/                                 # golden paths (needs the phase2 stack up; else skips)
191	```

199	## Phase 3 — Provider Search & Referral
200	
201	Phase 3 answers the question Phase 1/2 don't: *"who can this patient actually see?"* Given a
202	patient's location and a clinical need, it returns a ranked, explained list of **real**
203	providers — sourced from authoritative public data (NPPES), not a paid third-party directory
204	API — with full lineage back to the source record. **M1–M7 complete; Phase 3b (live cloud
205	deployment) not started.** Full design, milestone history, and every architectural decision
206	(with status tracking): [`docs/phase3/`](docs/phase3/README.md).
207	
208	It's also this platform's **first genuine Model Context Protocol integration**. Prior "agent
209	tools" (`mcp-agent/src/agent/tools.py`) are in-process Python function dispatch; Phase 3 builds
210	a real, hand-built MCP server and a real MCP client/host, talking the actual protocol
211	(`initialize` → `tools/list` → `tools/call`) — not a simulation of it.
212	
213	Request flow (opt-in `phase3` profile):
214	
215	```
216	provider-search-agent ──(MCP: stdio)──▶ provider-mcp-server ──(HTTP)──▶ provider-registry-service ──▶ Postgres
217	  (NL request, real MCP        (real MCP server —              (taxonomy resolution +
218	   client/host, discovers       genuine protocol                haversine proximity search;
219	   tools live via tools/list)   boundary)                       internal-only, never on Kong edge)
220	
221	provider-curation-agent ──▶ data/scripts/provider_ingest/*.py ──▶ Postgres
222	  (orchestrates + narrates       (real NPPES/NUCC/Census ingestion —
223	   a run; NOT an MCP client)      curated to NC/CA/MT, 12,582 real providers)
224	```
225	
226	Real, not synthetic, on the provider side: 12,582 real providers across three curated states
227	(NC/CA/MT), pulled live from the NPPES NPI Registry and NUCC taxonomy sources, with lineage
228	from every registry record back to its ingestion run. (Patients stay synthetic, as elsewhere in
229	this repo — Phase 3 is about *finding* a provider, not about patient data.)
230	
231	### Run the Phase 3 demo
232	
233	```bash
234	# Bring up Postgres + the registry service (Phase 1/2 services start automatically as
235	# dependencies if you also pass their profiles; phase3 alone is self-contained)
236	docker compose --profile phase3 up --build -d postgres provider-registry
237	
238	# Seed real data (NC only — fast; add CA,MT for the full curated set, ~1-2 min)
239	docker compose --profile phase3 run --rm -T provider-curation-agent --states NC --no-llm
240	
241	# Ask a real question (needs ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or CLAUDE_API_KEY in .env — this agent has
242	# no deterministic fallback, unlike claims-agent: its whole job is NL understanding)
243	docker compose --profile phase3 run --rm provider-search-agent \
244	  --query "find an endocrinologist near 27514"
245	```
246	
247	> **Use `-T` with `docker compose run` for any Phase 3 CLI agent** (`provider-curation-agent`,
248	> `provider-search-agent`) if you're scripting it non-interactively — some environments
249	> silently swallow stdout without it. `docker run -d ... && docker logs <container>` is a
250	> reliable fallback if output still doesn't show up. See [`docs/phase3/README.md`](docs/phase3/README.md).
251	
252	A plain `docker compose up` (no profile) still runs **only** the Phase 1 stack — Phase 3 is
253	strictly additive, same guarantee as Phase 2.
254	
255	### Tests
256	
257	```bash
258	pytest                                      # all Python suites, including Phase 3 (config in pytest.ini)
259	```
260	
261	CI (`.github/workflows/tests.yml`) runs `phase3-python` (the full Phase 3 suite against a
262	**real Postgres service container** — DB-backed tests execute for real in CI, not just
263	locally) and `phase3-terraform` (`terraform validate`, matrix across all four Phase 3
264	Terraform directories — deliberately `validate`, not `plan`, since `plan` needs live GCP
265	credentials this project doesn't provision). The real, billed-API-call groundedness eval
266	self-skips in CI (no key secret configured) — a deliberate cost-conscious choice.

283	cd fhir-agent

288	```bash

299	3. Convert it to JDBC format: `jdbc:postgresql://host/db?user=user&password=‹redacted:url-query-password›&sslmode=require`

304	SPRING_DATASOURCE_URL="jdbc:postgresql://host/db?user=user&password=‹redacted:url-query-password›&sslmode=require" \
305	SPRING_DATASOURCE_DRIVER_CLASS_NAME="org.postgresql.Driver" \

# Agentic Healthcare Workflow Platform

## Quick demo

A clinician types a natural-language query. The agent fetches FHIR data, evaluates medication safety, and returns a structured recommendation — in one turn.

```bash
docker compose up --build -d fhir triage
python3 data/scripts/seed_demo.py
# The mcp-agent image's entrypoint already runs the agent — pass only its args.
# No API key needed: the agent defaults to a self-hosted, free model (see below).
docker compose run --rm mcp-agent --query "Check refill risk for Kristle Mraz"
```

By default the agent runs against a self-hosted Ollama model — no API key, no cost, and PHI
never leaves this host (docs/phase6/decisions.md H45). The docker-compose `mcp-agent`/
`mcp-agent-api` services don't yet have host-Ollama networking wired in (a known, deferred gap —
see `docs/phase6/milestone-plan.md` M5), so for now, to use a real Claude model in the demo
above, set `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in `.env` (`cp .env.example .env`) and add
`--provider anthropic --model claude-sonnet-4-5` to the query above. Running the CLI directly on
the host (not via docker-compose) already works against a locally-running `ollama serve` with no
extra configuration.

Expected output:
```
🚨 HIGH RISK — Do not dispense without physician review
   Patient: Kristle Mraz  |  RiskAssessment/...
   Reason: Penicillin-class allergy conflicts with Amoxicillin prescription.
```

Demo patients loaded by `seed_demo.py`:

| Patient | Scenario | Expected result |
|---|---|---|
| Kristle Mraz | Penicillin allergy + Amoxicillin Rx | HIGH risk |
| John Doe | No allergies + Lisinopril Rx | LOW risk |

---

## Documentation

Everything is indexed in **[`docs/`](docs/README.md)**. Start with what you're doing:

| I want to… | Read |
|---|---|
| **See it work**, or demo it (clinician / insurer / architect / layperson) | [`docs/demo-guide.md`](docs/demo-guide.md) |
| **Understand the code** and change it safely | [`docs/developer-guide.md`](docs/developer-guide.md) |
| **Run the tests**, or write good ones | [`docs/testing-guide.md`](docs/testing-guide.md) |
| **Operate the gateway** (local, cloud, migration) | [`docs/gateway-runbook.md`](docs/gateway-runbook.md) |
| **Know why** Phase 2 is built this way | [`docs/phase2/plan.md`](docs/phase2/plan.md) |
| **Know why** Phase 3 (Provider Search) is built this way | [`docs/phase3/design.md`](docs/phase3/design.md) |
| **Audit Phase 2 decisions** (status + supersession) | [`docs/phase2/decisions.md`](docs/phase2/decisions.md) |
| **Audit Phase 3 decisions** (status + supersession) | [`docs/phase3/decisions.md`](docs/phase3/decisions.md) |
| **Know what was agreed** (normative requirements) | [`docs/phase2/requirements.md`](docs/phase2/requirements.md) |
| **Know what to build next** | [`docs/phase2/plan.md` §16](docs/phase2/plan.md#16-future-work) |

Working agreements (git rules, the two worktrees, how to work here): [`CLAUDE.md`](CLAUDE.md).

---

## Overview

This project builds a platform where clinicians can describe healthcare workflows in natural language, and an **agentic orchestration layer** (powered by LLMs and MCP) generates, deploys, and maintains FHIR-based automations. The goal is to replace traditional SaaS development with AI-driven orchestration, giving healthcare organisations custom tools without needing a full-time software development team.

**First workflow:** *Prescription Refill Risk Triage* — an agent that assesses drug-allergy conflicts, interactions, and fulfilment risks, producing triage recommendations with confidence scores and audit trails.

---

## Architecture

The platform is built as a collection of microservices, designed to be cloud-agnostic and fully compatible with FHIR R4.

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    Agentic Orchestration                        │
│                (MCP Agent — LLM-powered)                       │
│   - Interprets user intents                                     │
│   - Discovers and composes MCP tools                           │
│   - Executes workflows, logs decisions                         │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                              │
                              ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                       MCP Tool Servers                         │
│   - FHIR Tools (Patient, Medication, Allergy)                  │
│   - Safety Tools (drug-allergy, interactions)                  │
│   - Workflow Tools (submit triage, escalate)                   │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                              │
                              ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                        FHIR Servers                            │
│   - Generic FHIR R4 server (development & testing)            │
│   - Future: EHR sandboxes (Epic, Athena) or emulators         │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Microservices

| Service | Purpose | Status |
|---|---|---|
| **fhir-service** | Generic FHIR R4 server (HAPI JPA). Used for local development and as the FHIR data source for the MCP agent. | ✅ Running (H2 local, Neon PostgreSQL cloud) |
| **epic-emulator** | Placeholder — will add Epic-specific customisations (auth stubs, custom profiles, proprietary extensions). | ⏳ Not yet implemented |
| **athena-emulator** | Placeholder — will add Athena-specific customisations. | ⏳ Not yet implemented |
| **triage-service** | FastAPI drug-allergy rule engine → FHIR `RiskAssessment` (HIGH/MODERATE/LOW) with audit trail. | ✅ Running (local + Docker Compose) |
| **mcp-agent** | LLM-powered orchestration layer that composes FHIR + triage tools. Self-hosted Ollama by default (no API key, no cost); Anthropic and other OpenAI-compatible providers available via explicit opt-in (`docs/phase6/decisions.md` H45). | ✅ Running (local + Docker Compose) |
| **rxclaim-emulator** *(Phase 2)* | Simulated legacy IBM i / RxClaim adjudication core: fixed-width DDS-style records, DB2/SQL400-style tables, RPG/CL-style `ADJRXCLM`. Internal-only. | ✅ Running (`--profile phase2`) |
| **claims-service** *(Phase 2)* | Spring Boot claims-adjudication façade: anti-corruption layer + layered rules engine + Decision Contract; persists a FHIR decision graph. | ✅ Running (`--profile phase2`) |
| **claims-agent** *(Phase 2)* | Non-authoritative agent that explains adjudication decisions in plain language. | ✅ Running (`--profile phase2`) |
| **provider-registry-service** *(Phase 3)* | FastAPI façade over the real, curated NPPES/NUCC provider registry: taxonomy resolution + haversine proximity search. Internal-only. | ✅ Running (`--profile phase3`) |
| **provider-mcp-server** *(Phase 3)* | The platform's first real, hand-built MCP server — genuine `initialize`/`tools/list`/`tools/call`, stdio transport. Thin adapter over `provider-registry-service`. | ✅ Running (local child process; no compose service — see [`docs/phase3/README.md`](docs/phase3/README.md)) |
| **provider-curation-agent** *(Phase 3)* | Non-authoritative agent that orchestrates real NPPES/NUCC/ZCTA ingestion and narrates the run. | ✅ Running (`--profile phase3`) |
| **provider-search-agent** *(Phase 3)* | Real MCP client/host: turns a natural-language clinical request into ranked, traceable providers by discovering and calling `provider-mcp-server`'s tools live. | ✅ Running (`--profile phase3`) |

---

## Current Status

**This section covers Phase 1 (the original walking skeleton) specifically.** Phase 2
(claims adjudication) and Phase 3 (provider search) are also complete and run locally —
see their own sections below, or [Status & future work](#status--future-work) for the
full picture across all three.

The end-to-end walking skeleton runs locally and via Docker Compose:
**mcp-agent → triage-service → fhir-service**. A natural-language clinician query
resolves a patient, evaluates drug-allergy risk, and returns a structured
recommendation (see [Quick demo](#quick-demo)).

The FHIR R4 server is built on the **official HAPI FHIR JPA starter (8.8.0)**. It supports:

- All FHIR R4 resource endpoints (`Patient`, `MedicationRequest`, `AllergyIntolerance`, etc.)
- Local development with an in-memory H2 database (`./mvnw spring-boot:run`)
- Cloud deployment with Neon serverless PostgreSQL (environment-variable-based configuration)
- FHIR `CapabilityStatement` at `GET /fhir/metadata`

The server is intentionally generic — it does not emulate any specific EHR. The agent and MCP tooling are built against a standard FHIR R4 endpoint first, ensuring portability. EHR-specific authentication, profiles, and extensions will be added later in the emulator modules.

---

## Phase 2 — Claims Adjudication Modernisation Slice

Phase 2 extends the platform into **prescription claim adjudication**, wrapping a simulated
legacy RxClaim / IBM i core with modern services — an **API façade**, an **anti-corruption
layer**, a deterministic **rules engine**, an auditable **FHIR decision graph**, and a
plain-language **explanation agent**. Design, requirements, and architecture live in
[`docs/phase2/`](docs/phase2/README.md).

Request flow (opt-in `phase2` profile):

```
claims-agent ──▶ claims-service ──┬──▶ rxclaim-emulator   (legacy pricing/SOR, internal only)
 (explains)        (façade + ACL   ├──▶ triage-service     (clinical safety, reused Phase 1)
                    + rules engine) └──▶ fhir-service       (Claim/ClaimResponse/Task/Provenance)
```

The legacy core is **wrapped, not rewritten** (strangler pattern): the modern layer owns the
rules, experience, and audit trail; pricing and the member system-of-record remain "legacy".
Decisions are **deterministic** and **idempotent** — the same claim yields the same decision
and never double-writes its artefacts.

### Run the Phase 2 demo

```bash
# Bring up the full stack (Phase 1 services start automatically as dependencies)
docker compose --profile phase2 up --build -d

# Seed the FHIR fixtures and drive the six golden paths
# (approved / pended / routed / denied / multi-reason / clinical-safety)
python3 data/scripts/seed_claims_demo.py

# Explain a decision in plain language (deterministic without an API key)
docker compose --profile phase2 run --rm claims-agent \
  --no-llm --claim '{"claimId":"C1","memberId":"000000001","planId":"COM-SILVER","rxcui":"1991302","ndc":"63552-200","drugName":"semaglutide","quantity":1,"daysSupply":28,"dateOfService":"2026-06-01","prescriberNpi":"1234567890","coverageEffective":"2026-01-01","coverageTermination":"2026-12-31","priorAuthOnFile":false,"stepTherapyMet":false}'
```

A plain `docker compose up` (no profile) still runs **only** the Phase 1 stack — Phase 2 is
strictly additive.

> **The demo FHIR server is in-memory**, so it boots empty every time, and adjudication **fails
> closed** — a member with no clinical record pends rather than approving. Always run the seeder
> (it seeds fixtures *and* drives the paths). See the
> [demo prep checklist](docs/demo-guide.md#1-before-any-demo).

### Tests

```bash
pytest                                      # all Python suites (config in pytest.ini)
mvn -f claims-service/pom.xml test          # Phase 2 façade: unit + contract tests
mvn -f rxclaim-emulator/pom.xml test        # simulated legacy core
pytest e2e/                                 # golden paths (needs the phase2 stack up; else skips)
```

CI (`.github/workflows/tests.yml`) runs a **Phase-1-only** job (proving independence) plus the
Phase 2 suites. It does **not** run the e2e suite — that gap, and everything else that is and
isn't covered, is documented in the [testing guide](docs/testing-guide.md).

---

## Phase 3 — Provider Search & Referral

Phase 3 answers the question Phase 1/2 don't: *"who can this patient actually see?"* Given a
patient's location and a clinical need, it returns a ranked, explained list of **real**
providers — sourced from authoritative public data (NPPES), not a paid third-party directory
API — with full lineage back to the source record. **M1–M7 complete; Phase 3b (live cloud
deployment) not started.** Full design, milestone history, and every architectural decision
(with status tracking): [`docs/phase3/`](docs/phase3/README.md).

It's also this platform's **first genuine Model Context Protocol integration**. Prior "agent
tools" (`mcp-agent/src/agent/tools.py`) are in-process Python function dispatch; Phase 3 builds
a real, hand-built MCP server and a real MCP client/host, talking the actual protocol
(`initialize` → `tools/list` → `tools/call`) — not a simulation of it.

Request flow (opt-in `phase3` profile):

```
provider-search-agent ──(MCP: stdio)──▶ provider-mcp-server ──(HTTP)──▶ provider-registry-service ──▶ Postgres
  (NL request, real MCP        (real MCP server —              (taxonomy resolution +
   client/host, discovers       genuine protocol                haversine proximity search;
   tools live via tools/list)   boundary)                       internal-only, never on Kong edge)

provider-curation-agent ──▶ data/scripts/provider_ingest/*.py ──▶ Postgres
  (orchestrates + narrates       (real NPPES/NUCC/Census ingestion —
   a run; NOT an MCP client)      curated to NC/CA/MT, 12,582 real providers)
```

Real, not synthetic, on the provider side: 12,582 real providers across three curated states
(NC/CA/MT), pulled live from the NPPES NPI Registry and NUCC taxonomy sources, with lineage
from every registry record back to its ingestion run. (Patients stay synthetic, as elsewhere in
this repo — Phase 3 is about *finding* a provider, not about patient data.)

### Run the Phase 3 demo

```bash
# Bring up Postgres + the registry service (Phase 1/2 services start automatically as
# dependencies if you also pass their profiles; phase3 alone is self-contained)
docker compose --profile phase3 up --build -d postgres provider-registry

# Seed real data (NC only — fast; add CA,MT for the full curated set, ~1-2 min)
docker compose --profile phase3 run --rm -T provider-curation-agent --states NC --no-llm

# Ask a real question (needs ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or CLAUDE_API_KEY in .env — this agent has
# no deterministic fallback, unlike claims-agent: its whole job is NL understanding)
docker compose --profile phase3 run --rm provider-search-agent \
  --query "find an endocrinologist near 27514"
```

> **Use `-T` with `docker compose run` for any Phase 3 CLI agent** (`provider-curation-agent`,
> `provider-search-agent`) if you're scripting it non-interactively — some environments
> silently swallow stdout without it. `docker run -d ... && docker logs <container>` is a
> reliable fallback if output still doesn't show up. See [`docs/phase3/README.md`](docs/phase3/README.md).

A plain `docker compose up` (no profile) still runs **only** the Phase 1 stack — Phase 3 is
strictly additive, same guarantee as Phase 2.

### Tests

```bash
pytest                                      # all Python suites, including Phase 3 (config in pytest.ini)
```

CI (`.github/workflows/tests.yml`) runs `phase3-python` (the full Phase 3 suite against a
**real Postgres service container** — DB-backed tests execute for real in CI, not just
locally) and `phase3-terraform` (`terraform validate`, matrix across all four Phase 3
Terraform directories — deliberately `validate`, not `plan`, since `plan` needs live GCP
credentials this project doesn't provision). The real, billed-API-call groundedness eval
self-skips in CI (no key secret configured) — a deliberate cost-conscious choice.

## Getting Started

### Prerequisites

- **Java 21** (JDK — required; pom.xml targets Java 21)
- **Maven 3.8+** (or use the included Maven wrapper `./mvnw`)
- **Docker** (optional — required for integration tests using Testcontainers)
- **Neon** account (optional — required for cloud PostgreSQL profile)

### Clone the repository

```bash
git clone https://github.com/bhaskarcmu/fhir-agent.git
cd fhir-agent
```

### Run the FHIR server locally (H2)

```bash
cd fhir-service
./mvnw spring-boot:run
```

The server starts on `http://localhost:8080`. Visit `http://localhost:8080/fhir/metadata` to see the FHIR `CapabilityStatement`.

### Run with Neon PostgreSQL (cloud)

1. Create a [Neon](https://neon.tech) account and database.
2. Get your connection string from the Neon dashboard (format: `postgresql://user:‹redacted:url-credentials›host/db?sslmode=require`).
3. Convert it to JDBC format: `jdbc:postgresql://host/db?user=user&password=‹redacted:url-query-password›&sslmode=require`
4. Run:

```bash
cd fhir-service
SPRING_DATASOURCE_URL="jdbc:postgresql://host/db?user=user&password=‹redacted:url-query-password›&sslmode=require" \
SPRING_DATASOURCE_DRIVER_CLASS_NAME="org.postgresql.Driver" \
HIBERNATE_DIALECT="ca.uhn.fhir.jpa.model.dialect.HapiFhirPostgresDialect" \
./mvnw spring-boot:run -Dspring-boot.run.profiles=neon -Dmaven.test.skip=true
```

## Development Environment

The project uses a **devcontainer** to ensure a consistent environment across all contributors. The `.devcontainer/` directory defines:

- `Dockerfile` — Java 21, Python 3, Node.js, Maven, Docker-in-Docker, kubectl, Helm, Terraform
- VS Code extensions — Java, Spring Boot, Python, GitHub Copilot, Continue, Roo Code
- Post-start automation — configures AI tools (Claude Code, Continue, Roo Code) using secrets stored in Ona

**Opening the project:**

- **Local (Docker Desktop):** Open the folder in VS Code and click *Reopen in Container*
- **Cloud (Ona):** The container builds automatically on first launch

### Build and test before committing

```bash
# Python packages (editable installs + test tooling via the [dev] extras)
python -m pip install -e "client/clinical[dev]" -e "agent-platform[dev]" -e "triage-service[dev]" -e "mcp-agent[dev]"
pytest                              # runs all Python suites (config in pytest.ini)
pytest agent-platform/tests -q      # separate invocation -- see pytest.ini's own comment on why

# FHIR service (Java).
# NOTE: unset any SPRING_DATASOURCE_URL / NEON_* env vars first, so the tests use
# the in-memory H2 default. Otherwise MdmTest boots the full app against a live
# database and fails on auth — a config/env issue, not a code failure.
cd fhir-service && ./mvnw clean verify
```

## Project Goals and Success Metrics

| Goal | Metric |
|---|---|
| Interoperability | System can pull FHIR data from any R4-compliant endpoint |
| Risk accuracy | Triage recommendations match a validated clinical ruleset ≥ 95% |
| Guardrail effectiveness | Zero autonomous actions below confidence threshold; all high-risk scenarios escalate |
| Agent adaptation | Agent learns from human overrides |
| Development velocity | Adding a new MCP tool takes < 1 day |

## Status & future work

### Done
- ✅ **Phase 1** — FHIR R4 server (H2 dev / Neon PostgreSQL cloud), triage rule engine, MCP
  agent, end-to-end demo. Tagged `phase1-v1` and independently runnable.
- ✅ **Phase 2 (M0–M7)** — legacy emulator, adjudication façade + ACL + rules engine, Decision
  Contract, FHIR audit graph, explanation agent, compose profiles, DB-less Kong, golden paths.
  Runs end to end locally.
- ✅ **Phase 3 (M1–M7)** — real NPPES/NUCC provider registry (12,582 real providers, 3 states),
  a hand-built MCP server + real MCP client/host agent (this platform's first genuine MCP
  integration), a curation agent, a root Terraform module, `deploy-phase3.sh`, and CI wired to
  actually run the Phase 3 suite against a real Postgres service container. Runs end to end
  locally, including through the real Docker images. Design/decisions:
  [`docs/phase3/`](docs/phase3/README.md).

### Next
Phase 2's prioritised backlog lives in
**[`docs/phase2/plan.md` §16](docs/phase2/plan.md#16-future-work)**. The headlines: run e2e in
CI (the top gap), non-regression decision snapshots, a circuit breaker on the triage call, the
Postgres swap behind the C3 seam, and **M8 / Phase 2b** — the cloud deploy, which needs its
root Terraform module **written** before it can be applied
([cloud-delivery gap](docs/phase2/plan.md#6-workstreams--milestones)).

For Phase 3: **Phase 3b** — live GCP deployment (`terraform apply` + `deploy-phase3.sh`
against a real project; nothing has been deployed yet, only `terraform validate`). Also
tracked but not built: an `accepting_new_patients` data source (NPPES has none — every
provider reports `unknown`, honestly, rather than guessing), and a taxonomy-matcher quality
pass (found real: `resolve_specialty("endocrinologist")` returns `ambiguous` against the full
NUCC code set — see [`docs/phase3/design.md` §14](docs/phase3/design.md#14-risks)).

Longer-standing: EHR emulators (`epic-emulator/`, `athena-emulator/` are placeholders),
drug-drug interaction rules, and load testing.

### Known issues
- Versioned profile URL fallback (`VersionedUrlFallbackValidationSupport`) is a workaround for a
  gap in HAPI FHIR core; removable once HAPI resolves versioned canonical URLs natively in
  `DefaultProfileValidationSupport`.
- Binary storage defaults to database; filesystem mode needs explicit
  `hapi.fhir.binary_storage_mode` + `hapi.fhir.binary_storage_filesystem_base_directory`.
- MDM (patient matching) is disabled by default; enable with `hapi.fhir.mdm_enabled=true`.
- Compose pins HAPI `v7.2.0` while docs reference `8.8.0` — drift to reconcile.

## The guides

**[Demo guide](./demo-guide.md)** — how to experience the system, and how to demo it to four
audiences (clinician, insurer, architect/developer, layperson). Includes the prep checklist that
stops a demo failing in front of people: the FHIR server is in-memory and adjudication fails
closed, so you must seed first.

**[Developer guide](./developer-guide.md)** — the mental model, the lifecycle of one claim
through the packages, the invariants you must not break, the local dev loop, a list of traps that
have already cost real hours, and how to add a rule / a downstream call / a FHIR artefact.

**[Testing guide](./testing-guide.md)** — what is tested (with counts), what is *not* (with
honesty), how to run every level, and how to write unit / white-box / component / interface /
e2e tests here. Its case study — how a dead clinical-safety check passed every test for several
milestones — is the most useful thing in this folder.

**[Gateway runbook](./gateway-runbook.md)** — the single operational source of truth for the Kong
edge across **both** phases: why two gateways exist, which one owns which route in each strangler
state (S0/S1/S2), exact local procedures (including the template→generated config flow), the
cloud position, the migration and its rollback, and troubleshooting.

## Conventions for this folder

- **`requirements.md` is normative and stable.** It says *what must be true*. It does not carry
  status, milestones, branches, commits, or PR numbers — those live in git history and the plan.
- **`plan.md` / `design.md` says how and in what order**, including what's next.
- **The guides are practical.** They tell you what to type and what will bite you.
- **Service-level READMEs** (`claims-service/`, `triage-service/`, `provider-registry-service/`,

  "Phase 3.x". "Phase" is reserved for top-level phases — Phase 1, Phase 2, Phase 3, and
  **Phase 3b** (the future live-deployment phase, mirroring Phase 2b).

# Phase 6 — Agent Platform Hardening + Overall Observability — Milestone Plan

> Sequencing, deliverables, and status for the requirements in [`prd.md`](./prd.md) and the
> architecture in [`design.md`](./design.md). **This is a separate document from `design.md`**,
> a deliberate departure from Phase 3/4's consolidation convention — see
> [`decisions.md` H23](./decisions.md) for why.
>
> **Status is stated once, canonically, in [`README.md`](./README.md).** The Status column
> below is the per-milestone record.

## Order and dependency

Order is by dependency, **not** by the topic numbering in [`design.md` §2](./design.md#2-the-five-topics):

| # | Status | Milestone | Topic(s) | Depends on |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **M1** | 🔜 Next up | Output Contract & Fail-Closed Enforcement | 5 | — |
| **M2** | ⏳ Not started | Observability, Platform-Wide | 2, 3 | M1 |
| **M3** | ⏳ Not started | Context, Memory & Session Transport | 1, 4 | M2 |
| **M4** | ⏳ Not started | Deploy Resilience & Cost Control | 2 | M2, M3 |
| **M5** | ⏳ Not started | Provider Abstraction & Cross-Model Follow-ups | 4 | M1, M3 |
| **M6** | ⏳ Not started | Policy, Knowledge & Judge | 5 | M1, M5 |
| **M7** | 📋 Planned, not started | Strong Model in Production | 4 | M5 |

**Minimal-viable-cut re-examination is deliberately deferred to the end of M2**, not decided now
([`decisions.md` H23](./decisions.md)). M2's scope grew substantially once it took on closing
Phase 2's R15 platform-wide (H16) — whether "M1+M2" is still a sensible minimal cut, or whether
M2 itself needs splitting, gets decided once M2's real size is known, not guessed here.

---

## M1 — Output Contract & Fail-Closed Enforcement

**Short story:** Every agent turn ends in one of a small set of enum outcomes, code-validated,
with `REVIEW` as the fail-closed catch-all — and a data-layer guard makes sure a broken or
unclear triage response can never quietly look like "safe" in the first place.

**Long story:** Two paired deliverables (see [`design.md` §4.1](./design.md#41-output-safety--m1)
for the full design):

62:## M2 — Observability, Platform-Wide

| **H56
80:| **H55** | Knowledge-base citation fetch triggers on a **code-observable signal** (`assess_refill_risk`'s new `flagged_medications` field being non-empty) — never by `agent.py` re-deriving "is this HIGH risk," which would be re-implementing clinical logic the agent isn't supposed to hold. Best-effort throughout: any lookup failure already returns `None`/`[]` from `knowledge.py`, so a citation-fetch failure can never affect the decision it would have supplemented | ✅ Accepted | Keeps "no clinical logic in the agent" intact (design.md §3) -- `agent.py` reacts to what a tool result already contains, it doesn't independently judge risk severity. Rationale: `tools.py`'s `assess_refill_risk`, `agent.py`'s `_fetch_citations`. |
81:| **H56** | openFDA Drug Label lookups are **by generic drug name**, extracted from the medication's FHIR display text — not by RxNorm code, unlike RxClass (which uses the RxNorm code directly) | ✅ Accepted | Verified live during design: this repo's FHIR data carries ingredient-level RxNorm codes (e.g. RXCUI 723 for plain amoxicillin), but openFDA's own `openfda.rxcui` field only lists product-level (specific labeled product) RXCUIs -- a real rxcui-based lookup for 723 404s. RxClass, being NLM's own system, works directly with the same ingredient-level RXCUI already on hand. Rationale: `knowledge.py` module docstring, live-verified 2026-08-02 (see `milestone-plan.md` M6). |

>   research rounds: rules, steps, the target scorecard, the holdout ledger, promotion, and how
>   to resume after a long gap. Outlives the phase.
> - [`prototype-baseline.md`](./prototype-baseline.md) — what the research prototype
>   established: data-source choices, MEPS and Synthea facts, the prototype's method, the exact
>   numbers M1, M2 and M4 must reproduce, and reference URLs.

## What Phase 8 is

The platform's first **machine-learned** clinical capability. Given an adult patient in
`fhir-service` and an as-of date, estimate the probability of at least one inpatient stay in
the next 12 months, and return it as a FHIR `RiskAssessment` — with a simple, hand-checkable
comparison score beside it, a population percentile, the top contributing features, and
references to the FHIR resources the estimate was derived from.

The model is trained only on free, open, US data — AHRQ's Medical Expenditure Panel Survey
(MEPS) longitudinal panels 21–27 — so every reported number can be reproduced from public
files. Synthea is used to test the pipeline, never to judge accuracy.

It deliberately does **not** produce qualitative risk bands, recommend treatment, read free
text, persist scores into the patient record, or deploy to the cloud this phase — see
`prd.md` §4 and §8.

## Where the model lives, and what the agent can't do

All model, feature and FHIR-mapping logic lives in one new service,
`outcome-prediction-service/` (O2). A new agent, `outcome-prediction-agent/`, built on
`agent-platform`, lets a clinician ask for a patient's risk in plain language — but its tools
can only look a patient up, fetch their `RiskAssessment`, and read the model card. **No tool
accepts feature values, thresholds or a model choice**, so the agent cannot re-score, adjust,
or band a result (`design.md` §9).

## Research that outlives the phase

Which outcomes are worth predicting — and as a probability, a count, a cost or a tier — is a
question this phase starts answering, not one it closes. `outcome-prediction-lab/` (built in
M3) is the permanent workbench: config-driven runs tracked in a local MLflow store, committed
round reports, a target scorecard that weighs measurability in customer data and actionability
alongside model metrics, and model cards. Two rules keep it honest: the test panels are opened
only for logged confirmation (O32), and nothing reaches the service without a promotion record
tied to a decision (O33). Later explorations are new **rounds** under
`experimentation-protocol.md`, never reopened milestones (O28).

## Data that outlives its source

The MEPS files are public and re-downloadable, but a source can go down, move, or quietly
republish different bytes. So the data is **pinned in git** — the committed
`outcome-prediction-service/meps-manifest.json` records the SHA-256 of every original file,
documentation page and codebook — and **preserved outside it**, in write-once,
content-addressed private mirrors. Downloads accept only bytes that match the manifest, and
fall back to a mirror when AHRQ can't supply them (O41, O42; `design.md` §13). Today the
preserved copy is the repo owner's off-workspace `file://` mirror; the retention-protected GCS
bucket (`outcome-prediction-service/infra/`) is ready but deferred, with a local GCS emulator
standing in for testing (O43).

## Relationship to Phase 1, 6, and 7

Additive. `fhir-service`, `triage-service`, `mcp-agent` and the Kong gateway are unmodified;
the new service is internal-only (O14) and runs under its own `phase8` compose profile.
`client/clinical` is extended additively (M5), coordinated with Phase 7 M3, which widens the
same client (O9). `outcome-prediction-agent` reuses Phase 6's session, observability,
provider seam and output-gate pattern, with the self-hosted model as default (O15, O16).
The `RiskAssessment` follows `triage-service`'s resource type but adds a numeric probability,
using Phase 8's own models (O3).

## Terminology

Internal work is tracked as **milestones** (M1–M13, in `milestone-plan.md`) — never
"Phase 8.x", same convention as every prior phase. The prototype's own planned stages are mapped onto
these milestones in `milestone-plan.md` (O4); its stage numbering is not used anywhere.

# Phase 8 Design — Patient Outcome Prediction

Architecture, component breakdown, and the technical sketches `milestone-plan.md` builds
against. Status and requirements live in [`README.md`](./README.md) and [`prd.md`](./prd.md).
The research prototype's method, data facts and reproduction numbers are in
[`prototype-baseline.md`](./prototype-baseline.md); where the two disagree, this document
wins.

## 1. Repo layout

```
outcome-prediction-service/       # NEW (O2) — training pipeline, ETL, scoring API; no conversational logic
  pyproject.toml                  # requires-python >=3.11; scikit-learn pinned exactly (O12)
  README.md                       # service-level detail, per docs/README.md conventions
  src/outcome_prediction/
    meps/
      download.py                 # FR-D1: fetch h{n}dta.zip, extract with zipfile, record SHA-256
      build.py                    # FR-D2: modelling table + label(s)
      dictionary.py               # FR-D3: variable dictionary (not inspect.py: would shadow stdlib `inspect`)
    model/
      __init__.py                 # contract features/order, split, hyperparameters — one definition
      fit.py                      # fit_validation (21–25) / fit_release (all panels); importable by the lab
      train.py                    # FR-M1–M4: evaluate, refit, write artifact + reports
      evaluate.py                 # FR-E1–E6: metrics.json + model_report.md
      artifact.py                 # write/verify artifact dir + SHA-256 manifest (O17); percentiles
    contract.py                   # feature contracts (meps25-v1, later v2), Pydantic, feature order
    etl/
      canonical.py                # the five canonical tables (§7)
      extract/synthea_csv.py      # reproduction/parity harness (O8)
      extract/fhir.py             # NEW vs. the prototype: canonical tables from client/clinical (M6)
      transform/to_contract.py    # canonical → contract rows; training vs scoring mode (§6)
      codelists/                  # M13: versioned ICD-10-CM prefix lists per flag + the SNOMED map (O73)
    fhir/
      risk_assessment.py          # Phase 8's own RiskAssessment/Bundle models + builder (O3, §4)
    api.py                        # FastAPI app (§5)
    tools.py                      # the tool surface outcome-prediction-agent may call (§9)
    tests/                        # repo convention (src/<pkg>/tests); synthetic Stata fixtures built in conftest
      fixtures/                   # tiny committed Synthea sample + synthetic contract rows (no MEPS)
  models/                         # gitignored — built artifacts
  data/                           # gitignored — MEPS cache, Synthea CSV/FHIR outputs

outcome-prediction-lab/           # NEW (O28, O29) — experimentation workbench; research-only deps
  pyproject.toml                  # depends on outcome-prediction-service; MLflow pinned (O30)
  src/outcome_prediction_lab/
    cli.py                        # run / compare / confirm / card / promote (§12)
    targets.py                    # label definitions: outcome × form (O34)
    search.py                     # panel-grouped CV + hyperparameter search on training panels only
    holdout.py                    # ledger check — refuses unlogged test-panel evaluation (O32)
    scorecard.py                  # target scorecard template + ML-criteria fill (O36)
    modelcard.py                  # model card from tracked metadata (O39)
    promote.py                    # writes the promotion record the service requires (O33)
  rounds/NNN-<slug>/              # COMMITTED: README (pre-registration), configs/, report.md, metrics.json, scorecards
  holdout-ledger.md               # COMMITTED, append-only
  notebooks/                      # optional; committed with outputs stripped (O38)
  mlruns/                         # gitignored — local MLflow store (O30)

outcome-prediction-agent/         # NEW (O15) — conversational layer, own top-level package
  src/outcome_prediction_agent/
    agent.py                      # tool-use loop on agent-platform (Phase 6)
    explain.py                    # grounded narration of a RiskAssessment (FR-A2, FR-A3)

client/clinical/                  # extended additively (O9, FR-F1)
e2e/test_outcome_prediction_acceptance.py   # M9
```

Not created: a separate `hosp-risk/` repo, a Makefile, a second devcontainer, a second CI
workflow, `LICENSES.md` (`prd.md` §11 V2, V7). `mcp-agent/`, `triage-service/` and
`gateway/` are untouched.

**Dependency direction.** `outcome-prediction-agent` → `outcome-prediction-service` (HTTP, via
`tools.py`'s contract) and → `agent-platform`. It does **not** import `client/clinical`,
`triage-service`, or any model code. `outcome-prediction-service` → `client/clinical` → the
FHIR server. `outcome-prediction-lab` → `outcome-prediction-service` (imports its `meps`,
`model` and `contract` modules — one implementation, not a fork); the service never imports
the lab (O29). Nothing in earlier phases depends on anything in Phase 8.
...
sex, racethx, regiony1, agey1x, inscovy1, povcaty1, ipdisy1, ipngtdy1, ertoty1, obtotvy1,
optotvy1, hhtotdy1, rxtoty1, totexpy1, hibpdx, chddx, angidx, midx, ohrtdx, strkdx, emphdx,
diabdx, arthdx, asthdx, choldx
```

Two interpretation changes, both from review (§11):

- In scoring mode, every `*y1` feature means **the 12 months ending at `as_of`** (O10). The
  names keep MEPS' `y1` suffix because the model was trained on them; the window is documented
  in `contract.py`, not encoded in the name.
- `regiony1 = 0` for an unknown or non-US state, as the contract always said; the prototype's
  default to South (3) is not carried over.

`meps25-v2` (M10) pairs the contract with `label_unplanned_12m`; feature changes from O25/FR-D5
arrive as a new contract version, never as an edit to an existing one. The service serves one
contract version per loaded artifact and rejects requests that name another.

# Phase 8 Design — Patient Outcome Prediction

Architecture, component breakdown, and the technical sketches `milestone-plan.md` builds
against. Status and requirements live in [`README.md`](./README.md) and [`prd.md`](./prd.md).
The research prototype's method, data facts and reproduction numbers are in
[`prototype-baseline.md`](./prototype-baseline.md); where the two disagree, this document
wins.

## 1. Repo layout

```
outcome-prediction-service/       # NEW (O2) — training pipeline, ETL, scoring API; no conversational logic
  pyproject.toml                  # requires-python >=3.11; scikit-learn pinned exactly (O12)
  README.md                       # service-level detail, per docs/README.md conventions
  src/outcome_prediction/
    meps/
      download.py                 # FR-D1: fetch h{n}dta.zip, extract with zipfile, record SHA-256
      build.py                    # FR-D2: modelling table + label(s)
      dictionary.py               # FR-D3: variable dictionary (not inspect.py: would shadow stdlib `inspect`)
    model/
      __init__.py                 # contract features/order, split, hyperparameters — one definition
      fit.py                      # fit_validation (21–25) / fit_release (all panels); importable by the lab
      train.py                    # FR-M1–M4: evaluate, refit, write artifact + reports
      evaluate.py                 # FR-E1–E6: metrics.json + model_report.md
      artifact.py                 # write/verify artifact dir + SHA-256 manifest (O17); percentiles
    contract.py                   # feature contracts (meps25-v1, later v2), Pydantic, feature order
    etl/
      canonical.py                # the five canonical tables (§7)
      extract/synthea_csv.py      # reproduction/parity harness (O8)
      extract/fhir.py             # NEW vs. the prototype: canonical tables from client/clinical (M6)
      transform/to_contract.py    # canonical → contract rows; training vs scoring mode (§6)
      codelists/                  # M13: versioned ICD-10-CM prefix lists per flag + the SNOMED map (O73)
    fhir/
      risk_assessment.py          # Phase 8's own RiskAssessment/Bundle models + builder (O3, §4)
    api.py                        # FastAPI app (§5)
    tools.py                      # the tool surface outcome-prediction-agent may call (§9)
    tests/                        # repo convention (src/<pkg>/tests); synthetic Stata fixtures built in conftest
      fixtures/                   # tiny committed Synthea sample + synthetic contract rows (no MEPS)
  models/                         # gitignored — built artifacts
  data/                           # gitignored — MEPS cache, Synthea CSV/FHIR outputs

outcome-prediction-lab/           # NEW (O28, O29) — experimentation workbench; research-only deps
  pyproject.toml                  # depends on outcome-prediction-service; MLflow pinned (O30)
  src/outcome_prediction_lab/
    cli.py                        # run / compare / confirm / card / promote (§12)
    targets.py                    # label definitions: outcome × form (O34)
    search.py                     # panel-grouped CV + hyperparameter search on training panels only
    holdout.py                    # ledger check — refuses unlogged test-panel evaluation (O32)
    scorecard.py                  # target scorecard template + ML-criteria fill (O36)
    modelcard.py                  # model card from tracked metadata (O39)
    promote.py                    # writes the promotion record the service requires (O33)
  rounds/NNN-<slug>/              # COMMITTED: README (pre-registration), configs/, report.md, metrics.json, scorecards
  holdout-ledger.md               # COMMITTED, append-only
  notebooks/                      # optional; committed with outputs stripped (O38)
  mlruns/                         # gitignored — local MLflow store (O30)

outcome-prediction-agent/         # NEW (O15) — conversational layer, own top-level package
  src/outcome_prediction_agent/
    agent.py                      # tool-use loop on agent-platform (Phase 6)
    explain.py                    # grounded narration of a RiskAssessment (FR-A2, FR-A3)

client/clinical/                  # extended additively (O9, FR-F1)
e2e/test_outcome_prediction_acceptance.py   # M9
```

Not created: a separate `hosp-risk/` repo, a Makefile, a second devcontainer, a second CI
workflow, `LICENSES.md` (`prd.md` §11 V2, V7). `mcp-agent/`, `triage-service/` and
`gateway/` are untouched.

**Dependency direction.** `outcome-prediction-agent` → `outcome-prediction-service` (HTTP, via
`tools.py`'s contract) and → `agent-platform`. It does **not** import `client/clinical`,
`triage-service`, or any model code. `outcome-prediction-service` → `client/clinical` → the
FHIR server. `outcome-prediction-lab` → `outcome-prediction-service` (imports its `meps`,
`model` and `contract` modules — one implementation, not a fork); the service never imports
the lab (O29). Nothing in earlier phases depends on anything in Phase 8.
...
sex, racethx, regiony1, agey1x, inscovy1, povcaty1, ipdisy1, ipngtdy1, ertoty1, obtotvy1,
optotvy1, hhtotdy1, rxtoty1, totexpy1, hibpdx, chddx, angidx, midx, ohrtdx, strkdx, emphdx,
diabdx, arthdx, asthdx, choldx
```

Two interpretation changes, both from review (§11):

- In scoring mode, every `*y1` feature means **the 12 months ending at `as_of`** (O10). The
  names keep MEPS' `y1` suffix because the model was trained on them; the window is documented
  in `contract.py`, not encoded in the name.
- `regiony1 = 0` for an unknown or non-US state, as the contract always said; the prototype's
  default to South (3) is not carried over.

`meps25-v2` (M10) pairs the contract with `label_unplanned_12m`; feature changes from O25/FR-D5
arrive as a new contract version, never as an edit to an existing one. The service serves one
contract version per loaded artifact and rejects requests that name another.

## 4. The `RiskAssessment` (O3)

| Summary review | Clinical and business value of each target | Non-obstetric admission = clinical anchor; any ER visit = strongest lift over a simple rule; high cost = finance view; death and insurance loss = learning only (O48) | conversation summary, reflected here |
| Round 002 | Text representations, self-explanatory narratives, the lab CLI | Text adds little on a pregnancy-free label; character n-grams map messy drug names well; every patient can get a plain-language explanation | [round 002 report](../../outcome-prediction-lab/rounds/002-text-and-explanations/report.md) |
| Idea considered | **"Find similar patients"** with autoencoder embeddings | Critiqued (similarity must be intervention-specific; autoencoders unlikely to beat simpler methods here; no ground truth in MEPS; privacy and anchoring risks) — **then dropped by the repo owner** | §5 below |
| ETL review | What survives conversion from customer FHIR | Last-year spending isn't portable; high cost can be predicted without it (CV 0.860 → 0.852) | O25 → O52–O53 |
| Round 003 | The portable contract `meps-portable-v2` | Production models lose nothing for admissions and ER visits, a little for high cost; high cost needs claims to be validated | [round 003 report](../../outcome-prediction-lab/rounds/003-portable-contract/report.md), O52–O54 |
| **2026-10-18** | **Repo owner narrows the focus to the four in §1** | — | **O55** |
| Round 000 | M2's model reproduced through the lab, bit for bit | The lab and the service agree exactly | [round 000 report](../../outcome-prediction-lab/rounds/000-baseline-reproduction/report.md) |
| Round 004 | Readiness of the four: ER-admission production model, fairness, 65+ | All four have production models; fairness findings recorded (uninsured rarely flagged — labels measure use, not need); general models beat 65+ specialists | [round 004 report](../../outcome-prediction-lab/rounds/004-focus-four-readiness/report.md), O56–O58 |
| **2026-10-18** | **First promotion chosen; M3 closed** | Non-obstetric hospital stay goes first (M12) | **O59, O60** |

## 3. What changes now

- **Default scope:** every new round, model card, scorecard, narrative and milestone deliverable
  targets these four unless the repo owner says otherwise.
- **Gap closed (round 004):** admission through the ER now has its production-contract model
  (`er-admit-v2`, O56). Every focus model's card carries a subgroup fairness report (O57) and 65+
  performance; no separate 65+ model (O58).
- **O40 decided (O59):** the first promotion is **non-obstetric hospital stay** (`nonobstetric-v2`);
  the other three follow as later promotions.
- **Service work (M6, M7, M12)** builds the four labels' inputs on `meps-portable-v2`; any-stay
  (`meps25-v1`) stays only as the reproduced reference model from M2.

## 4. Parked work — kept, not deleted

| Item | Status | Where it lives | Pick it up by |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Any hospital stay** (the prototype's target) | Reference only — reproduced exactly; distorted by childbirth | M2 artifact; `meps25-v1`; round 001 §3 | Re-running `outcome_prediction.model.train` |
